title: Name the codimension-two surjectivity condition: the 3-cell hypothesis
description:
hsound for general K is FALSE from SeparatesMerges alone (see Cubical-vcp). pact k = 'flip the square at position k, if K has one', built from mergeLift. Commutation (|i-j| >= 2) is free: the windows are disjoint and non-adjacent, so the square at j is literally the same square before and after, and this follows from SeparatesMerges alone. The BRAID case (j = i+1) is not: the two routes traverse SIX DIFFERENT squares — route A the three faces s_i s_j s_i crosses, route B the three s_j s_i s_j crosses — and SeparatesMerges is INJECTIVITY ONLY, giving no reason for route B's squares to exist when route A's do.

So hsound's braid case is a codimension-two EXISTENCE condition on K: a 3-cell condition.

TASK: name that hypothesis. It sits strictly between SeparatesMerges and IsSegal and is not defined anywhere in the tree. Give it a definition, the basic API, and the instance for the bare cube (box n has all its cells, so it holds there). Then hsound becomes provable under it and Cubical-vcp is completable.

WHY THIS MAY BE THE RIGHT HYPOTHESIS FOR THE WHOLE PROGRAMME, not just for vcp: atomLoop_comm and atomLoop_braid are proved in Ch Zbp, where exists_pairCell ALWAYS supplies the codimension-two cell; transporting them to K needs a chart of that cell, which is surjectivity. And it is Cubical-r1x's corollary read backwards — 'every 3-cell of K induces an Artin braid relation' and 'Ch(K)[W^-1] depends only on the 3-skeleton'. The relations come FROM 3-cells; a K without them has no reason to satisfy them.

NOTE the Garside spelling is WORSE, not better: germPresentation's generators are all of Perm (Fin N), so its pact would need a codimension-l(beta) cell of K for every simple beta.
notes:
SUPERSEDED IN THE RIGHT DIRECTION by Cubical-yl5s. HasDiamonds as first defined asserted all three species of codimension-two join; it is now the ADJACENT species alone, which is the genuine 3-cell condition and nothing else.

FAR is a theorem for every K (hasDiamonds_disjoint), by wedge2Map_isPushout.
SAME JUNCTION is EMPTY unconditionally (eq_of_join_of_dims_eq) — and note SeparatesMerges would NOT have settled it, since the merge-versus-atom pair at one junction is not a merge and separation never reaches it.
ADJACENT is the hypothesis.

So the codimension-two story is hypothesis-free except for the 3-cell, which is a stronger outcome than this bead's original plan.

title: Presents.coproductDecompose: a presentation of a coproduct decomposes
description:
The converse of Presents.coproduct (Machinery/Presentation/Coproduct.lean), and what makes Phase C parametric in an ARBITRARY presentation rather than only in zLocPresentation.

Claim: if C is a coproduct (Sigma i, C i) and P presents C, then P decomposes uniquely as a coproduct of polygraphs P i, with P i presenting C i. The reason it is forced: a 0-cell of P names an object of C, which lies in exactly one component; a 1-cell names an arrow, and there are no arrows across components, so no 1-cell can cross either; likewise no relation can relate words in different components.

Why it matters: Phase Z built zLocPresentation as Polygraph.coproduct of the germ polygraphs, so ITS decomposition is definitional. But the machinery must work for any presentation of Ch(Z)[W-inv], including the Artin one and ones not yet written. This lemma is what turns 'the nth component' from a feature of one construction into an operation on arbitrary presentations.

Home: Machinery/Presentation/Coproduct.lean, beside Presents.coproduct.

Likely shape: given the hom-emptiness across components, build the component polygraphs by restricting V, Gen and rel to a fibre, then show the coproduct of those is isomorphic to P as a polygraph, or at minimum that each restriction presents the corresponding component. The second is what consumers need.

title: Identify Ch(box n)[W-inv] as a category
description:
Direction-independent prerequisite for C1: whatever presentation we eventually build, we should first know WHAT the localized cube-slice is. This does not depend on the open C1 direction question.

Wanted: an equivalence identifying (W (box n)).Localization with an explicitly described category. Expected answer: the weak (right) Bruhat order on Perm (Fin n), read as a thin category, opposite. Objects the n! runs, a unique arrow sigma to tau exactly when tau is below sigma in weak order.

Evidence it is posetal rather than braided: Ch (box n) is thin (chCube_isThin, Concurrency/Grading/ChartHom.lean:38), and the localization adds no loops - see not_nonempty_equiv_posBraidAction in Concurrency/Merge/CubeCrossing.lean, which proves the localization is disconnected while PosBraidAction n is connected.

The tools are warm and were built for that refutation, in CubeCrossing.lean: cross (the crossing permutation of a chain's unique refinement of the one-bead chain), crossLen (its Coxeter length), crossLen_eq_add (length-additivity along a morphism), crossFunctor, crossLoc, and isEmpty_loc_hom_of_crossLen_lt. crossLen_eq_add is precisely the statement that a morphism drops the Coxeter length by the length of its own crossing permutation, which is the weak order.

Also relevant: exists_W_from_ones (Concurrency/Grading/TopBead.lean:76) puts every object W-isomorphic to a run; onesTopEquiv n (:98) says the runs are Perm (Fin n); eq_of_W (:26) and endo_eq_id keep distinct runs distinct.

title: The Artin presentation of Ch(Z)[W-1], and Ch(K)[W-1] on the 3-skeleton
description:
THE headline result for the paper. The cut presentation (zCutPresentation) is morally the GARSIDE one: 1-cells every codimension-one refinement between arbitrary shapes, 2-cells every codimension-two. Wanted: the ARTIN one, whose cells are counted by the 2- and 3-skeleton.

Downstairs, in Ch(Z)[W^-1]:
- 1-cells: the atoms, the codimension-one non-merges out of a run, 1^n -> [1,...,2,...,1]. Only the 2-skeleton is visible.
- 2-cells: the codimension-two cells out of a run, of which there are exactly two species (artin_of_codim_two): [1,...,2,...,2,...,1] gives commutation, [1,...,3,...,1] gives the braid relation. Only the 2- and 3-skeleton is visible.

Pull that back along Ch(K) -> Ch(Z) (Presentation.elements, unconditional) and read the cells as cells of K:
- every reachable 2-cell of K induces a generator
- every pair of 2-cells not sharing an edge induces a commuting Artin relation
- every 3-cell of K induces an Artin braid relation

COROLLARY, and the sanity check on the whole design: **Ch(K)[W^-1] depends only on the 3-skeleton of K.** If that is not immediate from the statement, the statement is wrong.

Inputs already in the tree: Cut.exists_eq_atom (a codim-1 non-merge out of a run is an atom), artin_of_codim_two (the codim-2 dichotomy, an iff), atomLoop_comm, atomLoop_braid, exists_atomWord_conj, factorisationEquiv. Missing: the presentation object itself, and the translation of its cells into cells of K.

count; only Hbp K with representable symmetrization is covered. This bead's 'pull back along

title: Completeness at height > 1 needs a normal form, not just the diamond
description:
PresentationProofStructure.md item 8 asks 'do we need anything else for completeness?'. Assessment: yes.

The diamond closes completeness at HEIGHT 1 only. Two atom-words with the same composite refinement out of 1^n are related by the codim-2 relations -- that is Cut.quot_eq_of_ev_eq (Presentation/CutPresentation.lean), already proved from exists_diamond by induction on codim, with no permutations.

It does NOT close height > 1. conj_comp is multiplicative only on COMPOSABLE pairs, so the image of conj is not a submonoid, and a product of non-composable (conj f) followed by (conj g) need not be conj of anything. Height > 1 is genuinely attained -- the deleted locOf_ne_atomLoc_sq was the witness (sigma_i squared is not the class of any single arrow); see Cubical-0we for its rebuild.

title: A category presentation of ((Winf Zbp).op).Localization
description:
chLocPresentation (Chains/LiftPresentation) takes a presentation of the LOCALIZED base as a hypothesis: a quiver V, a HomRel r on Paths V, and an equivalence Quotient r = ((Winf Zbp).op).Localization. No such presentation exists in the tree; the unlocalized one (zPresentationOp, Chains/CutPresentation) does not supply it.

Wanted: a term of that type with V and r explicit, and chLocPresentation applied to it, so that the transport to Ch K[Winf^-1] is unconditional.

## Context

Two routes, each needing one general theorem the tree lacks.

(a) Add formal inverses to a quiver presentation: for D presented by Quotient r on Paths V and W generated by a subset S of the edges, W.Localization = Quotient r' on Paths V' where V' has an extra edge inverting each e in S and r' adds the two inverse laws.  Mathlib presents W.Localization only via LocQuiver W, whose edges are ALL morphisms of D (Localization.Construction).  With this, cutDataOp's generators plus inverted merges present the localization directly.

(b) One strand count at a time: locFullOpEquiv (Salvetti/HPosAction) already gives ((Winf Zbp).op).Localization = FullPosBraid^op, and localizationEquivGarside gives the Garside monoids.  Missing: SingleObj (PresentedMonoid rel) = Quotient (paths of a one-vertex quiver); a coproduct comparison (Sigma_n Quotient r_n) = Quotient (Sigma quiver); and (Graded M)^op = Graded (fun n => (M n)^mop).

## Landmine

In this tree Quiver.{v} means Hom : Type v.  ElementsPresentation and chPresentation were written with Quiver.{v+1}, which puts the homs one universe up and makes them uninstantiable by any quiver built from a Category.{v}; they now read Quiver.{v}.

title: C(K) presented in bounded codimension, filtered by degree, Artin at the bottom
description:
C(K) is the localization of ECh*(K) at W: the arrows that fix the attached
refinement. Wanted: a presentation of it whose generators and relations are
bounded in codimension, filtered by degree, whose bottom stratum is the
localization of Ch*(K), and which for the standard cube is the Artin
presentation of the braid groupoid.

NOTATION. For z an object of ECh*(K) -- that is, an arrow attachHom z :
attach z --> z.base of Ch K -- the two numbers are ChainCat.degree (attach z)
and ChainCat.codim (attachHom z), and ChainCat.degree z.base is their sum.
For F : z --> z' the codimension is ChainCat.codim F.1.unop = the drop in
ChainCat.degree of the base. There is one codim and one degree; ECh.codim is
not a second notion.

GENERATORS AND RELATIONS.
  Gen K = { F : z --> z' | codim F.1.unop = 1, not W K F,
                           codim (attachHom z) <= 1 }
  Rel K = { z | codim (attachHom z) <= 2 }, each contributing the equality of
          the two taut paths at z.
A taut path at z is a path in Gen K from attach z to attach (compl z), every
step of which is a generator y --> y' with y.base --> z.base. compl z is the
object with the same base whose subdivision is reversed inside each bead of
that base.

  T-COMPL   compl is an involution; it fixes the base, the degree and the
            codimension.
  T-TAUT    for codim (attachHom z) = 2 there are exactly two taut paths at z,
            of common length 2 or 3 according to the two species of
            codim_two_species -- two disjoint two-bead windows, or one
            three-bead window.
  T-PRES    the functor ECh*(K) --> Quotient (Rel K) on Paths (Gen K), sending
            an object to its attached chain and a morphism to the word of any
            codimension-one factorisation, is a localization at W.

THE FILTRATION.
  T-SUBPSH  the cube chains of degree <= n are a subpresheaf of chainPresheaf;
            restriction along a face never raises the degree. Degree = n is
            not a subpresheaf.
  T-RUNS    the degree-zero subpresheaf is runPresheaf. Hence Ch*(K) is the
            degree-zero part of ECh*(K), and Lines is the degree-zero part of
            LinesAll -- a statement the tree presently lacks in any form.
  T-GRADE   the total degree of a subdivision is the sum of its bead degrees,
            so the filtration of LinesAll by ChainCat.degree (attach z) <= n is
            the convolution of the degree grading of chainPresheaf through the
            oplax monoidal structure of pshExtFunctor.
  T-FILT    T-PRES restricts to each stratum: the generators and relations
            with ChainCat.degree (attach z) <= n present the full subcategory
            of C K on the chains of degree <= n.

THE BOTTOM STRATUM.
  T-BOT     at degree zero Gen's bound <= 1 is forced to = 1, and the
            generators of C(0) K out of a run r ARE the codimension-one arrows
            out of r in Ch K -- one per two-bead window of r that bounds a
            cube of K. Each carries exactly one generator, whose target is the
            other run of that window.
  T-BOT2    the relations out of r are the codimension-two arrows out of r, in
            the two species.
  T-SKEL    C(0) K depends only on the 3-skeleton of K: the comparison
            C(0)(sk_3 K) --> C(0) K induced by the inclusion is an
            isomorphism. Generators see 2-cells, relations 3-cells.

THE CUBE.
  T-CUBE    C(0)(cube n) has n! objects, n-1 generators out of each and
            C(n-1,2) relations out of each, the adjacent pairs of positions
            giving the braid relation and the rest the commuting one.
            Concretely 6/12/6 for n=3 and 24/72/72 for n=4, splitting 48/24.
  T-BRAID   choosing a run to carry the identity permutation extends to an
            isomorphism onto the positive part of BraidGpd n = ActionCategory
            (Braid n) (Perm (Fin n)); the position index of a generator goes
            to the Artin generator of that index, forced rather than chosen.
            Since Braid n is PresentedGroup (germRels n), this comparison IS
            Garside against Artin, and discharges Matsumoto n.

NOT CLAIMED. C K as a whole does not depend on the 3-skeleton -- its objects
are all the chains of K. C(0)(Zbp) is not Artin's one-object presentation: Ch
Zbp is not thin, and at dimSum two the presentation has two loop generators and
no relation while B_2+ is N. Whether Conc identifies them is open.

title: C(K) presented by non-W codim-1 moves, and IsLocalization
description:
C(K) = ECh*(K)[W^-1], presented by the non-trivial codimension-one moves
modulo the codimension-two relations.

W z z' F holds when attach z = attach z'.

Results wanted, in dependency order.

THE HINGE

* attachHom_natural: for F : z --> z' with attach z = attach z', the
  attached refinement of the target composed with F's base arrow is the
  attached refinement of the source. Everything below rests on it.
* eta z : z --> (attach z, trivial subdivision), lying in W at every
  degree, and terminal among the W-arrows out of z. The W-arrows out of
  z are the factorizations of attachHom z, i.e. the interval
  [attach z, z.base] in Ch K.
* the W-local objects -- no non-identity W-arrow out -- are exactly
  those with trivial subdivision, hence the chains of K.
* W is generated, as a class to invert, by the eta's: each w in W is
  eta_z followed by the inverse of eta_z'.

THE PRESENTATION

* Move K c c': z, b, and w : b --> z.base with codim w = 1, together
  with attach z = c, attach (lift z w) = c', and c /= c'.
* Rel K: the same with codim w = 2. A structure, not a Prop, so that
  codimension-three coherence can attach to a type later.
* C K := Quotient (moveRel K) over Paths (MoveQuiver K), and
  loc K : ECh*(K) ==> C K.
* loc_isLocalization : (loc K).IsLocalization (W K). THE TARGET.

THE PAYOFF

* Move.IsAtom m := codim (attachHom m.z) = 1, and: the atoms generate.
* degree 0 is closed under moves, and every move between runs is a
  complement (SiteCut.complHom). The argument is that restriction never
  raises a bead's dimension while dimSum is fixed.
* degree is non-increasing along moves, so C_{<=n}(K) is closed. Less
  certain: the degree-0 argument does not generalise, since bead count
  and bead dimension trade off.
* End of C_0(cube n) at a run is the pure braid monoid; via Zbp, the
  full braid monoid.

NOT WANTED, each deliberately.

* C K is not the full subcategory of ECh* on W-local objects. attach is
  not functorial -- permOf is the obstruction -- and that failure is
  exactly why the braid generators exist.
* W is not required to be generated in codimension one. It is generated
  by the eta's, which are not codimension one.
* Move is not minimal in its base a. There is no canonical minimal
  common coarsening: cut sets do not determine chains (two runs of the
  square share both), and a candidate need not have fillers in K. The
  atoms are carved out afterwards by IsAtom, not built in.
* C K is not graded by degree. A move with trivial subdivision drops the
  degree of the attached chain.

A stepping stone that adjoins formal inverses is acceptable if it helps,
but the goal is the presentation by non-W generators.

Witness: K = Zbp (terminal). A := (dims [2]), B := (dims [1,1]) in Ch Zbp; the two runs of the square give u1 =/= u2 : B --> A (Hom(B,A) is not a subsingleton -- Zbp is self-linked). Let z carry the subdivision named by u1 (attach z = B, attachHom z = u1) and z' := lift z u2. Then attach z' = B by counting alone (a chain of the wedge of an all-ones list has bead count between its length and its dimSum), so W holds; but attachHom z' is an endo of B, hence 1, so the hinge would force u2 = u1.

attach forgets the arrow, so W cannot see the base arrow. Falls with it: eta terminal among W-arrows; 'W-arrows out of z = factorisations of attachHom z' (machine-checked separately); the triangle w >> eta = eta; W generated by the etas.

Survives: W is multiplicative and contains isos (landed, ECh.W); eta_mem_W and 'trivial subdivision => W-local' do not use the hinge.

Repair to decide: W' z z' F := exists h : attach z = attach z', attachHom z' >> F.1.unop = eqToHom h.symm >> attachHom z (arrow-level, not object-level). W' is contained in W, equals it when Ch K is thin (NonSelfLinked + AdmitsAltitude), and makes the hinge definitional.
CORRECTION, machine-checked. W as an OBJECT-level condition (attach z = attach z') is too weak and the hinge attachHom_natural is FALSE for it: over Zbp, Ch Zbp is not thin, so two distinct refinements u1, u2 of the same pair of chains give z with attachHom z = u1 and z' its lift along u2, with attach z = attach z' by bead count while attachHom z' is an endomorphism hence the identity -- the triangle collapses to u1 = u2. attach forgets the arrow while an object of ECh* IS the arrow, so the object-level condition cannot see two subdivisions that differ only in their classifying map. The statement is a thinness statement in disguise. Refutation: scratchpad Hinge.lean, axiom-clean. W is therefore ARROW-level: exists h : attach z = attach z', attachHom z' >> F.base = eqToHom h.symm >> attachHom z. Under it the hinge is definitional, the W-arrows out of z really are the factorizations of attachHom z, and eta is terminal among them. Arrow-level W implies object-level W, with equality exactly when Ch K is thin -- so nothing changes for the cube.
LANDED (sorry-free, axiom-clean, unconditional in K): W at arrow level in Chains/Complexify.lean -- W z z' F := exists h : attach z = attach z', attachHom z' >> F.1.unop = eqToHom h.symm >> attachHom z. IsMultiplicative, isomorphisms_le_W, eq_of_hom_hom kept. Hinge attachHom_natural is now the definition unpacked. Geometric input proved: self_restrict -- pulling a chain of a serial wedge back along its own classifying map trivialises it (via coord_beads_disjoint + the Segal splitting; bead_taut). eta z : z --> trivSub (attach z) with eta_mem_W; the triangle comp_wComp; eta terminal among W-arrows (exists_unique_comp_eta); isWLocal_iff (no non-identity W-arrow out iff attach z = z.base); isInvertedBy_of_eta and map_eq_eta_comp_inv (W generated by the etas). Also proved en route, in Chains/CoordFunctor.lean: every refinement is right-cancellable (wedgeMap_cancel, ChainCat.hom_cancel) -- hence Ch(wedge) is thin with no side condition.

OPEN: the converse half of the interval -- every factorisation attachHom z = u >> v arises from a W-arrow, i.e. attach (liftObj z v) = attach z with attachHom (liftObj z v) = u. Equivalent chain-level statement: for C : Ch(wedge d) with C.map = U >> V, chRestrict V C = (C.dims, U). It is closed under composing V (right-cancellation), so by generation it is equivalent to the codimension-one case, and via the Segal splitting to: C : Ch(cube n), V : wedge[p,q] --> cube n with C.map = U >> V implies the restriction of C to each of V's two beads is the corresponding half of C. The forward half is landed (attachHom_eq_wComp_comp). NOT provable from eta alone: restricting a trivial subdivision along any refinement is again trivial, so 'liftObj y p is trivial' does not pin p.
TWO CORRECTIONS to §2's design, found while landing .29. Neither is machine-checked yet; both are consequences of the already-machine-checked arrow-level W.

(1) Move's non-triviality must be hne : ¬ ECh.W K (ECh.lift z w), NOT c ≠ c'. The bead's comment '-- non-trivial: exactly ¬ W (ECh.lift z w)' asserts the two agree; they do not, and the witness is the SAME one that refuted the object-level hinge. Over Zbp with A = dims [2], B = dims [1,1] and the two runs u1 ≠ u2 : B ⟶ A: take z with attachHom z = u1, and w := u2. Then attach z = B = attach (liftObj z u2), so c = c', but ¬ W (lift z u2) because attachHom (liftObj z u2) = 1 and the W-square would force u2 = u1. So c ≠ c' EXCLUDES this move while ¬W KEEPS it. It must be kept: conjugating it by the etas gives an endomorphism of B in the localization, and that endomorphism is exactly the braid generator (up from the run B to the square and back down the other run). Excluding it kills the braiding, which is the whole point.

(2) §2 IS gated by the converse half of the interval, contrary to 'it does not gate this work'. loc is defined on the presentation, so loc.map F is the composite of the images of the codim-1 steps of ANY factorisation of F, each of which is a Move or an identity. Hence loc.map (eta z) = 1 requires every codim-1 step of eta z to lie in W. Since every refinement is monic (ChainCat.mono), that is exactly: for every factorisation attachHom z = u ≫ v, ECh.W K (ECh.lift z v) -- i.e. restricting z's subdivision along a factor v of the refinement it names gives back u. That is the converse half. Without it, loc does not invert W and IsLocalization is out of reach.

WHAT THE CONVERSE HALF REDUCES TO (a partial self_restrict; self_restrict is the χ = 1 case):
for ψ : ⋁e ⟶ ⋁d and χ : ⋁D ⟶ ⋁e in BPSet,
  ψ.hom ≫ (chainPshEquiv d).symm ⟨D, χ ≫ ψ⟩ = (chainPshEquiv e).symm ⟨D, χ⟩.
The obvious shortcut FAILS: bead_taut gives χ.hom ≫ LHS = χ.hom ≫ RHS immediately, but χ.hom cannot be cancelled -- restriction along χ is not injective on subdivisions. Witness: along a run u1 : ⋁[1,1] ⟶ □2, both the taut chain of □2 and u1's own chain restrict to the trivial chain of ⋁[1,1] (each bead is a 1-face and the 2-cell restricted to it is that 1-cell). So the proof has to compute restriction beadwise through the Segal splitting: the missing lemma is 'ιᵂ e j ≫ (chainPshEquiv e).symm C = the classifying map of C's j-th Segal component', the iterated form of chainPsh_symm_inl/inr.

Step 1 (.29) is landed, so loc can be built by ECh.presentation + Quotient.lift as soon as the above is available.
LANDED (Chains/Localize.lean, sorry-free, axiom-clean, unconditional in K): loc_isLocalization : (loc K).IsLocalization (W K).

C K = Quotient (moveRel K) over Paths (MoveQuiver K); objects are Ch K wrapped in a structure (MoveQuiver), because the bare type synonym lets Ch K's own category instance win the Quiver search. Move and Rel carry (z, z', F : z --> z') rather than (z, b, w : b --> z.base); the target is forced either way (tgt_eq) but the arrow form needs no HEq transport at any call site, and Move.mk z (liftObj z w) (lift z w) recovers the bead's shape. hne is the negation of W, as corrected. Rel is a structure.

New geometry-free input: W is closed under FACTORS (W.of_comp_left via W_lift_of_factor, W.of_comp_right by cancelling the monic first factor). That is what makes every codim-1 step of a W-arrow again a W-arrow, hence loc_map_of_W : loc.map F = eqToHom for F in W -- an identity, not just an iso.

The localization proof: liftF (any functor inverting W, conjugated by the etas -- conj) with facIso : loc >> liftF = Phi up to the etas; natIsoOfLoc ('a family of isos natural over ECh* is natural' -- the moves generate C K) and natIsoOfLoc' ('an iso over ECh* descends to C K', using loc.map (eta z) = eqToHom to move a component from trivSub (attach z) to z). Then Localization.lift/fac + liftNatIso for the unit, natIsoOfLoc' for the counit, and Functor.IsLocalization.of_equivalence_target.

STILL OPEN (section 3): Move.IsAtom and the atoms generate; degree-0 closure; C_{<=n}; End of C_0 (cube n) at a run.

GOTCHA worth the context: rw/simp match at instances transparency, so the object arguments of >> and Functor.map hidden behind the plain defs loc/locPaths/liftF/liftPaths never unify with the chObj/Phi.obj spellings, and Category.assoc fails on a goal that PRINTS as (f >> g) >> h. Also, the second factor of a composition inherits its implicit object args from the first factor's target, so a 'have' stated in one spelling will not rw into it. Cure used throughout: state the step as a have/calc and close it with exact/congrArg/.trans, which unify at default transparency.
SECTION 3, PART 1 LANDED + PART 2 REFUTED (Chains/DegreeZero.lean, sorry-free, axiom-clean, unconditional in K).

DEGREE ZERO IS CLOSED. beadChain C j is the chain a subdivision of a wedge reads at bead j of its base (bead_read). The one new geometric step is beadChain_restrict: restricting a subdivision along a wedge map psi reads, at bead j, the chain at bead (blockIdx psi j) restricted along blockFace psi j -- that is the hL step of restrict_factor, extracted as Complexify.bead_leg_wedge (restrict_factor now uses it). With restrictChain_dim_one (restriction never raises a cube's dimension and never reaches 0) that gives dims_one_restrict, hence:
  ECh.degree_attach_liftObj / ECh.degree_attach_eq_zero : degree (attach z) = 0 -> degree (attach z') = 0 for EVERY morphism of ECh*, not just codim-1 ones (the target of any morphism is a lift, tgt_eq).
  ECh.Move.degree_eq_zero, and ECh.Move.dims_eq : between runs the dimension list itself is preserved -- 'the partitions agree, only the block order differs'. dims_eq is the cheap half of 'every move between runs is a complement'; the SiteCut.complHom half is NOT done (see below).

ATOMS: THE LITERAL CLAIM IS FALSE. Move.IsAtom m := ChainCat.codim (attachHom m.z) = 1 is landed, and so is a machine-checked refutation of 'the atoms generate C K'. A chain c with ONE bead has no proper coarsening, so every move out of it has height 0, never 1 (Move.not_isAtom_of_length_one: dimSum forces the base to have a bead, and codim = 1 - 1 = 0). But moves out of it exist: Move.ofTrivSub turns ANY codim-1 refinement w : b --> c into a move out of trivSub c (the step is not in W because the target refines b, which is strictly finer than c). By induction on MorphismProperty.multiplicativeClosure, nothing generated by atoms leaves such a chain (eq_of_atoms_of_length_one), so not_atoms_generate / not_atoms_generate_ofTrivSub. Over the cube this is Testing/CubeC3's moveList entries with c = a: 18 of the 84 moves of C(cube 3), e.g. (0,0,1).

THE REPAIR, not attempted: IsAtom should be codim (attachHom m.z) <= 1, and then 'the atoms generate' is consistent with all of CubeC3's data (the only height >= 2 moves there are the 24 degree-0 moves with a one-bead base, and those reduce). Its proof is the Tietze reduction and needs TWO mechanisms, both visible in CubeC3: (i) SPLITTING -- for a move (z, w : b --> A) pick a codim-1 factor g1 : d --> b of attachHom (liftObj z w); then g1 >> w is codim 2, so it is a Rel, the step over g1 is in W (W_lift_of_factor) hence free, and the relation rewrites the move as [move over the other middle v] >> [move out of liftObj z v]; (ii) REPARALLELISING -- when attachHom z factors through that v the first factor is free and the height drops. In C(cube 3) the ell=2 move (0,4,9) splits into (0,4,2) >> (2,5,10) by (i) and then (0,4,2) becomes the atom (3,4,5) by (ii). What is missing in general is the TERMINATION measure: over the cube it is the wall-crossing number ell (CubeC3.ell), which is COM-specific; height alone does not decrease at step (i).

Section 3 part 3 (End of C_0 (cube n) at a run = positive pure braid monoid) NOT attempted.
IsAtom and 'the atoms generate' are DEMOTED to a nice-to-have; do not spend on them. They were introduced speculatively, to make the generating set look like Artin's, and nothing consumes them: loc_isLocalization is proved with the full generating set of non-W codimension-one moves, Tietze-equivalent presentations present the same category, and the comparison in Cubical-zmi.13 is a statement about the category rather than about a chosen generating set. The reduction to Artin-shaped generators already happens in the quotient via the relations -- verified in Testing/CubeC3, where the 36 moves between runs collapse to the Cayley graph of S3, two adjacent transpositions per run, by parallel-pair identification and factoring of the length-two moves. The refutation recorded above (atoms as codim = 1 cannot leave a one-bead chain) stands and is correct; it refutes something that was not needed. The repair (codim at most one) plus its missing induction measure is therefore optional tidying, NOT a blocker, and in particular is not a strong-normalization question -- SN belongs to the Garside story (cancellativity, normal forms, the embedding in the group completion) and not here.

title: Cure the wedge-vs-tensor spelling systemically
description:
X or Y (wedge2) and X tensor Y (tensorObj) are the same object - the wedge IS the default MonoidalCategory BPSet instance - but kabstract will not identify them, so monoidal lemmas silently fail to fire on goals that print as if they should. Recorded as a landmine on Cubical-zmi.25 after it cost a codim-2 proof.

Wanted: a systemic cure, not a per-proof workaround. The precedent is BPSet.cubeHom, which cured the toPsh-versus-yoneda.obj trap repo-wide by pinning one spelling.

DIAGNOSE FIRST. wedgeMonoidalStruct is already marked reducible and it still fails, so the mechanism is not simply transparency of the instance - establish what actually blocks the match before choosing a cure. Likely suspects: the projection MonoidalCategoryStruct.tensorObj applied to the instance, versus wedge2 as a bare def.

Candidate cures, to be chosen on the evidence rather than assumed:
- make the wedge notation elaborate to tensorObj, so downstream goals are uniformly tensor-spelled and wedge2 survives only inside the instance definition and the pushout cores that genuinely need it;
- a pinning definition in the cubeHom style;
- a normalization simp lemma, if and only if it actually makes rw fire rather than merely restating the equation.

Note the repo already has a rule bearing on this - notation for TERMS, abbrev for TYPES, because an abbrev in term position breaks keyed matching.

Whatever lands must be checked against a real case: the wedge anti-monoidality of the reversal on Cubical-zmi.19, (X or Y) reversed is Y reversed or X reversed, is the next proof that hits this and is the natural test.

Breaking existing proofs is acceptable; a compat layer is not.
notes:
DIAGNOSIS (machine-checked). The blocker is not transparency. Everything on the unfolding path is already reducible — wedgeMonoidal, wedgeMonoidalStruct and MonoidalCategory.ofTensorHom are all Lean.ReducibilityStatus.reducible, and the instance is implicitReducible — so X tensor Y really does whnf-reduce to wedge2 X Y at .instances transparency. The blocker is that kabstract (the engine under rw/simp) FILTERS candidate subterms BY HEAD INDEX before it ever calls isDefEq. X tensor Y is headed by MonoidalCategoryStruct.tensorObj; X wedge2 Y is headed by BPSet.wedge2. A tensorObj-headed pattern is therefore never even offered the wedge2-headed subterm, at any transparency, in either direction. No simp normalisation lemma can fix this, because the same head-index filter applies to it. The only cure is to pin one spelling, exactly as BPSet.cubeHom did.

CURE CHOSEN: pin the tensor. The wedge notation is DELETED; the wedge is spelled X tensor Y everywhere. Reason it must be that way round rather than the other: mathlib owns the monoidal API (associator, unitors, whiskering, tensorHom, the monoidal tactic) and it is phrased in tensorObj; we own only about fifteen pushout lemmas and can restate those.

SHAPE: Foundations/WedgeMonoidal.lean now has three parts. (1) namespace ChainCat.Wedge2 -- the pushout construction, necessarily in the wedge2 spelling because it precedes the instance; short names inl/inr/desc/condition/hom_ext/assocFwd/mapPsh/leftUnitPsh/etc. (2) the MonoidalCategory BPSet instance. (3) the public API, tensor-typed, every declaration a one-line re-export of the corresponding Wedge2 name by defeq. This bootstrap split is forced: the wrappers cannot be tensor-typed before the instance exists, and the instance cannot exist before the coherence proofs that use the wrappers.

Also moved: serialWedge, the big-wedge notation, serialWedge.iota and serialWedge1 now live after the instance and are DEFINED with tensor, so serialWedge_cons is a tensor-spelled rfl. Deleted: WedgeBP (unused compat alias), wedgeFunctor (unused), wedge2Assoc / wedge2MapIso / wedge2LeftUnit / wedge2RightUnit as public names (callers now use the associator, tensorIso/whiskerLeftIso and the unitors), and WedgeExtend's six duplicated component lemmas plus bpTensorObj_eq. bpUnit_eq moved to WedgeMonoidal.

REMAINING TRAP, one level down and NOT cured: the tensor unit has two spellings, tensorUnit BPSet and the cube of dimension 0. Same head-index mechanism. The public unitor lemmas are pinned to the cube-0 spelling, and bpUnit_eq is the rfl bridge. Worth its own bead if it starts costing.

title: Codim-1/2 as an ISO to a tensorator image (concatHomφ); delete splice
notes:
CLEANUP PASS, all green (lake build CubeChains 1687 jobs; full sweep 1698; no new warnings in touched files).

1. blockPrefix is now a NatIso of BPSet-endofunctors, tensorLeft M cmp tensorLeft V cmp tensorLeft X to tensorLeft Z, assembled from mathlib's tensorLeftTensor twice plus (curriedTensor BPSet).mapIso. blockPrefix_naturality is DELETED: disjoint_square_right now uses (blockPrefix E).hom.naturality h and disjoint_square_left uses (blockPrefix E).inv.naturality_assoc h. Same head-symbol filter as landmine 6, one level down in the IMPLICIT args. Normalising only the hypothesis is not enough.

disjoint_square_left and right do NOT collapse into one lemma. They are opposite-category duals: E identifies the prefix on the SOURCE of the merge w in one and on the TARGET in the other, forced by which of the two stacked codim-1 squares is the tail merge. Both are now a two-step naturality chain with zero monoidal coherence, which is as far as it goes without op-bookkeeping for BPSet.

2. ArrowIso f Theta (Chains/CutData.lean) factors the shared part of CutData, TripleCut, DoubleCut. Plain field iso, declared after w -- NOT a typeclass, NOT extends (the parent parameter Theta depends on the child's later field w).
Proved once on ArrowIso: Subsingleton (unconditional, from serialWedge_iso_unique), src_dims/tgt_dims (take the wedge spelling of A resp B as an argument), hom_ext (Theta is determined by f), and comp (stacking two squares).
DELETED: stacked_square and middle_iso_comp both fold into ArrowIso.comp -- rigidity supplies hkappa internally, so kappa is now an Iso argument and the hkappa hypothesis is gone from both call sites. Also deleted cutSrcIso3, cutSrcIso2, cutTgtIso2: each had exactly one use, and each was already just serialWedgeAppend plus associators, so they are inlined into src_dims/tgt_dims.
ArrowIso.comp takes iota1 and iota2 EXPLICITLY. They cannot be implicit: unifying (?iota2.hom) against (X whiskerLeft (N whiskerLeft S.hom)) is not first-order. That is why the old code got away with implicit ones -- they were pinned by the refine goal first.
codimOneWedgeUnique and codimTwoWedgeUnique keep their statements.

3. Chains/CubePeel.lean gained serialWedgePeel: the peel stated on serial wedges and PNat, so the box-vs-wedge and Nat-vs-PNat translation happens once there instead of at the call site. Generation.lean's last case of generated_wedgeHom_cube went from 20 lines to 4; serialWedge1 occurrences in Generation.lean went 8 to 0, and the ex k' : PNat repack is gone.
Inside serialWedgePeel the same spelling trap bites: the cancellation must be stated as a have in the tensor spelling (box a tensor wedge[k]) because the existential binder forces wedge[a,k] on the goal, and then rw finds nothing. Finish with (Iso.eq_comp_inv _).mpr hfac and .trans, i.e. term level, not rw.

4. Foundations/Reversal.lean: the toPsh crossings are IRREDUCIBLE, do not try to remove them. wedge2Desc lands in an arbitrary PrecubicalSet, not a BPSet, because the two legs of a wedge descent are not bi-pointed (the left leg sends X.final to the junction). So there is no BPSet-level universal property to descend along. (X tensor Y)^rho is not a wedge either, so the forward map cannot be descended and is obtained by reversing revWedgeAux -- which is why revInvolPsh, not revInvol, is what appears. The construction is built down there ONCE and packaged ONCE (isoOfPshInv into revWedge; antipodePsh into antipode); the twenty toPsh are type ascriptions in presheaf-level signatures, not unpack/repack round trips. revCubeHom must also stay presheaf-level: its only callers feed it wedgeInl/wedgeInr composites, which are not bi-pointed.
(revInvol and revFunctor had no callers at the time; zmi.20 supplied them -- revIsoFlip and revCompl.)
=== STANDING CHECKS FOR THIS MODULE (Foundations/Reversal.lean + Chains/Reversal.lean) ===
Both of the first two were fixes made in an earlier pass that ERODED one pass later. They belong
in the brief for any future work on this module, not as one-off cleanups.

CHECK 1 -- no hand-written naturality. An object-indexed family of isos must be a NatIso of
endofunctors, and every naturality square must be its NatTrans.naturality. Same finding as
blockPrefix above. Eroded once: revInvolPsh was a pointwise family carrying THREE hand-written
naturality lemmas, and the API was asymmetric (an inv-direction lemma at BPSet level with no hom
counterpart -- the tell that they were added on demand).
Now: revInvolPshNat : revPshFunctor cmp revPshFunctor iso identity (PrecubicalSet), and
revInvol : revFunctor cmp revFunctor iso identity (BPSet). Every naturality proof is
NatTrans.naturality; revInvol_inv_naturality is deleted outright and revCompl_revCompl uses
revInvol.inv.naturality directly. revPsh_id/revPsh_comp are now Functor.map_id/map_comp.

CHECK 2 -- no cast proliferation. A cast that a field type forces must live at ONE named site.
Eroded once: the add_comm p q renaming of the filler -- the cast that mergeCompl's free target
dimension n was introduced to kill -- came back at ~6 sites inside CutData.compl and its
involution proof. Now fillerSwap p q is the single named iso and mergeCompl_fillerSwap the single
lemma that cancels it. Same device for List.reverse_reverse: serialWedgeRevRev.
Rule of thumb that catches both: count eqToHom/eqToIso in the file before and after. A jump means
a boundary is being crossed at each use instead of named once.

CHECK 3 -- the pinned spelling here is revPsh / revInvolPsh, NOT revPshFunctor.map /
revInvolPshNat.app. Deleting revPsh in favour of the functor spelling was TRIED AND REVERTED:
revPshFunctor.obj X.toPsh does not reassociate against (X^rho).toPsh at rw's instances
transparency, so Category.assoc silently stops firing throughout revWedgeBwd_fwd,
revWedgeAux_bwd and revWedgeFwd_bwd. The two spellings are ONE definition (revPsh :=
revPshFunctor.map, the cubeHom device): the functor is where functoriality and naturality live,
the pinned name is what rw keys on. Do not collapse them.

<yourFunctor>_obj] on BOTH goal and hypothesis, or drop to term-level .trans, which unifies at
default transparency.

title: Generation in codimension 1
description:
Every morphism of Ch(K) factors as a composite of codim-1 morphisms.

Holds for every K with no side conditions: merging two adjacent sub-beads inside a larger bead lands on a face of that bead, and a face of a cube of K is a cube of K, so the intermediate chain exists.

This is what entitles the codim-1 morphisms to be called generators, and it is an input to the localization comparison.

title: Codimension 2 has exactly two species
description:
Results wanted:
- Every codim-2 morphism of Ch(K) either splits one bead into three, or splits two distinct beads into two each. Nothing else occurs.
- The proof is the codim formula: codim = sum over beads of (number of sub-beads - 1).
- The two species are disjoint and exhaustive, as a decidable classification.
notes:
The engine is already proved: codim_eq_sum_splitCount in Chains/Degree.lean, plus sum_beadDim_splitOf (the pieces of a bead have dimensions summing to that bead). What remains is only the codim = 2 case split into the two species.
CORRECTION to the previous note (which is now false): codim_eq_sum_splitCount and sum_beadDim_splitOf were DELETED in the Cubical-zmi.3 simplification, along with splitOf/splitCount. The per-bead sum formula is no longer stated anywhere.

What exists instead is codim_eq_length_sub (codim = beads lost) and exists_cut_of_length_succ (peel one bead via splitWedgeMorphism). Distinguishing the two species needs the per-bead distribution, not just the total, so this bead needs either the per-bead counts reinstated or the species read off a twice-iterated cut (one window of length 3, versus two disjoint windows of length 2). The second looks likelier to be cleaner but is unproven.
SUPERSEDES both earlier notes on this bead. The per-bead decomposition is back, in better form, and builds:

  BeadChains cd (one Ch (cube n) per target bead), BeadChains.dims/.counts, wedgeOf,
  exists_wedgeOf, hom_eq_wedgeOf, and codim_eq_counts:
      codim f + (counts t).length = (counts t).sum
  which is codim = sum of (m_j - 1) rearranged to avoid truncated subtraction.

So the engine this bead needs exists. description:

- (cube d)^rho is isomorphic to cube d (the antipode), and it exchanges the two vertices.
- (wedge a)^rho is isomorphic to wedge (a.reverse).

description:

  the chain it sits over has exactly one lift, and the target of that
  lift is forced.

  codimension-2 morphism factors in exactly two ways -- both transported
  along the projection rather than reproved.
* ECh*(K) is thin and its projection to Ch(K) is a discrete fibration,
  both inherited.

  assembly needs.

title: C(K): the codimension presentation of Ch(K), and its localization
description:
C(K): objects are the chains of K, generators are the codimension-1
morphisms of ECh*(K), relations the codimension-2 ones.

A generator is a codimension-1 refinement of Ch(K) decorated with a
subdivision of its target. Trivial subdivision recovers Ch(K)'s own
codimension-1 arrows, which change degree; non-trivial subdivision gives
the complement arrows, which preserve it. The two are one species, which
is why no grading is involved. The degree-0 part is the Artin /
positive-braid story.

The attached datum is a subdivision of arbitrary degree, not only a run.
ECh*(K) is the category of elements of the presheaf of all subdivisions;
its objects are the arrows of Ch(K). permOf is the degree-0 shadow of the
primitive condition "the attached chain is unchanged", which needs no
permutations.

TARGET: C(K) is equivalent to ECh*(K)[W^-1], where W is the
attached-chain-preserving morphisms. Ungraded on both sides: every object
of ECh*(K) is canonically W-isomorphic to its attached chain at every
degree, so the localization has the chains of K as its objects and the
decorated codimension-1 arrows as its generators.

Why the generators come out right rather than being assumed: inside
ECh*(K) the condition that no bead of the source subdivision is cut by
the target one says the source partition refines the target partition; at
equal degree the partitions then agree and only the block order differs,
which is the complement.

title: DECISION: enrich over Cat, or over the braid category?
description:
USER DECIDES. Do not close this from an agent session.

HARD CONSTRAINT (§4): you CANNOT literally enrich over the braid category as hom-objects. Enrichment over V needs hom-OBJECTS in V. The hom-objects here must be groupoids — their objects are the 1-cells. The braid category's objects are strand counts. So hom-objects cannot live in Braid.

What IS true, and is the flashy statement: CFund K is a Grpd-enriched category equipped with a MONOIDAL 2-FUNCTOR to the delooped braid category, under which 1-cell composition maps to the braid TENSOR (concatenating executions adds strand counts). Both halves already exist: Flow/Flow.lean (flowHom, flowComp) and Salvetti/BraidDeloop.lean (braidDeloopComp, where composition really is n (x) m = n + m).

OPTION A — enrich in Cat (the doc's recommendation). mathlib has NO monoidal structure on Grpd (Cat has CartesianMonoidalCategory; Grpd has only Grpd.has_pi), so EnrichedCategory Grpd is not available off the shelf. Cat hom-objects Cat.of (ConcCat (K;u,v)), composition via FreeGroupoid.lift whose universal property IS strict (lift_spec is an equality). EnrichedCategory Cat = a genuine strict 2-category. Only missing input: chambersConcat associativity/unitality.

OPTION B — build the monoidal structure on Grpd first. More faithful to the intended statement, strictly more work, and mathlib will not help.

TRAP: strictness cannot pass through freeGroupoidProdEquiv — it is Localization.uniq, characterised only up to natural iso. This is what kills the naive Grpd route.

The user's §10 note asks whether we can enrich over the braid category directly (objects = naturals, morphisms n->n = braid words). Per §4 that is exactly the thing that does not typecheck as an enrichment; it IS the monoidal 2-functor. Confirm the user wants the 2-functor framing.
notes:
RESOLVED BY USER (2026-07-14). Option A: enrich in Cat. NOT Cat/B, NOT Grpd.

WHY NOT Cat/B (the slice): it is the SAME DATA as (Cat-enrichment + strict 2-functor to the delooping) — change of base along the strict monoidal forgetful U : Cat/B -> Cat is iso on the underlying 2-category. And its EXISTENCE is vacuous: the trivial lift Phi_0 (every 2-cell |-> the identity braid on its strands) is a valid Cat/B-enrichment on the same 2-category. So the slice packaging costs ~300 lines of MonoidalCategory (Over M) (absent from mathlib) to restate what we already have.

WHY NOT Grpd: mathlib gives Grpd NO monoidal structure (only HasProducts). Cat has CartesianMonoidalCategory + CatEnriched (EnrichedCategory Cat => Bicategory.Strict) off the shelf. Hom-objects are still the groupoids ConcGrpd; 'every 2-cell is invertible' is a property from FreeGroupoid, not structure the base must carry.

TARGET: CFund K : EnrichedCategory Cat, plus Phi : CFund K -> MonoidalSingleObj B, a 2-functor to the delooped braid category.

CONTENT WARNING: since Phi_0 exists, 'CFund K is braid-enriched' is VACUOUS. The theorem is that the canonical event-count grading LIFTS to a braid grading, and that OUR lift is not trivial: writhe = salWind, S_n-shadow = evPerm, loops pure iff HDA. Bead 791 (composition |-> tensor) holds for Phi_0 too and is NOT the headline.

title: READ FIRST: braid-thread landmines and refuted claims
description:
Pinned reference. Source: BRAID_ENRICHMENT_CLEANUP.md §6, §7, §8.3, §10.

LANDMINES (each cost real time):
1. equivWedgeCat / refineToWedge CARRY NonSelfLinked + AdmitsAltitude. Routing through them silently imports both while the statement LOOKS unconditional. Never route through the RefineObj<->Ch bridge when the point is to have no side conditions. RefineConcat.append is unusable for the same reason. Unconditional replacements: Chains/Segal.lean's chConcat / wedgeInclL / wedgeInclR.
2. (n :: A) ++ B vs n :: (A ++ B) are defeq but not syntactically equal, and sit inside serialWedge/pushout TYPE arguments. rw/simp/reassoc/Category.comp_id silently fail to match. Use erw with FULLY EXPLICIT arguments (bare erw triggers a whnf blow-up through pushout/colimit).
3. Type's morphisms are bundled TypeCat.Hom; comp_apply/types_comp_apply do NOT fire in simp (ConcreteCategory outParams wreck the discrimination keys). Use exact/defeq.
4. Functor.map_id / map_comp unqualified resolve to the MONAD Functor under `open CategoryTheory`. Write CategoryTheory.Functor.map_id.

REFUTED - DO NOT RESURRECT:
1. "evPerm f = 1 for every morphism <-> K is an HDA" is FALSE, machine-checked (forall_isRun_of_evPerm_one). It forces every chain to be a run, i.e. K has NO concurrency. Witness: the square has a global naming AND a non-run chain. PURITY IS A STATEMENT ABOUT LOOPS.
2. Lifting a chain loop does NOT give an execution loop. A lifted loop at `a` is a path (a, L0) ~> (a, M): same chain, DIFFERENT line. The line must be SHIFTED back (exists_lineShift). Lines must be shifted, not just lifted.

DO NOT ATTEMPT:
- Do not shorten braidFunctor. It is ~70 lines and its proof is already the right one.
- Do not reuse salSumEquiv for the braid tensor. COM.directSum's ground set is only the WITHIN-block pairs; the extension-by-block-order is the whole content.
- Do not hand-roll freeGroupoidProdEquiv. It comes free from mathlib's Localization/Prod.lean.
notes:
LANDMINE 6 (cured; the cure is the reason the tree now spells the wedge as tensor). rw and simp select candidate subterms by HEAD SYMBOL (kabstract's HeadIndex filter) BEFORE they ever attempt isDefEq. So two spellings of one object with different heads can never be matched against each other, at any transparency, in either direction, and no normalisation simp lemma helps because the same filter applies to it. Machine-checked instance: X tensor Y is headed by MonoidalCategoryStruct.tensorObj and the old X wedge2 Y by BPSet.wedge2, while EVERYTHING on the unfolding path was already reducible (wedgeMonoidal, wedgeMonoidalStruct, MonoidalCategory.ofTensorHom all reducible; the instance implicitReducible). Marking things reducible is never the fix. The fix is to pin ONE spelling, as BPSet.cubeHom did for the cube. Cure in place: the wedge notation is deleted; the wedge is X tensor Y everywhere; wedge2 survives only inside ChainCat.Wedge2, the pushout construction that fills the MonoidalCategory BPSet instance, and the glue0 cores. Same mechanism, still live one level down: tensorUnit BPSet versus the cube of dimension 0 (bpUnit_eq is the rfl bridge), and any object argument that sits under a non-reducible def, e.g. a Ch object's .dims.
LANDMINE 6, third instance, one level further down. Replacing an Iso-valued helper by a NatIso and using (natIso).app blocks Category.assoc: the app's object arguments elaborate to Functor.obj (tensorLeft ..) .., and tensorLeft is an abbrev but curriedTensor is a plain def, so at rw/simp transparency (f >> g) >> h does not match a term that PRINTS as (f >> g) >> h. Confirmed with pp.explicit. Cure: simp only [Functor.comp_obj, Functor.comp_map, curriedTensor_obj_obj, curriedTensor_obj_map, Iso.app_hom, Iso.app_inv] on BOTH the hypothesis and the goal -- normalising only the hypothesis is not enough. Worked example: disjoint_square_left/right in Chains/CodimTwo.lean, prefixNatIso/blockPrefix in Chains/CutData.lean.
DO NOT DELETE, despite zero call sites. Two results in this tree have no consumers and are wanted anyway; call-site count is not evidence of vestigiality. (1) equivWedgeCat (Chains/Correspondence.lean) is the cited paper's section 3 correspondence -- keep it, and keep refineToWedge/wedgeToRefine/RefineObj/ChainRefine with it. (2) Braids/BraidFib/braidIncl/strands/braidHom (Braid/Category.lean), the graded encoding of the braid groupoid, is retained for the full Artin monoid story; it duplicates FullBraid (Braid/Full.lean) with no bridge, and that is known and accepted. Anything that looks like a stated result should be REPORTED, not deleted.

title: DECISION: generalize Ch/Lines/ConcCat to take endpoints, or keep repoint as the idiom?
description:
USER DECIDES. §8.2 says 'Decide once.' — so decide once.

OPTION A: generalize Ch / Lines / ConcCat to take endpoints as parameters.
OPTION B: keep BPSet.repoint K u v (Flow/ChainConcat.lean) as the official idiom and delete the bipointing from everything that does not use it.

The evidence for B: K.repoint K.init K.final = K is rfl (structure eta). That is a strong hint that repoint is the cheap, honest move and A is churn.

DONE WHEN: the choice is recorded here, with the reason.
close_reason:
DECISION: OPTION B — repoint is the idiom. Endpoints are a PARAMETER, not a commitment.

The evidence is decisive and it was already sitting in the repo:
- BPSet = <toPsh, init, final>. repoint K u v swaps only the two vertices; toPsh is untouched, so
  (K.repoint u v).cells n = K.cells n by rfl, and K.repoint K.init K.final = K by rfl (structure eta).
- Flow/ ALREADY runs entirely on this idiom: flowHom K u v := ConcGrpd (K.repoint u v), plus flowId,
  flowComp, chConcMor_assoc and the unit laws — all proved against Ch (K.repoint u v).

Option A (generalize Ch/Lines/ConcCat to take endpoints) would rebuild by hand exactly what repoint
gives for free, and would break every one of those existing lemmas. It is pure churn. Rejected.

NOTE the §8.2 premise ('BPSet is bipointed and most of the development does not need it') is
MISLEADING. The bipointing is STRUCTURAL, not spurious: Ch K is by definition the chains from K.init
to K.final, so Ch — and everything downstream (Lines, ConcCat, braidFunctor) — genuinely needs a
BPSet. What those files do NOT do is READ the endpoints: BraidFunctor, Lines, ConcGroupoid and
EventNaming contain ZERO references to K.init/K.final. They need endpoints to EXIST, not to be
anything in particular. Parameterizing them (repoint) is therefore the whole and correct answer.

title: Ch(wedge d)[W-1] presented bead by bead; verdict on Product.lean
description:
DELIVERED, green at 1743, sorry-free.
Concurrency/Presentation/SlicePresentation.lean (new, 57 lines, in CubeChains.lean):

  instIsThinProd            -- a product of thin categories is thin
  locSlice_isThin d         -- Ch(wedge d)[W-1] IS A POSET, by induction along locChConsEquiv
  slicePoly d               -- [] => thin (CubeStep 0); n :: rest => prod (thin (CubeStep n)) (slicePoly rest)
  slicePresentation d : Presents (slicePoly d) ((W (wedge d)).Localization)
  overSlicePresentation d : Presents (slicePoly d) (((W Zbp).over (zObj d)).Localization)

The whole induction is
  | [] => cubePresentation 0
  | n :: rest => ((cubePresentation n).prod (slicePresentation rest)).transport (locChConsEquiv n rest)
It compiled first try. WedgeLocalize.lean is no longer 0-of-22 consumed: locChConsEquiv and
locOverEquivWedge are both load-bearing here.

VERDICT ON Machinery/Presentation/Product.lean (B2): KEEP. IT IS THE RIGHT TOOL AND IT IS NOW
CONSUMED. Two independent reasons.

(1) SHORTER. Presents.prod is hypothesis-free -- (p : Presents P A) (q : Presents Q B) : Presents
(Polygraph.prod P Q) (A x B), no side conditions -- so the induction step is ONE LINE. Going
through Presents.ofThin instead would mean building the coordinatewise quiver, its interpretation,
and full + essSurj, all by induction and all transported through locChConsEquiv at each step --
which is prod_full and prod_essSurj re-derived with the relations thrown away. Strictly more work
for a strictly weaker output.

(2) BETTER OUTPUT. The target IS thin (locSlice_isThin), so ofThin applies; but Polygraph.thin
quotients by EVERY parallel pair, whereas Polygraph.prod's 2-cells are the factors' relations plus
ProdRel.interchange -- named, finite, and saying exactly the thing worth saying: ATOMS IN DIFFERENT
BEADS COMMUTE. That is the same alignment argument that makes an Artin presentation preferable to
an all-relations one: a presentation whose 2-cells mean something survives being lifted and glued;
'all parallel pairs' cannot match anything downstream.

So my earlier guess that ofThin might supersede B2 was WRONG, and the test settles it the other
way. ofThin remains the right tool where there is no product structure to expose -- that is
cubePresentation, which is what slicePresentation's factors are.

NOTE ON THE SHAPE: the recursion leaves a trailing Polygraph.thin (CubeStep 0) factor, because
wedge [] = box 0. It is a one-object, no-generator polygraph, so it is harmless; locOverSingleton
strips the analogous box 0 with the right unitor if a stripped form is ever wanted.

ALSO MOVED: isThin_of_equiv from Machinery/Presentation/GlueRefutation.lean (a refutation file) to
Machinery/Presentation/Basic.lean, beside Polygraph.thin -- it is a general fact with two consumers
now and mathlib has no IsThin transport along an equivalence.
notes:
DONE and committed. slicePresentation d : Presents (slicePoly d) ((W (wedge d)).Localization), plus overSlicePresentation and locSlice_isThin. One line per constructor because Presents.prod is hypothesis-free.

VERDICT ON Product.lean: KEEP — it is the right tool and is now load-bearing. Presents.ofThin also applies (the slice is thin) but quotients by every parallel pair, where Polygraph.prod's 2-cells are the factors' relations plus ProdRel.interchange: atoms in different beads commute. A presentation whose 2-cells mean something survives being lifted and glued. ofThin is right where there is no product structure to expose (the cube factors); prod where there is. WedgeLocalize.lean also went from 0-of-22 consumed to load-bearing.

title: The chart action as a functor on Ch(Z)[W-1], not generator-wise
description:
ASSESSMENT (survey only, nothing built).

THE MACHINERY IS ALREADY GENERAL. Presents.partialElements (Machinery/Presentation/Partial.lean:248)
already reads
  partialElements (G : C -> Type t) (bot) (hbot) (p : Presents P C) : Presents ... 
with p COMPLETELY UNCONSTRAINED. Partial.lean needs no restating. The design flaw is one level up:
partialAction (:294) calls it with G := (optionAction phi pact hsound).toFunctor p -- the functor is
MANUFACTURED FROM p, which is why hsound quantifies over P.rel. Supply a p-independent G and every
presentation is served at once, with no change to Partial.lean.

DOES THE ACTION FACTOR THROUGH THE LOCALIZED BASE? Two separate answers.

(1) NOT with charts-over-the-shape as fibres, and the reason is sharper than a functoriality
failure: the assignment is not DEFINED on C's objects at all. Ch(Z)[W-1] at strand count N is ONE
object (strandComponentGarside), so all shapes of a given dimSum are isomorphic there, while their
chart sets are not in bijection (charts over 1^N are runs of K; charts over [N] are N-cells).
Equivalently: Q w is an iso in C for w in W, a functor sends isos to bijections, and mergeLift is
only a RETRACTION -- mergeLift_map gives mergeLift . restrict = id, while restrict . mergeLift is
the partial identity on the liftable charts. Option-ifying does not repair this; a non-surjective
injection is not invertible in Type or in Par. A chart-fibred functor on C exists iff InvertsMerges
K, i.e. IsSegal-strength, which the bare cube fails. This is why PartialAtom picks a REPRESENTATIVE
(the run) instead, and that choice is forced, not stylistic.

(2) WITH run-charts as fibres it does factor, and this is the reformulation worth having. The
endomorphism monoid of the strand-N object is PosBraid N, so G is exactly a monoid hom
PosBraid N ->* (partial endos of runcharts). By posBraid_equiv_artinPos (PosBraid N ~=* ArtinPosBraid
N = the monoid presented by ArtinRel), such a hom IS an Artin family: IsArtinFamily g

title: hasDiamonds_disjoint: the far species is a theorem, not a hypothesis
description:
HasDiamonds currently hypothesises BOTH species of codimension-two join, but only the ADJACENT one is genuinely a hypothesis — that is the 3-cell. The FAR species (|i-j| >= 2) should be provable for EVERY K: two disjoint squares need no cell of K beyond themselves. Wanted: hasDiamonds_disjoint, unconditional; after which HasDiamonds can be weakened to the adjacent case alone.

This is also exactly what hsound's COMMUTATION case reduces to: the two disjoint squares assemble into one chart over the far codimension-two shape, and that chart's two factorisations are the two orders. The assembly is the whole difficulty.

NO EXTRA HYPOTHESIS IS NEEDED. Both ingredients are unconditional: chConcat is stated unconditional in Segal/Split, and chObjEquiv/splitObj needs only Z.AdmitsAltitude, which a serial wedge always has (BlockDecomp:239 says so explicitly).

TWO ROUTES, ONE BLOCKED BY POLICY AND ONE BY ABSENCE:
- via Grading/BlockDecomp (blockIdx/blockFace/beadCell bookkeeping) — this is EXACTLY the vocabulary CLAUDE.md forbids in a new proof. Do not take it.
- via the sanctioned cut vocabulary the argument IS Coarser.exists_diamond (Coarser.lean:456), whose single Zbp-specific step is 'obtain rfl : w = w' := Obj.eq_of_dims (boundaries_injective ...)'. A Ch Zbp object is pinned by its SHAPE; for Ch K an object is shape PLUS chart, so that is precisely the step that fails.

SO THE MISSING PIECE IS PINPOINTED: replace Obj.eq_of_dims by an explicit construction of the joint chart, via the wedge splitting (chConcat / chObjEquiv), which is sanctioned vocabulary. That exists_diamond fails to generalise for a locatable reason also confirms HasDiamonds is real content rather than an artefact.

title: hsound's braid case: HasDiamonds is necessary but not shown sufficient
description:
The five-step derivation recorded on Cubical-vcp DOES NOT CLOSE. What was verified was that each named ingredient exists in the tree, not that the derivation goes through. Three independent gaps:

(1) WRONG DIRECTION at steps 3-4. exists_atom_step requires an ASCENT (sigma (adjLo k) < sigma (adjHi k)) and factors a leg THROUGH mergeOnes N k. But an atomAct step is a DESCENT — descent_of_word_step gives sigma (adjHi i) < sigma (adjLo i). The leg from x0 to the codimension-two cell is the MOST CROSSED one, so it factors through no merge at all. This is not exists_atom_step in an unavailable form; it is the wrong lemma for that position.

(2) STEPS 1-2 GIVE LESS THAN CLAIMED. HasDiamonds produces SOME join e with no control over its legs' crossings: v1 then p = u2 then q yields only crossPerm p-bar * adjT i = crossPerm q-bar — one equation, two unknowns. Neither e's shape nor its crossing data is pinned.

(3) THE CUBE USES ALL THREE STEPS. Route A being defined at x0 forces the 3-window of x0 to be FULLY decreasing, which is a LENGTH COUNT across all three steps (each drops permLen by one). A two-step argument cannot see that count. With the window fully decreasing, j is a descent of x0 and route B follows; without it, nothing does.

THE HONEST SHAPE: the cube's own version, word_unique (CubeThin.lean), is an INDUCTION ON permLen using word_diamond plus exists_word for fullness — not a one-shot diamond. A general proof presumably needs the same shape. But its length parameter is a BASE notion — the crossPerm length of the leg to the top — and Ch K need not carry it at all, since K may have no chart over the top shape. THAT is the real obstacle, and it is not obviously repaired by strengthening HasDiamonds.

So HasDiamonds may still be NECESSARY; it is NOT SHOWN SUFFICIENT.
notes:
SETTLED FOR THE CUBE (Concurrency/Presentation/CubeChartAction.lean, green).
isArtinFamily_cubeAtom proves BOTH relations for atomAct at K = cube n, and the BRAID CASE USES NO
3-CELL: hasDiamonds_cube, exists_join and the whole CubeFaces counting/meet layer are unused.

WHY IT WORKS HERE. The obstacle recorded on this bead was that word_unique's induction needs a
length parameter Ch K need not carry. In the reformulation there is no induction: by
posBraid_equiv_artinPos a monoid hom out of PosBraid n IS an Artin family, so only two equations
remain. And both come out of a DOMAIN CHARACTERISATION rather than a codimension-two cell:
  atomAct k is defined at x  <=>  k is an ASCENT of cross x,  and then cross jumps by adjT k.
Each three-letter route is then defined exactly when the 3-window is increasing -- the same three
inequalities in a different order -- so the two routes have the same domain, and adjT_braid gives
the same value. Gap (1) of this bead (wrong direction: ascent vs descent) turns out to be the KEY:
the merge leg needs an ascent, the atom leg a descent, and that is what makes the domains match.
Gap (2) (HasDiamonds gives some join with no control) is simply not reached.

WHAT DOES NOT GENERALISE. The (<=) half of the domain characterisation constructs the square as the
atom face of the flipped run (exists_atom_face) and identifies the leg as THE merge
(existsUnique_W_ones). That is the cube's own cells. For a general K, atomAct's domain is only
'x lifts along mergeOnes', with no description, and the two routes' domains need not agree -- which
is where a 3-cell would be needed. So this bead's conclusion ('HasDiamonds necessary, not shown
sufficient') STANDS FOR GENERAL K; what changes is that the cube no longer needs it at all, and
that the general obstruction is now located precisely: it is the DOMAIN, not the value.

title: Localizing a discrete fibration at a class the presheaf only separates
description:
The unique-lift half of Cubical-vcp is NOT an instantiation of existing machinery. Machinery/Localization/FibrationLocalize proves exactly the wanted statement — all of the base's formal inverses lift and nothing else is created — but its hypothesis is that the presheaf INVERTS W. Under SeparatesMerges the presheaf does not invert, so that file does not apply, and ITS CONCLUSION IS FALSE AS STATED IN THAT REGIME: the localization is the DEFINED PART of a partial category of elements, not the whole integral of P-bar.

So this needs a new localization theorem: localizing a discrete fibration at a class the presheaf merely SEPARATES. Inputs that now exist: separatesMerges_cube (so the hypothesis is non-vacuous), mergeLift (Function.partialInv of the restriction map, with mergeLift_eq_some_iff), and Machinery/Presentation/Partial.lean's defined/partialElements/partialAction/definedEquiv, which were built for exactly this case and whose fit at the cube was verified by instantiation.

This is where the remaining risk in Cubical-vcp sits.

TARGET, in the orientation the tree forces: (defined (cubeFibre n) (cubeBot n)).FullSubcategory =~ WeakOrder n, hence =~ ((W (box n)).Localization)^op by locCubeWeakOrder + opOpEquivalence. Two independent reasons force the ^op: cubeFibre lives on ((W Zbp).op).Localization with Ch K =~ ((wedgeHoms K).Elements)^op, and atomAct goes UP the weak order where a localization morphism goes DOWN. Cubical-vcp already lists the same orientation.

  chartAction n beta (some xi) = some xi'  <->  crossOnes xi' = crossOnes xi * posPermHom n beta
                                                AND toAdd (posLen n beta) = permLen (posPermHom n beta)

i.e. a braid is defined at a chart exactly when it is REDUCED, and then it multiplies the crossing permutation. Two nested inductions: chartAction n (posPerm sigma) = matsuLift (cubeAtom n) sigma (from posPerm_eq_matsuLift + map_matsuLift, both inside posBraid_equiv_artinPos's own proof), then an induction on permLen sigma via matsuLift_mul_adjT_ascent (Matsumoto.lean:148) and eq_matsuLift_of_ascent (:179).

title: glue does not present the localization: L.ob d must be a bijection
description:
Presents (glue X L) ((int X)[W'^-1]) is FALSE under the hypotheses of Cubical-0ws (Presents (P d) ((Over d)[W^-1]) plus hL, hP). Two independent counterexamples, each killing one half of the missing hypothesis.

(a) L.ob d NOT SURJECTIVE onto the identity => glue has too few morphisms.
D = {0 -w-> 1} plus identities; W = {w} + identities. Over 1 is the walking arrow (Over.mk w -> Over.mk 1_1) and (W.over 1)^-1 inverts it, so it is the contractible groupoid on two objects; Over 0 is terminal. Take P.obj 0 and P.obj 1 each a single 0-cell with NO generators, L.ob 0 c0 = 1_0, L.ob 1 a = Over.mk w. Then presented (P.obj d) is terminal and E is an equivalence in both cases, hL holds, and hP at w holds because Over.map w (Over.mk 1_0) = Over.mk w. Take X the terminal presheaf, so (int X)^op = D and W' = W. GlueGen is EMPTY (no generators anywhere), so presented (glue X L) is DISCRETE on two objects, while (int X)[W'^-1] is the contractible groupoid on two objects. Not equivalent.
Cause: glue's 0-cells are all of GlueV X, but the 0-cell (d,x) lies in the copy at (d,x) only when some a has L.ob d a = Over.mk (1_d).

(b) L.ob d NOT INJECTIVE => glue has too many morphisms.
D terminal, W the isomorphisms, X the terminal presheaf; then Over * , (int X)^op and the localization are all terminal. Take P.obj * with 0-cells {a,a'} and generators e : a -> a', e' : a' -> a, relations e.e' ~ nil and e'.e ~ nil. presented (P.obj *) is the contractible groupoid on two objects, hence equivalent to the terminal localization, so p * is a Presents; hL and hP are trivial. Both 0-cells carry the same label (Over * has one object), so gluePt collapses them: glue has ONE 0-cell v and TWO loops E, E' at v, with only the copy relations E.E' = 1 and E'.E = 1. End v is therefore the free group on E, i.e. Z, not trivial. Concretely E is sent to 1 by the sound assignment E |-> 1, E' |-> -1 into SingleObj (Multiplicative Z), so E is not the identity, while glueDesc sends it to the identity: glueDesc is not faithful.
Cause: two 0-cells of P d with the same label become one 0-cell of glue, but their 1-cells do not get identified, so words that were not composable in P d become composable in glue.

WANTED: the corrected statement and its proof. hL says (p d).at' <a> = objEquiv (L.ob d a) and objEquiv is a bijection, so 'L.ob d bijective' is exactly '(p d).E bijective on objects' -- the presentation names each object of Over d exactly once. (a) needs surjectivity onto 1_d, (b) needs injectivity; bijectivity gives both and is what the intended applications satisfy. Under it, eta's component at the 0-cell (d,x) should be the unit of p d at the base 0-cell (L.ob d)^-1 (Over.mk 1_d), read through glueIncl d x, and the copy at (e, X f x) sits inside the copy at (d,x) for every f : e -> d because f is a label. Also affects Cubical-rxc (A5 GlueOn) and SlicePresentation.md's A4.

COUNTEREXAMPLE (b) IS NOW FORMALISED, sorry-free and axiom-clean.

title: Presents.glue: the two isos and the equivalence
description: A4 landed Psi (glueRetractDesc) but not Presents.glue. Remaining shape: (i) elementsLift_post — expected STRICT, since elements_snd_map gives exactly X.map (pi.map Y.hom).op c.unop.2 = Y.left.unop.2; (ii) glueRetractPre_desc, the leg iso, giving glueRetractPre c comp Phi iso Over.forget c comp Q_C, whose RHS is precisely the overCoconeLocEquiv leg of the identity; (iii) descend to epsilon via liftNatIso; (iv) eta by the same route on presented via Quotient.lift_unique'; (v) Presents.glue. 1. labelsOf does NOT satisfy bijectivity on its own. Now formal, in Glue.lean:
     presentedVEquiv (Q : Polygraph) : Q.V ≃ Q.presented        (:172, Quotient and Paths leave
                                                                 objects alone)
     labelsOf_ob_bijective_iff (d) :
       Function.Bijective ((labelsOf W p hP).ob d) ↔ Function.Bijective (p d).E.obj   (:318)
   So 'L.ob d bijective' is exactly '(p d).E bijective on objects'. Presents asks only for an
   equivalence, so this is a HYPOTHESIS ON p, not a consequence of it; labelsOf then transports
   it. The corrected statement is NOT wrong -- the hypothesis simply lands on p, and the
   Construction-style presentations the applications use (0-cells = objects of the slice) satisfy
   it. Two worked examples confirm the mechanism: D = {0 ⇉ 1} with X terminal, and D = 0→1→2,
   both give presented(glue) ≅ D on the nose, the second because the overlap relation at v
   identifies the copy-at-1 generator with the copy-at-2 one. The general mechanism is that a
   generator for h : a → b in the copy at (d,x) is identified, via the overlap at L.ob d b, with
   the canonical generator in the copy at b's own 0-cell -- which needs L.ob to be SURJECTIVE
   (so that both Over.mk h and 𝟙 are labels) and INJECTIVE (so that (P.map f).cells sends
   base e to a on the nose).

2. THE FORK. Under that hypothesis (p d).E is fully faithful AND bijective on objects, hence an
   ISOMORPHISM OF CATEGORIES, so it has a STRICT inverse. Verified in scratch (Strict.lean,

     comp_strictInv : F ⋙ strictInv F h = 𝟭 C

   conjugate hP by two equivalences, and glueRetractStep is 'the only non-strict step'. With
   strictInv, glueRetractStep is an eqToIso, glueRetractPreDesc is an eqToIso, and -- the point --
   eta collapses:

   and then Φ(quot gen) = eqToHom ≫ gse.map (E.map (quot g)) ≫ eqToHom, so

   exactly as SlicePresentation.md's A4 originally said.

   Needs gse ⋙ Ψ ≅ inv ⋙ glueIncl as an iso, the cross-copy component agreement, and a

title: WeakOrder n is a lattice; meets of lower covers
description: The right weak (Bruhat) order on Perm (Fin n) is a lattice. Provide the lattice structure on WeakOrder n (Concurrency/Merge/CubeWeakOrder.lean), and the fact that the meet of two lower covers of sigma is cross (d1 join d2) for the corresponding faces. This is what makes the induction on permLen sigma - permLen tau go through: given parallel p q from sigma to tau with distinct first covers, tau <= tau1 meet tau2, so both factor through the confluence point. CHECK MATHLIB FIRST — the weak order on a Coxeter group being a lattice may already be there, or derivable from Mathlib's Coxeter/Bruhat material. Needed by Cubical-yki.

Inversion.lean gives inversion sequences of reduced words (rightInvSeq/leftInvSeq), IsRightInversion,
IsRightDescent — but NO weak order, NO Bruhat order, NO lattice instance, and no CoxeterSystem
instance for Equiv.Perm (Fin n). Grepping 'Bruhat' across mathlib hits only Algebra/Module/Lattice.lean,
unrelated. Connecting it would also cost extra: the repo's permLen is its own (inversions σ).card, not
CoxeterSystem.length.

anything below two lower covers of σ is below the permutation sorting their merged window. The
inversion-set route (right weak order = containment of inversions (σ⁻¹), via the symmetric-difference

adjLo_ne_adjHi, adjLo_eq_adjHi, descent_mul_adjT_far, descent_mul_adjT_braid₁, descent_mul_adjT_braid₂;

title: W is closed under joins
description: For each permutation sigma, the W-class of chains with cross = sigma is an interval [runAt sigma, D(sigma)] in Ch (□n) — the vertex star of sigma in the permutohedron. Provide D(sigma), the terminal object of that class, and the arrow c to D(sigma) for every c in the class (in W). Warning already established: sigma to D(sigma) is NOT monotone — D(231) = 23|1 has no map to D(213) = 2|13 — so this cannot be used as a normal form. Needed by Cubical-yki.
notes:
RE-SCOPED. The original framing (D(sigma) as the terminal object of a W-class) was wrong, and the
recorded warning that sigma to D(sigma) is not monotone is now IRRELEVANT rather than a caveat — that
warning was about D as a normal form, and nothing in the proof uses D at all.

WHAT THE yki INDUCTION ACTUALLY CONSUMES. The proof needs a canonical family CAN with: Q f = CAN for
every Ch-morphism, wInv w = CAN for every W-arrow, and multiplicativity — the only shape
Localization.Construction.morphismProperty_eq_top accepts. Unwinding the first gives exactly:
g_{sigma,d} := Q(r_sigma to d) then Q(r_tau to d)inv depends only on cross d, not on d. That follows
from the WEAK fact alone: if d, d' have the same cross and admit a common coarsening e STILL IN THAT
CLASS, then d to e and d' to e are both W, so g_{sigma,d} = g_{sigma,e} = g_{sigma,d'}. The terminal
object is never used, only pairwise joins inside the class. (Finite poset makes the two equivalent,
but the weak form is what is consumed and is far easier to state.)

NOT SUBSUMED by Cubical-209, and the reason is instructive — they are COMPLEMENTARY REGIMES:
- exists_join is restricted to two CODIMENSION-ONE steps out of a common source; two faces in a class
  are generally not codim 1 over their run.
- cross_of_meet_far/_braid compute the join's cross precisely when BOTH steps cross (the join drops
  the crossing number by 2 or 3). The class statement is the opposite regime: NEITHER step crosses,
  and the join must drop nothing.

NEW STATEMENT: W is closed under joins — two refinements of a chain that cross nothing have a common
coarsening that crosses nothing.

COSTED PROOF (worked before proposing, ~150 lines, most of it the generalised join):
1. cross d = cross d' gives flatten d = flatten d' (cross_eq_flatten_inv) — same event order, differing
   only in where junctions sit.
2. For consecutive events either side of a junction of the join: the join's junctions are those of
   both, so that junction is missing from d or from d', so those events share a bead there, and within
   a bead coordinates rise (flatten_lt_iff).
3. Chaining (2) along the bead: within every join-bead, coordinates rise in event order. That is the
   transitivity making the class an interval.
4. flatten_apply identifies flatten e = flatten d, i.e. cross e = cross d.

THE ONE GAP: step 2 needs the join at ARBITRARY codimension with its boundary-intersection
description; exists_join currently hides that behind codim = 1. Either generalise exists_join (induct
peeling codim-1 steps via exists_first), or realise the intersection shape directly — the tree has
boundaries_injective but no 'every boundary set is a shape', though mathlib's
Composition/CompositionAsSet equivalence supplies it.
close_reason: Closed
