  is `Presents.elements` (Findings 1 and 3) and Retraction is not on that path.  So no amount of
  un-opping Retraction changes the op in any headline result; (b) only chooses WHERE between
  posGrade and chLocPresentation the op-boundary sits.

CORRECTION TO FINDING 4 (my own, from the survey above).
  The 15 ᵐᵒᵖ in Retraction are NOT irreducibly forced.  They exist to undo the ᵒᵖ in the
  localization — the file's own docstring says "x * y = x ≫ y only after op".  Un-op the
  localization and RunLoops becomes a plain End, and the ᵐᵒᵖ is not needed.  So (b)'s ceiling in
  Retraction is higher than the survey said: ~91 → the interface cost, not ~48.

WHAT (b) IS WORTH, HONESTLY
  It is a readability change, not an op-elimination: Retraction's own mathematics is un-opped
  (posGrade : Ch Zbp ⥤ FullPosBraid) and it currently pays 91 tokens to sit on the opped side.
  Moving the boundary to its exports would clear the 62 body ops and cost a bridge in
  BaseComponent/HAction.  Worth doing — but it is a refactor of a 364-line proof-dense file plus
  two consumers, NOT the local adapter change it appeared to be, and its rationale is legibility
  rather than removing ops.

CONSEQUENCE FOR (a)
  (a)'s case is stronger and now precisely bounded: the forced op lives in `Presents.elements`,
  and a fibration-side analogue is the only thing that deletes it.  (b) cannot substitute for it.

title: Ch(box n)[W-inv] is not PosBraidAction n: record the refutation
description:
A negative result the project should own, in the style of not_isSegal_cube_two (SegalCondition.lean:422) and end_not_generated_by_simples (LiftPresentation.lean). It currently exists only as a scratch computation and prose in SlicePresentation.md, and it is an error I made and would otherwise make again.

Claim to land: Ch(box 2)[W-inv] is NOT equivalent to (PosBraidAction 2)-op. Both have two isomorphism classes of objects, but their endomorphism monoids differ - trivial versus PosPureBraid 2.

The two halves, both already worked out:

(a) Non-trivial End downstairs. endEquivPosPure (Machinery/Braid/PosAction.lean:43) is a MulEquiv End p to PosPureBraid n, so End IS the pure braids. sigma-1 squared is pure (posPermHom of it, by swap_mul_self) and non-trivial (posLen of it is 2, of 1 is 0). This half was already machine-checked in scratch by the agent that found the refutation.

(b) Trivial End upstairs, by enumeration. serialWedge_dimSum_eq forces dimSum d = 2; endo_eq_id gives one chart for [2]; onesTopEquiv 2 gives two for [1,1]; endo_eq_id empties Hom(r1,r2); nonempty_hom_iff empties Hom(t,r_i). That leaves r1 -> t <- r2 with W = {p1}. Nothing maps INTO r1 or r2, so inverting p1 adds only its inverse t -> r1 and creates no loop.

Optionally also record the sharper structural reason, which is cheap: Ch(box n)[W-inv] = the category of elements of a PosBraid n-set COMPATIBLY with the projection requires wedgeHoms (box n) to invert merges (FibrationLocalize's descent needs Pd with W.Q followed by Pd equal to P, which exists iff W.IsInvertedBy P). At n = 2 that map sends one element to two.

Home: a new module under Concurrency/, or alongside the existing negative results. Do not put it in Machinery/ - it is about the cube, not generic.

This does not depend on which direction C1 takes; it is true either way and prevents the error recurring.

Done when: sorry-free, lake build CubeChains green, debloat pass run.
close_reason: not_nonempty_equiv_posBraidAction and its op form in Concurrency/Merge/CubeCrossing.lean. Refuted by CONNECTIVITY, not by End: crossLen is a W-invariant (crossPerm lengths add, W is crossPerm = 1), so crossLoc forces empty hom-sets between different crossing lengths, while PosBraidAction 2 is connected. Cheaper and rigorous - the End route would have needed a Fintype enumeration of Ch (box 2) that does not exist. Module green (1608 jobs), axioms clean.

title: SlicePres A3b: a pseudo-cocone of localized slices induces a functor
description:
Split out of A4 (Cubical-0ws) at its eighth checkpoint. A3 gives an Equiv between functors out of W.Localization and STRICT cocones on the localized slices (OverCoconeLoc, with w a strict equality). That is the right statement and A4's hypothesis hP depends on it staying strict. But it cannot be satisfied by the comparison functor A4 needs.

Why, established by working all three escape routes: Psi's component at c must invert the presentation p (F c). Inverting an equivalence is a choice (Functor.inv is non-constructive), and a chosen inverse is not strictly compatible with anything. Independently, the polygraph-level identity (P.map f).functor followed by glueIncl x equals glueIncl (f* x) holds only up to the canonical eqToHom from gluePt_map, and Functor.ext cannot rescue it because a Presents gives an essentially surjective E, not a bijective-on-objects one.

Wanted, ALONGSIDE the existing strict statement, not replacing it: from a pseudo-cocone — components obj c, an iso overMapLoc W u followed by obj c iso obj c', and the overMapLoc_id / overMapLoc_comp coherences — produce a functor W.Localization to E restricting to it up to iso. This is W.Localization being the BIcolimit of its localized slices rather than the strict colimit.

Do the unlocalized case first as a feasibility check; it should be the same argument as A3's with isos threaded. Define G c := (obj c).obj (id c), and G u := iso followed by (obj c).map u; functoriality is exactly what the two coherences give. If the unlocalized version goes through cleanly the localized one should follow as A3's did.

Home: CubeChains/Machinery/Localization/SliceFamily.lean. Leave OverCoconeLoc and overCoconeLocEquiv untouched.

Both A4 and A5 need this — A5's GlueOn faces the identical obstruction, which is the argument for paying once here rather than twice bespoke.

The two coherences are exactly what functoriality needs, no extra hypothesis. title: SlicePres A3: a functor out of C[W-inv] is a compatible family on localized slices
description:
Read SlicePresentation.md first.
Wanted, for any category C, any `W : MorphismProperty C` containing identities, and any target E: a bijection between functors `C[W⁻¹] ⥤ E` and families `G c : (Over c)[W.over c ⁻¹] ⥤ E` satisfying `G c' = G c ∘ (Over.map u)[W⁻¹]` for every `u : c' ⟶ c`.
This is the heart of Phase A. Suggested order:
1. Do the unlocalized statement first: a functor `C ⥤ E` is the same as such a family on `Over c`. Forward is `G c := Over.forget c ⋙ G`; backward uses that `Over c` has terminal object `𝟙 c`, sending `c` to `(G c).obj (𝟙 c)` and `u : c' ⟶ c` to `(G c).map u` read as an arrow `u ⟶ 𝟙 c` in `Over c`.
2. Then check that inverting `W.over c` for every `c` is the same as inverting `W`. One direction: `w : a ⟶ b` in `W` is an arrow `(a,w) ⟶ (b, 𝟙 b)` of `Over b` lying in `W.over b`.
Reuse: `Localization.lift` (Predicate.lean:299), `Localization.natTrans_ext`, `Localization.liftNatIso` (:353), `StrictUniversalPropertyFixedTarget` (:75). Do not build a colimit cocone in Cat.

title: SlicePres B3: the slice over a shape is the chains of its wedge, and splits over a wedge
description:
Read SlicePresentation.md first.
Two statements:
1. `Ch(Z)/d ≅ Ch (⋁d.dims)`, on the nose. A morphism of `Ch Zbp` is a bare wedge map (`serialWedgeFullyFaithful`, Concurrency/Merge/MergeClass.lean:46) and an object of `Ch K` is a shape plus a classifying map (Precubical/Chains/Category.lean:23), so the two sides have literally the same objects and morphisms. This is the identification the whole of Phase C rests on.
2. `Ch (X ∨ Y) ≌ Ch X × Ch Y` as categories, upgrading what exists: `chConcat X Y : Ch X × Ch Y ⥤ Ch (X ∨ Y)` (Precubical/Segal/Segal.lean:512) is the functor, and `splitObj (h : (X ∨ Y).AdmitsAltitude) : Ch (X ∨ Y) ≃ Ch X × Ch Y` (Precubical/Segal/Split.lean:587) is an `Equiv` of object sets only, with `chConcat_obj_splitObj` :590 and `splitObj_chConcat_obj` :596. Also show that `W` on a wedge is the product of the `W`s on the factors.
Warning: `splitObj` carries `AdmitsAltitude`. Check whether the serial wedge satisfies it before assuming; `AdmitsAltitude` is a known landmine that `equivWedgeCat` carries silently. If it is a genuine hypothesis, say so and thread it rather than hiding it.
Arrows in `Ch Zbp` run finer to coarser (`nonempty_hom_iff`, Concurrency/Grading/ChartHom.lean:509), so a refinement of a concatenation respects the junction — that is why the splitting is true.

notes: AdmitsAltitude is NOT a blocker: BPSet.serialWedge_admitsAltitude (Precubical/Segal/SegalAltitude.lean:204) proves every serial wedge admits an altitude, and wedge2_admitsAltitude (:179) composes them. title: Presentation.localize: the unconditional presentation lift through the localization
description:
`⟨a | r⟩ presents Ch(Z)[W⁻¹]` ⟹ `⟨pullback a | pullback r⟩ presents Ch(K)[W⁻¹]`, for EVERY K — no Segal, no InvertsMerges. That statement is not in the tree; the tree reaches the localized presentation through descent (isLocalization_chDescent), which needs InvertsMerges for a different reason (the fibre, not the presentation).

The one missing input: **localizing a presented category at some of its generators is the same presentation with those generators formally inverted, plus the two inverse laws**. It is proved, in `CubeChains/Machinery/Localization/PresentedLocalization.lean` — but that module is orphaned (nothing imports it, `lake build CubeChains` never reaches it) and RED: `uniq_of_comp` fails at the bwd case of `Paths.ext_functor`, ~line 257.

Wanted:
- `Presentation.localize (p : Presentation C) (S : ∀ {a b}, p.Gen a b → Prop)` : a `Presentation` of the localization of C at the S-generators, plus its `IsLocalization`.
- `Presentation.elements` commutes with it: the S-generators of `p.elements F` are the lifts of p's, so `(p.localize S).elements F = (p.elements F).localize (lift S)`. Inputs are all present and unconditional: `merge_iff` (merges = codim-1 members of W), `W_eq_inverseImage_toChZ`, and unique lifting of words along the discrete fibration (`Presentation.exists_lift`).
- Instantiate: `Ch K[W⁻¹]` presented by the pullback cut presentation, for every K.
close_reason: Superseded: adjoining formal inverses makes the polygraph BIGGER, and the presentation of a localization has to get smaller. Presentation.localize is the wrong primitive; PresentedLocalization.lean is dead by decision, not just orphaned, and can be deleted. The route is Machinery/Presentation/Partial: the localized fibration is a PARTIAL discrete fibration, classified by a presheaf with an absorbing global section, and Presentation.elements + Presentation.restrict give the presentation with no inverses among the cells. See Cubical-r1x and the new bead for the Ch instance.

title: Garside height at 1ⁿ is non-vacuous, and W has no calculus of fractions
description:
The Garside height at `1ⁿ` must be shown non-vacuous, and the Ore condition
must be shown to fail. Both were proved before, in `LocMonoid` language, in
files now deleted. Wanted, restated at the single vertex `1ⁿ`:

1. A length homomorphism on `Ch(Z)[W⁻¹]` at `1ⁿ`, and: every word of atoms
   whose product is the class of `f` has exactly `permLen (crossPerm f)`
   letters. (Was `length_eq_permLen_crossPermN` + `exists_atomWord`, via
   `locLen`.)

2. `atomLoop i ≫ atomLoop i` is not the class of any single refinement.
   (Was `locOf_ne_atomLoc_sq`.) The height-2 witness.

3. `W Zbp f ↔ permLen (crossPerm f) = 0` — already in the tree as
   `W_iff_crossPerm_eq_one` with `eq_one_of_permLen_eq_zero`. Nothing wanted;
   recorded so it is not re-proved.

4. `W Zbp` has no calculus of fractions: not every morphism of the
   localization is one zag.

Established, and not to be re-derived:

- The bound for (4) is non-circular and survives the deletion. `conj_congr`
  says a one-zag loop at `1ⁿ` is determined by the crossing permutation of its
  refinement, so there are at most `n!` of them.
- The infiniteness half of (4), as first argued, went through
  `endEquivPosBraid` (`End ≅ PosBraid n`, then `posWrithe`). That declaration
  is deleted, so that argument is now circular and must not be used.
- The repair needs no `PosBraid`: iterate (2). `atomLoop i ^ k` has crossing
  permutation `adjT i ^ k` and length `k`, so the powers are pairwise distinct
  and `End` at `1ⁿ` is infinite by an additive length function alone. A finite
  set of size `n!` cannot exhaust it, giving (4).

Surviving inputs: `conj` and its laws (`conj_comp`, `conj_congr`, `conj_leg`,
`conj_eq_of_crossPerm`, `conj_comp_W`, `conj_W_comp`, `conj_eq_id`),
`atomLoop`, `atomLoop_comm`, `atomLoop_braid`, `Cut.exists_eq_atom`,
`exists_pairCell`, `exists_leg`, `exists_merge_leg`, `atom_pair_eq`,
`runMerge` with `existsUnique_W_ones`/`eq_runMerge`, `crossPerm_comp`,
`permLen_crossPerm_comp`, `permLen_adjT`, `adjT_mul_self`,
`hom_ext_of_crossPerm`, `eq_of_W`.

title: The atom of Ch Zbp is the wall crossing of Ch (Hbp cube n)

title: UniqueComposites is a cell-level condition on K
description:
InvertsMerges K is equivalent to UniqueComposites K (Chains/LiftPresentation): one condition per cut position (l, r, p, q). What is wanted is the reduction to a condition on the cells of K alone, independent of the position: for all p q, the map from K.cells (p+q) to the composable pairs (x : cells p, y : cells q) with vertex1 x = vertex0 y, given by the two cubeMerge faces, is a bijection. Equivalently, restriction along the tensorator identity-w-identity is bijective on maps into K as soon as its middle w is.

## Context
The obstruction is that the cube list of splicePhi composed with m is not computed anywhere: WedgeMap has wedgeToCubes_comp only for POST-composition with a map of K. The equivalence CubeChain K = (dims, wedge map) (Correspondence.equivWedgeHom) is unconditional and is the natural frame.
acceptance_criteria: A theorem 'uniqueComposites_of_cells : (cell-level condition) -> UniqueComposites K', and ideally the converse.
close_reason: Chains/SegalCondition.lean. IsSegal K := for all p q, Bijective (wedgeTensorComparison K (box p) (box q)); isSegal_iff_existsUnique gives the cell form (composable cells have a unique composite via frontFace/backFace), faceComparison names the cell-level map. invertsMerges_of_isSegal is the wanted direction; isLocal_cubeMerge_iff_invertsMerges_repoint is the converse, an exact iff on positive blocks: (forall p q : PNat, IsLocal K.toPsh (cubeMerge p q)) iff (forall u v, InvertsMerges (K.repoint u v)). The splicePhi cube-list obstruction named in the description is sidestepped: a merge is 1 or cubeMerge or 1 up to iso (CutData), and IsLocal is closed under whiskering (wedge2Desc + wedge2_hom_ext) and under iso, so no bead computation is needed.

title: wedgeHoms (Hbp □ⁿ) inverts the bead merges
description:
Wanted: InvertsMerges (Hbp.obj (□n)), i.e. ((Winf Zbp).op).IsInvertedBy (wedgeHoms (Hbp.obj (□n))) — a bead merge acts bijectively on (⋁d ⟶ Hbp (□ⁿ)).

With it, ChainCat.isLocalization_chDescent (Chains/ElementsFibration.lean) makes Ch (Hbp □ⁿ) localized at Winf the category of elements of a presheaf on the localized serial wedges — the action category of PosBraid n on the runs, whose loops are the stabilizers. It is the hypothesis behind PermFibre / localizationEquivPosBraidAction (Salvetti/HPosAction.lean).

True at n = 2: the fibre over [2] is Perm(Fin 2) x {top cell} (2 elements), the fibre over [1,1] is the 2 runs, and the merge matches them; for the undecorated □² the same merge is a map from a 1-element set to a 2-element set. Fibre count in general: n! on both sides.

Reduction that looks cheapest: via chSymChStarEquiv and execEquiv, the fibre over d is {(C,w) : Ch (□n) x Perm (Fin n) // C.dims = d, chFace C ⊑ chFace (wordChain w)}, and (C,w) ↦ w is a bijection onto Perm (Fin n) for each d with dimSum d = n; merges have permOf = 1 so they preserve w.
notes:
Reduction lemma is in place: ChainCat.invertsMerges_of_merge (Chains/ElementsFibration.lean) — only single merges need checking. The contrast is proved: CubeChains.not_invertsMerges_cube_two : ¬ InvertsMerges (□2) (Salvetti/RunClassifier.lean), so the undecorated cube provably fails and H is doing real work. What remains is the positive statement for Hbp (□n).
The run factor alone provably FAILS: not_invertsMerges_runBp and not_invertsMerges_Hbp_Zbp (Salvetti/RunClassifier.lean) — the merge [1,1] -> [2] takes Hom(wedge[2], runBp) = Perm(Fin 2) (2 elements) to Hom(wedge[1,1], runBp) (1 element). So the hypothesis is NOT inherited from Hbp; the cube labelling has to compensate. Sharpened form: isEmpty_splitting_of_invertsMerges_cube_two — InvertsMerges (Hbp (box 2)) is equivalent to saying wedgeHoms (Hbp (box 2)) admits NO natural product splitting into wedgeHoms (box 2) x wedgeHoms runBp. The desym bijection of ChStarSym is provably not such a splitting (not_desym_natural).
Contrast now proved (Salvetti/RunClassifier.lean): Hbp Zbp has ONE all-edges chain per degree, so costarOnesH : Costar (WinfHn n) (onesObjH n) exists and Ch (Hbp Zbp)[W^-1] collapses degreewise to a single object (nonempty_locIso). The cube does not: runHbpCubeEquivPerm : Run (Hbp (box n)) = Perm (Fin n), n! rigid all-edges chains, so isEmpty_costar_cube — no costar for n >= 2. So the n! objects come from the cube, not from H.
close_reason: invertsMerges_Hbp_cube (Salvetti/HSegal.lean): InvertsMerges (Hbp (box n)) for every n, unconditionally. Route: not the product/twist reduction the description proposed, but IsSegal — K inverts wedgeToTensor at every pair of cubes — plus sbox_existsUnique: an SBox map is a coord : Fin n -> Bool + Fin m, so a symmetric cube map out of box(p+q) is a composable pair, i.e. sq(p+q) IS the wedge sq(p) or sq(q). Through symFreeCube/HCube that is isSegal_H_cube, and invertsMerges_of_isSegal transports it. #print axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound only.

title: The W k filtration does not yet control skeletal dependence
description:
GOAL (open): an invariant in the spirit of the braid functor that depends on the n-skeleton, for n = 4 and beyond. The braid functor itself depends only on the 3-skeleton: codim-1 generators use 2-cells, codim-2 relations use 3-cells, and a monoid presentation has no room for codim-3 data.

Two dead ends recorded so the next attempt does not repeat them:

1. The mergeLe / W k filtration (deleted). Filtering the morphism class alone bounds nothing, because the basepoint [n] of the localization uses the top cell however the class is filtered.

2. Also restricting the OBJECTS to chains with beads of dimension at most k (proposed, rejected by the user, never implemented). The resulting tower stabilises only at k = n, which contradicts the presentation argument that 3 suffices -- so bead dimension is not the right cut.

Note also that going up in coherence does not help: factorisations of a codim-j morphism are the subsets of its j cuts, so the factorisation complex is the permutohedron, which is contractible. There is no extra information above codim 2 in that direction.
notes: mergeLe / W k and their API are removed from Chains/MergeClass.lean (user decision, superseding 'do not delete'). MergeClass now carries only merge, Winf, the inverseImage transport, and the properness section. Anyone resuming this goal starts from merge/Winf and rebuilds the filtration.

title: The degree-dropping label is a shuffle: the target for it
description: Wanted: the label of a degree-dropping move, given that it is neither a braid nor a planar operadic structure map. Machine-checked in Testing/DropSplit: drop_label_not_function_of_words gives two degree-dropping moves out of the one-bead chain of the 3-cube with the same base word, the same new-base word (widths (2,1)) and no pair of coordinates reordered (each target refines its source), landing on different chains. So no assignment factoring through words-plus-a-braid is well defined. shuffle_check: 22 of the 42 degree-dropping moves of the 3-cube split a bead whose lower part is not an initial segment, so braidOperad's planar substitution cannot express them either without inserting a crossing that the geometry does not have. The datum is the subset of the bead's coordinates forming the lower cable.
notes:
The order and partition inputs are available: Chains/BeadFibre gives Move.part_lt_iff (parts ordered by (side, source bead)), Move.part_eq_iff (a part IS a side) and Move.parts_of_straddles (exactly two parts at a codim-1 cut). What is still missing is only the datum itself -- the subset of the split bead's coordinates forming the lower cable.
Landed. Datum: ECh.Move.lowerCable (Chains/BeadFibre) -- the Finset of a bead's coordinates going to the j0 side, characterised by mem_lowerCable_iff and proper+nonempty exactly when the bead straddles; as an ordered datum it is (m.lowerCable t).orderEmbOfFin. Structure: Salvetti/MoveFace, ECh.Move.chFace_tgt -- chFace(target) = chFace(newBase) (+) chFace(source), the covector composition SignVec.comp, i.e. the Tits product of the braid face monoid; labels compose by (+) (Move.chFace_comp), a LEFT REGULAR BAND (comp_self, comp_assoc, comp_comp_self now in Arrangements/COM), not a group. Negative, machine-checked: Move.part_interleave -- when two beads straddle, one bead's parts are NOT consecutive in the target, so no operadic substitution (planar or braided) can be the move; Testing/DropSplit's straddle_count_check shows no move of the 3-cube has two straddling beads, which is why the cube-3 censuses look operad-compatible.
close_reason:
Answered at 7c55ef6, and it is a reframing rather than a fill-in.

THE LABEL: Move.chFace_tgt -- (chFace c').1 = (chFace m.z'.base).1 (Tits product) (chFace c).1. A move acts as its NEW BASE read as a FACE, by the covector composition already in Arrangements/COM.lean. The bridge is braidSign_lex: reading v first and breaking its ties by w IS braidSign v (Tits) braidSign w, applied to BeadFibre's lexicographic law.

COMPOSITION: Move.chFace_comp -- labels compose by the Tits product. With the band laws now in COM.lean (comp_self, comp_assoc, comp_comp_self: X Y X = X Y), the labels form a LEFT REGULAR BAND, not a group. The Coxeter-complex dictionary lands on the FACE MONOID, not on parabolic cosets.

WHY NO OPERAD, as a theorem rather than a witness: Move.part_interleave -- if beads t < s both straddle, then part t k0 < part s k < part t k1, so one bead's parts are NOT consecutive in the target. Any operadic substitution, planar or braided, keeps a slot's outputs consecutive by construction. The Tits product can do it because the new base decides BEFORE the source.

METHODOLOGICAL WARNING: straddle_count_check -- NO move of cube 3 has two straddling beads (two would need two coordinates each, and the cube has three). So every cube-3 census looks operad-compatible; the computable model cannot witness this obstruction at all.

CONSISTENCY: the degree-preserving case is the shadow -- where the Tits product does not refine it merely permutes blocks, and the positive lift of that block permutation is crossCable q p. So Move.read_crossCable is a sub-case, not a competing answer.

DATUM: Move.lowerCable m t : Finset (Fin w), choice-free as the fibre of Move.part over its minimum; mem_lowerCable_iff identifies it with the j0 side for a straddling bead; lowerCable_nonempty_ne_univ makes it a genuine shuffle.

SCOPE, stated plainly: the coordinate-level results (beadIdx_restrict_*, part_*, lowerCable, part_interleave) hold for general K. The covector packaging chFace_tgt is cube-only, because braidCOM and chFace are. Generalising needs a face monoid attached to K itself; the coordinate-level lex law is that statement without the packaging.

The mirrored reading is false, not untransported.

title: Braid operad: associativity and braid equivariance of braidSubst
description:
`CubeChains/Operad/` has the definition (`BraidedOperad`), the cabling cocycle (`cable`, `cable_mul`), the k-ary juxtaposition (`braidProd`), the substitution `braidSubst w hw x y = braidProd w hw y * cable ⟨w,hw⟩ x`, and both unit laws.

Wanted: `braidSubst` is associative and braid-equivariant, and a `BraidedOperad` instance carrying it.

The carrier cannot be `n ↦ SingleObj (Braid n)`: cabling is not a homomorphism (`cablePerm_mul` has `u ∘ σ` in the middle slot, not `u`), and `SingleObj (Braid n)` admits no free `Bₙ`-action (endofunctors of `SingleObj G` are monoid endomorphisms of `G`). `SingleObj (PureBraid n)` with `Bₙ` acting by conjugation, or the discrete category on `Braid n` with right translation, both do.
notes:
ALSO NEEDED for the SingleObj (PureBraid n) carrier, and currently missing: the k-ary analogues of what Braid/Sum already has for the binary case -- permHom_braidProd and braidProd_pure (a juxtaposition of pure braids is pure). Braid/Sum.lean has permHom_braidSum and braidSum_pure; Braid/Blocks.lean has braidProd but neither. Without them the instance cannot land in pure braids.
ORIENTATION CORRECTION to Operad/Basic. comp_assoc currently takes the double-indexed family primary and derives the flat one, on the grounds that this is definitional. For blk it is the other way round: blk maps INTO the flat ordinal with slots read off it, so the FLAT widths are the definitional orientation, and the bridge flatWidth w hw v (blk w hw i a) = v i a is only propositional -- it goes through symm of a trans of equivs, which is not rfl. Restating comp_assoc with the flat widths primary would make it cast-free; leaving it as is makes the instance pay a transport at exactly that seam. Change it BEFORE building the instance, while nothing depends on it. Progress: (C) regrouping is proved as braidProd_assoc in Braid/BlockAssoc. (A) cable of a cable needs one transport, since subWidth of a permuted width family agrees only propositionally. (B) cable of a juxtaposition is reachable for the pure carrier specifically, since cable is multiplicative on pure braids so both sides become homomorphisms in y and MonoidHom.pi_ext applies. (D) sliding should be stated in BLOCK form, which is transport-free because composition with a permutation is definitional on the index.
close_reason: braidOperad : BraidedOperad lands at d29d691. Associativity is cable_cable (cabling twice is cabling along the slot totals), equivariance is braidSubst_conj from the sliding identity cable_mul_braidProd, and both unit laws are discharged. Purity is needed of the slots only, never of the operation or the blocks. Verified non-degenerate by rfl: arity n IS SingleObj (PureBraid n), comp on morphisms IS braidSubst, and braidSubst IS braidProd * cable.

comments.author: zstone
comments.text:
The hom route is refuted, and the reason is structural: a semidirect product absorbs a shift in the BASE, never in the FIBER. The block braid lives in Braid (u i), a fiber indexed by the thing being shifted, so the inverse case moves a group element across a propositional type equality however the identity is phrased. Checked and rejected: the normalizer phrasing (subgroup-equality loses which block goes where, and comp's functoriality needs the pointwise form) and the bundled-Widths phrasing (braidBlock still reads u'.1 i).

mathlib has no MulEquiv.piCongrLeft (only Equiv/Homeomorph/MeasurableEquiv/LinearEquiv/IsometryEquiv) and no composition lemma for Equiv.piCongrLeft, whose apply lemma states the transport explicitly. So the hom route relocates the transport into machinery that would have to be built first.

The transport is therefore load-bearing, and braidBlock_congr / braidBlock_congr_idx (ff0a26c) are its devices. Remaining: inv_mem', then one_mem'/mul_mem' (routine via sigma-as-parameter-with-equation), then BraidedOperadStruct.

comments.author: zstone
comments.text:
CORRECTION to my earlier comment: the fiber transport is NOT unavoidable, and the claim that it was is refuted by 16e3a90.

The earlier finding was right that the transport cannot be removed by algebraic repackaging (semidirect product, normalizer, bundled Widths) -- but wrong to conclude it is intrinsic. The cure was a change of INDEXING DIRECTION, not of packaging: state the identity for a whole slot family y : forall i, Braid (u i) PRECOMPOSED by the covered permutation s, rather than one block postcomposed by s-inverse. Then y (s j) : Braid (u (s j)) is Braid ((u . s) j) on the nose. mul_mem' becomes transport-free, and inv_mem' costs exactly one WIDTH transport ((u . s-inverse) . s = u) at family level; the index transport s (s-inverse i) = i never appears.

braidBlock_congr and braidBlock_congr_idx (ff0a26c) were built for the abandoned route and are deleted.

slidesPast : Subgroup (Braid k) is complete, all three obligations. cable_mul_braidProd holds for every braid, not just ofPerm. braidOperadStruct lands, carrier SingleObj (PureBraid n) with B_n acting by MulAut.conjNormal. Remaining: comp_assoc, comp_equivariance, the full BraidedOperad.

title: The labelling functor: braidings and cablings, not permutations
description: permOf labels a degree-0 morphism by a permutation. The generalization is the Coxeter-complex dictionary: a chain with beads of dimension d1..dk determines a parabolic S_d1 x ... x S_dk, a degree-0 chain is a chamber and a degree-d chain a face, so the label of a degree-d morphism lives in a parabolic coset. Testing/Parabolic.lean already proves the degree-0 shadow (outLabels_eq_parabolic: the crossing permutations out of an execution are exactly the parabolic of its bead dimensions). Results wanted: the label of a move as the longest element w0 of the window's parabolic; length additivity, generalizing permOf_noDoubleCross -- this should BE revSerialWedge_append, since w0(xy) = w0(y)w0(x) is exactly lengths adding for disjoint windows; and the labelling functor on C(K), generalizing ConcPos = proj followed by braidFunctor. Reversal.lean already has the generic w0 calculus and is currently the least used file in the cluster.
notes:
AMENDED. Parabolic cosets describe the OBJECTS (a chain with beads d1..dk is a face, i.e. a coset of S_d1 x ... x S_dk) but they are the wrong target for the MORPHISM labels. Read a bead of dimension d as a cable of d strands. Then a codimension-one move comes in two flavours and only one of them is a braid: a degree-PRESERVING move swaps two adjacent cables, which as a permutation is the block transposition of length p*q and as a braid is its positive lift, the cable crossing with p*q crossings (degree 0 is p=q=1, giving sigma_i); a degree-DROPPING move splits a cable, which is not a braid at all but an operadic structure map. Witness that no braid word can do the job: in the square, [b0] with trivial subdivision has one cable of width 2, and the two moves to the two runs have the same window pieces (1,1) and differ only in which splitting -- nothing is crossed. So the target is a braided operad, not a group: morphisms generated by braidings and cablings, with the braid group the sub-structure visible when every cable has width 1. This is Cubical-zmi.13 reached from the other side. It also explains why braids sufficed at degree 0: degree 0 is closed under moves, since restriction never raises a bead's dimension, so from a run only degree-preserving moves occur and the cabling half is invisible. Naturality is Matsumoto's: the positive lift is canonical as a group element, not as a word. serialCompl at a 2-window IS the block transposition and revSerialWedge_append is the cabling calculus.
CORRECTION to the reading of the cube-3 split. The generators DO split cleanly: every move is either degree-preserving (a cable swap) or degree-dropping (a cabling), 42 and 42 in C(cube 3), a clean binary. Only the RELATIONS mix, 24 of 78, equating a path that uses a degree-preserving cable swap with one that does not. That is not a failure of the split, it is the equivariance between cabling and braiding -- the compatibility axioms that make a braided operad rather than a product of two independent structures. Expect morphisms to be GENERATED by strictly-cabling and strictly-braiding generators, not to be individually of one kind; a general morphism is a composite of both. So the labelling target needs the mixed relations as structure, not as an obstruction.
Labelling functor landed for the cube: Salvetti/LabelFunctor's chFaceFunctor : C (box n) -> FaceRef, chain to its face of the braid arrangement, morphism to the refinement it performs, assembled by ECh.Collapse.desc (relations discharged by the existing machinery). Generalises ConcPos with the face monoid in place of braidFunctor. NEGATIVE, and it is structural not a weakening: the band ELEMENT is not a functor invariant of a morphism of C K, only its action is. Collapse demands map on all of EChStar with map_id and map_W; a W-arrow leaves the attached chain fixed but carries label chFace z'.base, which is nonzero, and Localize's stepP erases it to 0. So on a codim-2 window with a W-step in one factorisation and none in the other the two band elements differ (chFace (middle base) vs chFace (z'.base)), while chFace is injective by chFaceEquiv. Hence FaceRef must be thin. Not machine-checked with a witness -- see Cubical-4g0's warning that the box-3 model can be blind to obstructions of this shape.

comments.author: zstone
comments.text:
The braid-side targets now exist, so this bead is gated only on the cube side.

Available: braidOperad : BraidedOperad (d29d691) -- the degree-DROPPING move's target, an operadic structure map. crossCable p q (179641c) -- the degree-PRESERVING move's target, with permLen = p*q, crossCable 1 1 = the Artin generator, naturality, the hexagon, and cable_crossCable.

The amended reading is confirmed on the braid side: crossCable IS sigma_1 cabled along (p,q), so the degree-0 case (p=q=1) is literally the old generator and nothing about the old labelling needs revisiting.

One orientation correction for whoever writes the functor: the bundles read (p,q) BELOW the crossing and (q,p) ABOVE, so a juxtaposition on top of crossCable p q must be read on (q,p). The mirrored form is FALSE, machine-checked at p=1,q=2, not merely untransported.

comments.author: zstone
comments.text:
CORRECTION to the amended note, machine-checked at dc58f3e.

'A degree-preserving move swaps two adjacent cables' is FALSE. counterMove : ECh.Move (cube 3) (chOf 4) (chOf 10) is degree-preserving (both endpoints are runs) and is not a swap of adjacent cables: the runs 0,1,2 and 2,0,1 differ by a three-cycle. Not an edge case -- ell_counts already records that of the 36 degree-preserving moves out of a run in cube 3, TWELVE cross two walls, and an adjacent-cable swap crosses exactly one. The square cannot separate the claim from the truth, since its base cable contains only one bead of the subdivision.

What holds instead. The BASE half is exactly as claimed and is proved: Move.base_split (a codim-1 move splits exactly one bead of its base, l ++ (p+q) :: r to l ++ p :: q :: r) and Move.base_split_unique (position and both widths determined). The ATTACHED half is governed by attach_liftObj_comp: the target's bead order is the lexicographic refinement of the new base's order by the old attached order. So the beads of the attached chain lying in the split base bead are 2-coloured by which new cable their strands fall into, and the new chain lists all p-side pieces first, then all q-side.

The true dichotomy: degree-preserving iff NO bead of the attached chain straddles the split, and the move is then the (p,q)-UNSHUFFLE of the strands in that base bead -- which is the cable crossing of widths p and q. The two cables are adjacent IN THE BASE; their strands are in general interleaved in the attached chain. Degree-dropping iff at least one bead straddles, and MORE THAN ONE cable can split (so 'splits one cable' is also false; the witness needs n >= 4 -- base [4], beads {0,1},{2,3}, split P={0,2}, degree 2 to 0 -- and is NOT machine-checked, the repo having no computable model above cube 3).

crossCable remains the right target: p and q are the base-split widths. It is the word 'adjacent', and the identification of the crossed cables with BEADS of the attached chain, that fail.

comments.author: zstone
comments.text:
REFUTED, elementarily: 'restricting a chain along a face never decreases the bead count' is false. The run of the square has two beads; restrict to either coordinate edge, and any chain of the 1-cube has exactly one bead (dimSum is 1 and beads are positive). Two down to one. Restriction to a proper face discards every bead missing the face; dims_one_restrict constrains the DIMENSIONS of survivors, not how many survive.

Bead count is not monotone for a single restriction. It is monotone for the FAMILY: attach (liftObj z w) is the COMMON REFINEMENT of w's partition and attach z's, and a common refinement has at least as many blocks, since every bead is nonempty and so meets at least one block of the other partition.

Also refuted, and it kills the obvious shortcut: there is in general NO morphism attach z' --> attach z, so dims_length_le_of_hom cannot supply this. counterMove witnesses it -- run(0,1,2) and run(2,0,1) refine each other in neither direction. The common refinement refines the PARTITION, not the ORDER.

Reduced at HEAD: degree monotonicity along a move is now exactly a bead-count statement (Move.degree_le_iff, degree_attach_le_iff), with the dimSum bookkeeping discharged. What remains is (attach z).dims.length <= (attach (liftObj z w)).dims.length for general K -- the general-K analogue of attach_liftObj_comp.

comments.author: zstone
comments.text:
REFUTED again, at 17c80c3: the label is not a function of the cut. counterMove and counterMove' cut the same base word [3] into the same refined word [1,2] -- identical BeadCut, p=1, q=2 -- and have different targets, so no assignment reading only the widths labels both. counterMove crosses 2 = p*q walls; counterMove' crosses 1. Since permLen (permCross p q) = p*q, the second's label is not crossCable 1 2.

Cause: the two cables are adjacent in the BASE, so the beads of the attached chain over the split bead INTERLEAVE, and the move un-interleaves them. The label is the unshuffle braid of that interleaving, which sees more than the widths.

The missing hypothesis is Move.IsAtom -- an atom leaves exactly two beads over the split bead, so there is nothing to interleave. Census over cube 3: 84 moves, 42 degree-preserving, 18 of those atoms, 12 degree-preserving moves crossing a number of walls other than p*q. So the atom hypothesis is neither vacuous nor cosmetic.

ORIENTATION, machine-checked over all 18 atoms and with a p != q witness: a degree-preserving atom carries its two cables (q,p) in the SOURCE word and (p,q) in the TARGET, where p = width j0 and q = width j1. crossCable P Q has bundles (P,Q) below and (Q,P) above. So the label of a degree-preserving atom is crossCable q p -- the BeadCut widths passed j1 FIRST, which is the opposite order to BeadCut.unshuffle (that reads the split bead's coordinates, not the source word). The mirrored reading is FALSE (atom_swap_mirror_fails), an orientation fact rather than a transport.

Remaining cube-side input: the bead bijection a degree-preserving move induces, plus which of j0/j1 each source bead lands in. Move.degree_eq_iff_beadCut gives only the predicate 'no bead meets both', not the bijection.

comments.author: zstone
comments.text:
CORRECTION to the amended note's second half, machine-checked at 600edb7. 'A degree-dropping move splits a cable, which is not a braid at all but an OPERADIC STRUCTURE MAP' -- the first clause holds, the second does not.

drop_label_not_function_of_words: two degree-dropping moves out of the one-bead chain of cube 3 share a base word AND a new-base word (widths (2,1), so the same BeadCut), each has a target refining its source so nothing is reordered and ell = 0 for both, and they land on DIFFERENT chains. No braid separates them, since any braid label of either is the identity. And braidOperad's substitution is planar by construction (Operad/Basic: no S_k action anywhere), so it sees only the widths, which agree. Expressing an interleaved split as braid-then-planar-cabling inserts exactly the crossing the geometry does not have.

What a degree-dropping move actually is: for each straddling bead, the SUBSET of its coordinates forming the lower cable -- an (a,b)-SHUFFLE. 22 of the 42 degree-dropping moves of cube 3 split a bead whose lower part is not an initial segment of it; witness [3] cut into {0,2}|{1}. Filed as Cubical-4g0.

So the target structure needs shuffles as well as braidings and cablings; a planar braided operad is not enough.

The degree-preserving half is DONE and unaffected: Move.read_crossCable (89c4f67), an atom's label is crossCable q p, resting on Move.coordMap_side -- an atom moves no coordinate within a bead, so the move IS its bead map.

title: C is a functor BPSet to Cat
description: C(K) is only an invariant of K if K |-> C(K) is functorial. ECh* should be nearly free: pushforward along psi : K --> L preserves dimension lists, so the wedge is unchanged and the subdivision carries over verbatim, (a,x) |-> (psi a, x). W should be preserved since attachHom pushes forward. The Ch-level machinery exists (ChainCat.pushforward, codim_pushforward, generated_pushforward, SiteCut.pushforward). THE SUBTLETY, and it is the actual content: pushforward can collapse a move into a W-arrow, since distinct chains c /= c' in K can have equal images in L. So C is NOT free-functorial on generators -- the induced map must be defined through the quotient and the relations shown to survive. Without this, the family End(C(K), c) is a construction and not an invariant.
notes:
PRIORITY NOTE: this is semantics, not hygiene. Reducing a semaphore count means deleting cells of dimension >= 2, which removes fillers, hence merges, hence moves -- at the extreme, delete every 2-cell and C(K) is discrete, every interleaving distinguishable, no concurrency (the Swiss flag: delete the middle 2-cell of a square and the two runs stop being equivalent). The right formulation is naturality: an inclusion K' -> K induces C(K') -> C(K), and the invariant of the semaphore constraint is the FAILURE of that functor to be full or faithful. So functoriality is what makes concurrency constraints expressible, not just what makes C(K) well defined.
MUCH CHEAPER ROUTE, and it retires the objection in the note above. Do NOT define C(psi) on generators and check the relations survive. Use the universal property: for psi : K -> L, the composite ECh*(K) -> ECh*(L) -> C(L) inverts W(K) provided pushforward carries W(K) into W(L), and loc_isLocalization then gives the factorization through loc_K, i.e. C(psi). Generators and relations are never touched. Two inputs, both cheap-looking: ECh* functorial in K (pushforward preserves dimension lists, so the wedge is unchanged and the subdivision carries over verbatim, (a,x) |-> (psi a, x)); and W preserved (W says attachHom z' followed by F's base arrow is attachHom z, and pushforward commutes with attachHom). The collapse worry recorded earlier -- that pushforward can turn a move into a W-arrow -- is NOT an obstruction on this route: the induced functor simply sends such a generator to an identity, automatically. CAVEAT to check rather than assume: Localization.lift gives loc followed by lift ISO to G, not equal, so composing lifts makes C a pseudofunctor a priori. It may strictify, since loc is z |-> attach z and attach z = (pushforward z.base.map).obj z.sub, so attach of a pushforward is plausibly definitionally the pushforward of attach. Establish that, since an invariant reads better as a functor than as a pseudofunctor and the difference is whether the comparison isos are identities.
LANDED (Chains/Functorial.lean, sorry-free, axiom-clean, unconditional in K and L). IT STRICTIFIES — C is an honest BPSet ⥤ Cat (ECh.cFunctor), not a pseudofunctor.

The caveat on the cheaper route is answered in the affirmative, and the reason is that the comparison isos are identities ON THE NOSE, not merely provably identity: with ECh.pushforward psi z := (op (ChainCat.pushforward psi z.base), z.2) — dimension lists do not move, so LinesAll's fibre is literally the same type — all of the following are rfl (machine-checked as bare examples): attach of a pushforward = pushforward of attach; attachHom likewise; pushforward (id) = id and pushforward (psi >> chi) = pushforward psi >> pushforward chi; pushforward of trivSub = trivSub of pushforward; and the Elements-morphism condition is literally F.2.

What does NOT strictify is Localization.lift, and also my own liftF from Chains/Localize: both land on trivSub c and conjugate by the etas, and attach (trivSub a) = a is NOT rfl (it needs Equiv.apply_symm_apply on chainPshEquiv), so their object map is only isomorphic to the one wanted. The fix is a new abstraction rather than a transport: ECh.Collapse K E — the data of obj : Ch K -> E, map on ECh* morphisms read between the ATTACHED chains, functoriality, and map_W (a W-arrow goes to an eqToHom). A Collapse descends to C K strictly (Collapse.desc, obj X := Phi.obj X.as.as) with Collapse.desc_loc recovering it. cmap psi is the descent of ECh.pushforward psi >> loc L; the collapse worry is discharged exactly as predicted, by map_W: a move whose image lies in W L goes to an identity.

Statements: W_pushforward; Collapse.desc / desc_loc; funext_loc (functors out of C K agreeing on objects and on loc's image are equal — the moves generate); cmap; cmap_obj (rfl); cmap_loc; cmap_id : cmap (id K) = id functor; cmap_comp : cmap (psi >> chi) = cmap psi >> cmap chi; loc_naturality : loc K >> cmap psi = pushforward psi >> loc L (an EQUALITY); cFunctor : BPSet ⥤ Cat.

Note for whoever generalises: liftF (Chains/Localize) is now the non-strict special case of Collapse.desc — conj Phi hPhi is itself a Collapse (conj_id, conj_comp, conj_of_W are exactly the three fields), so liftF could be re-derived as (that Collapse).desc and the duplicated relation-check in liftPaths_relPath would go. Left alone to keep the audited file untouched.

GOTCHA (third instance of the instances-transparency landmine, worth the context): in a composite, the SECOND factor's hidden object arguments are taken from the FIRST factor's target, so writing G.map ((loc K).map F) inside a composite whose left factor is an eqToHom into chObj (attach z) silently spells the object chObj (attach z) instead of (loc K).obj z, and rw with a hypothesis in the other spelling fails on a goal that PRINTS as a match. Cure used: a type ascription on the middle factor, (T.map ((loc K).map e.F) : T.obj ((loc K).obj e.z) ⟶ _), which pins the spelling at elaboration.
close_reason: cFunctor : BPSet -> Cat, with cmap_id and cmap_comp as equalities. Strict, because pushforward keeps the dimension list so the subdivision is literally the same type. Localization.lift does not strictify; the fix is the Collapse abstraction, which descends on the nose. Chains/Functorial.lean, axiom-clean.

title: Is Ch(cube n) thin without side conditions?
description: Ch K's morphisms are all monic unconditionally (ChainCat.mono, via wedgeMap_cancel: the coordinate map pins the target bead and Box rigidity the face). That cancels wedge-to-wedge maps. A coordFlip-based analogue for v : wedge b --> cube m would very likely give thinness of Ch (cube n) with NO side condition, replacing the current route through chainCat_hom_subsingleton, which takes NonSelfLinked and AdmitsAltitude. If it works it deletes that plumbing at three sites: Salvetti/Elements, Salvetti/ExecData, Salvetti/ChainBraidFace, each of which currently passes cube_nonSelfLinked and cube_admitsAltitude by hand. Note this does NOT extend to Correspondence's descent_mono, which cancels the descent map into an arbitrary K and where the side conditions are load-bearing -- the two-squares counterexample is at Correspondence.lean:104-117.
close_reason: Not a question. Ch(cube n) IS thin and already proved -- cube_chainCat_isThin in Salvetti/Elements.lean, since cubes are non-self-linked and admit altitude. The bead described a cosmetic tidy (three Salvetti sites pass cube_nonSelfLinked and cube_admitsAltitude by hand rather than using the instance) dressed up as a theorem. Not worth tracking.

title: ECh*(K) as a quotient of a path category on its own codim-1 generators
description:
Chains/Complexify has the presentation of Ch(K) pulled back along the category of elements (presentation K : elements of LinesAll over Quotient (codimTwoRel K), equivalent to ECh*(K)), plus generation in codimension one and the codimension-two factorisations upstairs. What is missing is the path-category form: Quotient (eRel) equivalent to ECh*(K), where the quiver is the codimension-one morphisms of ECh*(K) and eRel the two-step paths of its codimension-two factorisations.

Fullness is ECh.generated. Faithfulness is the only content: a congruence downstairs must be lifted, i.e. unique path lifting along the discrete opfibration plus transport of EqvGen (CompClosure codimTwoRel). Two general statements would give it and are the reusable form: (1) elements of a presheaf over Paths Q is Paths of the quiver of elements; (2) elements over Quotient r is the quotient by the lifted relation.
notes:
LANDED. Chains/EPresentation.lean: ECh.presentation K : Quotient (ECh.codimTwoRel K) ≌ ECh* K, identity on objects, unconditional in K. Full = ECh.generated; faithful = ECh.quot_eq_of_eval_eq.

Route taken, and why NOT the two general Elements lemmas: elements of LinesAll K sit over (Ch K)^op, so 'elements over Paths Q is Paths of the elements quiver' needs (Paths Q)^op vs Paths (Q^op) and 'elements over Quotient r' needs (Quotient r)^op vs Quotient (r^op). Neither op transport is in mathlib and both are ~40 lines of Path/Quotient bureaucracy. The upstairs sorting argument instead REUSES every combinatorial lemma of Chains/Presentation (cuts, CutsAt, cutsAt_dims_eq, exists_swap, factor_ext, sInf_cuts_comp) and only redoes the two inductions.

The one real difference: a composite upstairs is the downstairs composite read BACKWARDS, so the lowest junction height sorts to the FRONT (ECh.exists_min_first, front-peeling by Quiver.Path.eq_toPath_comp_of_length_eq_succ). That orientation is forced: ChainCat.factor_ext pins a factorisation whose codim-1 step is LAST downstairs, i.e. FIRST upstairs. Sorting to the back upstairs would need a 'first step' version of factor_ext.

Added downstairs in Chains/Presentation.lean: CutsAt.ne_of_comp (two consecutive generators cut at different heights -- the middle word has the second's junction and not the first's) and exists_swap' (the swap exchanges BOTH heights, not just one).
close_reason: Closed

title: The interval of a refinement is Boolean on its cuts
description:
The interval of a refinement is a Boolean lattice, and what that buys.

Results wanted:

* interval_iso: for f : a --> b in Ch K, the chains c with a --> c --> b
  correspond to the subsets of cuts f. A middle chain satisfies
  cuts b subset cuts c subset cuts a, its word is fixed by the subset,
  and its map by factor_ext / merge_factor_unique. The load-bearing
  half is realizability: every subset is an actual chain of K, i.e. the
  intermediate fillers exist. The argument is that a sub-window merge is
  a face of the full filler and precubical sets are closed under faces.
* hence the factorizations of a codimension-k morphism are the orderings
  of cuts f, so there are k! of them, and Factor2.equivBool is the k = 2
  case.
* hence the graph on factorizations, with an edge per codimension-two
  relation, is the Cayley graph of S_k under adjacent transpositions:
  k!(k-1)/2 edges.

Already proved, for the 4-cube, in Testing/Hexagon.lean: the interval
from the run to the top chain IS the Boolean lattice on three cut
heights, six factorizations, hexagonal swap graph, five single-window
edges and one disjoint pair. Evaluated at k = 4 and k = 5 the counts are
24/36 and 120/240, matching k! and k!(k-1)/2.

A trap the 4-cube exposes: the species of an edge depends on the word at
that moment, not on the pair of heights. Cuts 1 and 3 are disjoint while
cut 2 survives and adjacent once it is gone, so the pair {1,3} appears
once as a DoubleCut and once as a SiteCut. Counting by pairs gives two
interchange edges; the answer is one.

NOT wanted, and deliberately so: a coherent presentation in the
polygraph sense. mathlib has a ModelCategory framework but no
polygraphs, no computads, and no folk model structure on 2-Cat, so both
the homotopy-basis definition and Guiraud-Malbos-Mimram's cofibrant
approximation characterization would have to be built from nothing.
Cofibrant approximation remains the right justification for calling the
output an invariant -- approximations are unique up to homotopy
equivalence -- but it is not a route. The interval theorem gives the
contractibility that coherence would be used for, with no library.

Why none of this is content on its own: Ch (cube n) has a terminal
object, so it is contractible and constant coefficients see nothing. The
invariant is the homotopy colimit of the coefficient system over
Ch(K)^op, which for runs is the Salvetti complex. The presentation of
Ch(K) is the resolution that computes it, not the answer.
close_reason: factorisationEquiv f : Factorisation f = {S // cutSet b.dims subset S subset cutSet a.dims}, at 6d7ea2b. Both halves are hypothesis-free: exists_factor and factor_ext, no codimension, no NonSelfLinked, no AdmitsAltitude. comments.author: zstone
comments.text:
Realizability is not a side condition of the interval theorem. A factorisation of f : a --> b through an intermediate word needs an intermediate chain c : Ch K, but its classifying map is manufactured as e (composed with) b.map rather than chosen, so existence reduces to a statement about serial wedges with no K in it: no fillers to find, and no NonSelfLinked / AdmitsAltitude side condition. Checked at the square in Zbp and at [1,1,1] --> [3].

The keystone is uniqueness of a factorisation through an ARBITRARY word, and it is necessarily a presheaf-level statement: the tail leg of a wedge starts at the junction, so it is not bi-pointed. The refinements on either side stay bi-pointed.

title: [open] How to package the presentation of C_d(K)
description:
Decide how C_d(K) is built in Lean. Deliverable: a decision plus the signature, not a proof.

Candidates:
- by hand: free category on the codim-1 graph, quotiented by the codim-2 relations;
- via a 2-truncated simplicial set and hoFunctor2 (mathlib has hoFunctor2, nerveFunctor2, nerve2Adj, fullyFaithfulNerveFunctor2, and hoFunctor2 is monoidal), which is definitionally free-category-modulo-2-simplices.

Facts bearing on the choice: mathlib has no builder for a truncated simplicial set from face/degeneracy data, so a hand-built one means defining a presheaf on the truncated simplex category directly. A 2-simplex asserts only that one composite of two equals one edge, so a length-3 = length-3 braid relation needs auxiliary 1-simplices and several triangles. If the simplicial set is a nerve then hoFunctor2 is the identity up to isomorphism and buys nothing.
close_reason: Decided: by hand. Paths on the generator quiver via Paths.lift, quotiented by CategoryTheory.Quotient. The 2-truncated simplicial set route buys nothing: mathlib's Functor.homRel instances already give the equivalence for free once the evaluation functor is full and essentially surjective, which is cheaper than building a truncated presheaf by hand.

title: Normalization by codimension-2 moves: Ch(K) is presented in codim 1 and 2
description:
GOAL: the free category on codimension-one morphisms, quotiented by the codimension-two relations, is isomorphic to Ch(K) -- identity on objects, unconditional in K.

This is a presentation of Ch(K) itself. It is NOT the localization and NOT the braid presentation; those are later and their relations have a different shape (braid relations have length 3, these have length 2). Do not drift into cospans or complements.

Four statements, in dependency order.

1. THE HINGE -- exactly two factorizations.

  structure Factor2 {a b : Ch K} (g : a -> b) where
    c : Ch K ; g1 : a -> c ; g2 : c -> b
    h1 : codim g1 = 1 ; h2 : codim g2 = 1 ; comp : g1 >> g2 = g

  Factor2.equivBool {g : a -> b} (hcod : codim g = 2) : Factor2 g ~ Bool

with the two values pinned by the species from codimTwoWedgeUnique, so this is derived from the classification rather than a bare cardinality claim. Then Factor2.swap is the transport of Bool.not: a fixed-point-free involution, giving the move as a FUNCTION rather than a choice.

This is the statement that can actually fail. Ch(K) is NOT thin for general K -- only for the cube, and only via NonSelfLinked plus AdmitsAltitude -- so a third factorization through the same intermediate, differing in its inclusion data, is not excluded a priori. Establish or refute this before building anything on it.

2. THE FREE CATEGORY AND THE RELATION.

  CodimOne K := Ch K, with Quiver instance {f : a -> b // codim f = 1}
  eval : Paths (CodimOne K) => Ch K            -- Paths.lift of the inclusion
  codimTwoRel : HomRel (Paths (CodimOne K))    -- inductive, one constructor:
     the two length-2 paths of a Factor2 and its swap

The relation must be CONTEXTLESS -- no p ++ _ ++ q. CategoryTheory.Quotient generates the congruence, so whiskering comes for free; building context into the relation makes every later proof worse.

3. NORMALIZATION.

  normalForm {a b : Ch K} (f : a -> b) : Paths (CodimOne K) a b
  eval_normalForm : eval.map (normalForm f) = f
  normalForm_eq (P) : Quotient.functor codimTwoRel |>.map P
                    = Quotient.functor codimTwoRel |>.map (normalForm (eval.map P))

normalForm f is the canonical schedule: right-bracketed within each merge group, leftmost group first, by recursion on codim f. normalForm_eq is proved DIRECTLY -- bubble the leftmost merge into position, induct, with the lexicographic order on merge positions as the termination measure. Do NOT set up local confluence plus Newman, and do not introduce a Relation.ReflTransGen of moves; the direct argument is one induction and needs no diamond bookkeeping.

4. THE PRESENTATION.

  presentation (K) : Quotient (codimTwoRel K) ~= Ch K   -- identity on objects

Fullness is ChainCat.generated. Faithfulness is two rewrites: if eval P = eval Q = f then P and Q are both equal to normalForm f in the quotient.

UNCONDITIONAL in K throughout -- no NonSelfLinked, no AdmitsAltitude. That is the point of this formulation rather than the interval one, and it is consistent with generated / codimOneWedgeUnique / codimTwoWedgeUnique all already being hypothesis-free.
notes:
DONE.  Chains/Presentation.lean (772 lines), sorry-free, axioms propext/Classical.choice/Quot.sound.
lake build CubeChains 1690 jobs; full sweep 1701; no warnings in the new file.

HEADLINE
  presentation (K) : CategoryTheory.Quotient (codimTwoRel K) ≌ Ch K
  presentation_obj : (presentation K).functor.obj {as := CodimOne.mk a} = a  (rfl)
via presentationFunctor = CategoryTheory.Quotient.lift (codimTwoRel K) (eval K) _, with Full /
Faithful / EssSurj / IsEquivalence instances.  codimTwoRel is contextless: two length-2 paths
coming from two Factor2's of a common map.

THE SHAPE OF THE ARGUMENT differs from the bead's plan.  There is no normalForm.  A junction
height is an ABSOLUTE number (dimSum of a prefix), because dimSum is constant along a refinement.
So:  cuts f = {t | IsCut a.dims t and not IsCut b.dims t}  depends only on the two words;
cuts_comp says cuts (f >> g) = cuts f + cuts g;  CutsAt e t (codim 1) gives cuts e = {t}.
A generating path is then an ORDERING of cuts (eval P), and sorting is one induction:
exists_min_last (induction on length) bubbles the generator at sInf (cuts (eval P)) to the end,
using exists_swap (the Factor2 swap, which exchanges the two heights) for each step.
quot_eq_of_eval_eq then inducts on length: sort both paths, the two last steps cut at the same
height, factor_ext identifies them, recurse.  No normalForm, no Newman, no ReflTransGen.

THE CONTENT is factor_ext: two factorisations f = g >> e = g' >> e' with codim e = codim e' = 1
and a COMMON middle WORD cd agree in every component (cm = cm', g.phi = g'.phi, e.phi = e'.phi).
Note it is stated unbundled and phrased on .phi -- those live in types depending only on cd and
the endpoint words, never on cm, which is what dodges every HEq.  Factor1.eq_of_dims /
Factor1.eq_of_cutsAt are the bundled corollaries.

factor_ext reduces (splitAt + tensorHom_injective, twice) to merge_factor_unique:
  u >> w = u' >> w'  with u,u' : /\A -> /\[p,q] and w,w' : /\[p,q] -> /\[n]  implies  u=u', w=w'.
That is the one new geometric input and it is short: the left leg of w is a map of CUBES, so it is
pinned by its two extremal vertices (cubeHom_ext_vertex, transported by hom_ext_vertex_of_cubeIso);
u is bi-pointed so both vertices are already visible in u >> w; merge_ext_inl' then pins w, and the
leg is monic (cubePsh_mono, transported by mono_of_cubeIso) so it cancels and pins u.
Factor2.eq_of_dims (Chains/Factor2) is NOT used by this route -- only Factor2.exists_pair is, via
Factor2.exists_other.  equivBool and swap are not used at all.

WHAT THE PROOF ACTUALLY NEEDED from Factor2.lean: exists_pair, eq_of_dims (inside exists_other),
codim_eq_two.  Nothing else.

TRAPS PAID FOR (beyond the ones already recorded):
* CodimOne K := Ch K must be a plain def (Ch K already has a Quiver from its Category), and then
  the quiver instance does NOT unfold at anonymous-constructor / rw transparency.  Cure: named
  crossings CodimOne.as / CodimOne.mk / gen / genHom, each written with `show ... from`.  Every
  attempt to write (a : Ch K) as an ascription instead picks the WRONG Quiver instance.
* (eval K).obj a and a.as are defeq but not syntactic, so rw/simp of anything whose implicit
  object arguments come from one spelling fails against the other.  Cure: state each step as a
  `have` with the spelling you want, and connect with congrArg / Category.assoc as TERMS.
* rw [h] inside `exact f _ _ (by ...)` sees a goal still full of metavariables; hoist to a named
  `have` (CutsAt.mem_cuts exists only for this).
* Quotient.sound and Quotient.lift resolve to core's Quotient, not CategoryTheory's.  Qualify.

title: Germ vs Artin as two presentations of B(cube n): Matsumoto, geometrically
description:
Results wanted:
* The single-bead objects of degree d are the Garside germ generators: one per permutation of the d+1 events in that bead.
* Composition of those generators is length-additive exactly when no pair of strands crosses twice, i.e. the germ relation of Braid/Germ.lean.
* Hence the germ data presents B(cube n).
* Combined with the degree-<=2 (Artin) presentation of the same category, this gives GarsideBraid n = ArtinBraid n with no hypothesis -- discharging Matsumoto n, and making garside_equiv_artin unconditional.

This subsumes the old standalone Matsumoto goal: the point is that both presentations are read off the SAME object, B(cube n), at different degree cutoffs.

title: B(cube n) is the positive braid category -- faithfulness of Conc
description:
THE headline result of this thread.

Results wanted:
* B(cube n) is equivalent to the positive braid category: objects Perm (Fin n), and Hom(x,y) the positive braids lifting the permutation carrying x to y.
* BConc is that equivalence, so it is full and FAITHFUL. This is the faithfulness of Conc on the cube, stated with no arrangement, no asphericity and no K(pi,1) input -- purely precubical.
* The vertex groups are the pure braid groups; at the terminal Zbp the full braid group.

title: Coherence for C_d(K): what is canonical and what is not
Codimension-2 morphisms are the relations
description:
For each of the two species of codim-2 morphism, build the two codim-1 sequences and prove they are parallel: same source chain and same target chain.

Results wanted:
- one bead into three: two sequences of length 3, endpoints the chain and its complement over the whole 3-window. All four intermediate swaps have fillers inside the single filler cube, so no hypothesis on K beyond that cube is needed.
- two beads into two: two sequences of length 2, the commutation square.
- parallelism is equality of the source and target chains of K, not merely of their dimension lists.
- at degree 0 these are the Artin braid and commutation relations.

title: Codimension-1 morphisms are the generators
description:
For a codim-1 morphism wedge p -> wedge a -> K of degree n, build its source and target chains: the chain itself, and its complement. Both have degree n, so generators preserve degree and C(K) splits over the degree.

Results wanted:
- source and target are chains of K of the same degree, differing by transposing two adjacent beads.
- the construction is natural in K.
- at degree 0 these are exactly the braid generators between adjacent runs, one in each direction, and they are not mutually inverse.
notes:
LANDED, all three results (Chains/Reversal.lean unless noted).

Source and target, same degree, adjacent beads transposed:
CutData.complHom : d.srcCompl --> b is the partner codim-1 refinement, same target and same
filler cube; degree_srcCompl (degree preserved) and codim_complHom = 1. The source word is
d.l ++ d.q :: d.p :: d.r, i.e. the cut bead's two pieces transposed -- and that transposition
is the adjacent transposition of S_2 inside the word, see zmi.20's serialCompl_pair. Involutive
on objects: srcCompl_compl : d.compl.srcCompl = a. Fixed-point free: srcCompl_dims_ne.

Natural in K:
CutData.pushforward g transports the cut data along g : K --> L (same beads, same filler,
same identifications). complphi_pushforward is rfl -- the wedge map does not move at all --
and srcCompl_pushforward says complementing commutes with ChainCat.pushforward g on objects.

Degree 0 = the braid generators:
pieces_eq_one -- at degree 0 both pieces of the cut bead are EDGES (p = q = 1), so the cut
bead is a square. srcCompl_dims_of_degree_zero -- the dimension word is therefore UNCHANGED,
so the complement moves within the runs over a fixed b: it exchanges the two adjacent runs
through that square, one arrow into b in each direction. mergeCompl_inl/inr say what it does
concretely: each leg of the complement is revCubeHom of the OTHER leg, which on a square sends
the bottom-then-right run to the left-then-top run.
They are not mutually inverse -- indeed neither is invertible at all:
ChainCat.not_isIso_of_codim_ne_zero (Chains/Degree.lean), since codim is additive and kills
identities. So the pair is a SPAN over b, which is exactly why the localization (zmi.6) and
not a groupoid quotient is what turns these into braid generators.

title: Design record: computational model of the braidGrading tower (READ FIRST)
description:
The architecture and constraints every gvp bead follows. SCOPE: only the braidGrading tower (Ch K -> Lines K -> Int(Lines K) -> evKey/evPerm/event-count -> the braid category -> braidGrading). Nothing else in Testing/ or the repo.

APPROACH (B, chosen): make the REAL topos-model tower computable by starting from finite data (finite cells + face table -> PrecubicalConstructions -> Nerve -> BPSet) and giving computable bodies to the noncomputable ops. Fidelity by SOUND @[csimp] (a proof spec = impl), NOT trusted @[implemented_by].

SMALL LOCAL CORE REFACTORS are permitted and preferred: delete the .choose block calls (blockIdx/blockFace), give Chamber a decidable order, rewrite nEvents = dims-sum. Use @[csimp] only where a direct refactor would be large or destabilise a proof, notably the wedge pushout.

THE WEDGE PUSHOUT is a pointed glue: gluing two presheaves at one vertex = disjoint-union-of-cells + one identification, and desc = a case-split on the summand. Implement wedge2/serialWedge/iota/desc computably + csimp. A necessary evil for any computational model of this math.

DO NOT route the compute path through equivWedgeCat: it carries NonSelfLinked + AdmitsAltitude, which the target K will not satisfy, so it would silently narrow the domain. It stays a theorem-transport tool only.

DO NOT enumerate Ch K / ConcCat K: loops make them infinite. Evaluate the functor POINTWISE on given executions/refinements.

OUTPUT: braidGrading.map f = ofPerm (evPerm f), a single germ generator, so the computable signal is evPerm f : Perm (Fin (nEvents x)). Emit a NON-normalized Artin braid word (List of signed generator indices) from a reduced word of that permutation; writhe = permLen. Feed GAP later. The PresentedGroup word problem is never on braidGrading critical path (only braidGrpd).
design: Coq-extraction contrast that motivates the approach: Lean has no separate extraction pass; noncomputable is a static refusal; @[csimp] internalises the runnable-vs-spec equality as a kernel-checked theorem (vs Coq trusting an external erasure). So we bolt verified computable bodies onto the noncomputable spec rather than rewriting the theorems.

title: The exact sequence: forgetting the line loses only PURE braids
description:
PROVED (Braid/Purity.lean, green, sorry-free):
  permHom_braidPhi_eq_one_of_concProjN : concProjN gamma = id  =>  permHom (Phi gamma) = 1
i.e. a loop of executions whose CHAIN-zigzag is trivial has a braid with trivial permutation.
Since PureBraid n := (permHom n).ker, that IS 'its braid is pure'.

THE MAP OF EXACT SEQUENCES:
  1 -> ker(concProjN) -> Aut(mk x) --concProjN--> Aut(mk (chain x))
          |                 |                          |
          | Phi             | Phi                      | rho  (chain event monodromy)
          v                 v                          v
  1 ->  PureBraid n ----> Braid n  ---permHom------> Perm (Fin n)

 - bottom row exact BY DEFINITION (PureBraid n = ker permHom).
 - RIGHT SQUARE COMMUTES: braidPhi_comp_permHom (the permutation part of the braid IS the event
   monodromy -- germ version, new) + concRho_forget (the event monodromy reads ONLY THE CHAIN:
   concFrameSystem's action on a morphism is eventEquiv of its chain map, so it factors through
   'forget the line' -- new).
 - TOP ROW SPLIT by the standard line (stdSectionGrpd_comp_concProj, Braid/ChGrading).
 - LEFT VERTICAL = the induced map on kernels. That is this theorem.

WHY IT MATTERS: it says exactly what Ch(K) can miss. NOT arbitrary braids -- only PURE ones. The
S_n-shadow of the braid functor is a CHAIN invariant, full stop; the line buys only the lift from
S_n to B_n, and the entire discrepancy lands in P_n.

CONVERSE FAILS, and that is the point: Ch(box^n) has a terminal object, so EVERY loop is
concProjN-trivial there, yet the braids are nontrivial pure braids. On box^2 the generator of
pi_1(ConcGrpd) = Z maps to the FULL TWIST sigma_1^-2 (hand-computed; the 4-object K_2,2 graph).

ALSO LANDED: subsingleton_hom_of_isTerminal (Foundations/FreeGroupoidLift) -- the free groupoid on a
category with a terminal object is CODISCRETE. Elementary (build 1 = const(mk t) via liftNatIso from
its generator components); no nerve, no Gabriel-Zisman. This is the 'Ch(box^n) is contractible' half.

STILL OPEN: (a) Ch(serial wedge) has a terminal object -- the taut chain <dims, id>; 3 lines, not yet
written. (b) whether Phi(ker) is GENERATED by the local cube twists, i.e. whether a global Fund loop
acts nontrivially on them. That is the remaining K-dependent content.

Plus the split exactness (stdSectionN_comp_chainProjN' = rfl; stdSectionGrpdN_comp_concProjN' = 𝟭; loopProj_surjective). Right square commutes via braidPhi_comp_permHom + concRho_forget'.

title: The delooping: rebuild it on Braids as EnrichedCategory Cat PUnit (BraidDeloop's cannot be a strict-2-functor target)
description:
CORRECTION to the first framing of this bead: the delooping is NEEDED — it is the target of the 2-functor CFund => B(Braid) (Cubical-791). The claim is narrower and it is this:

*** BraidDeloop's delooping CANNOT serve as the target of a strict 2-functor from CFund. ***

The target of an EnrichedFunctor Cat must itself be an EnrichedCategory Cat, whose 'assoc' axiom is an EQUALITY of functors. braidDeloopComp (BraidDeloop.lean:699) is built as
    (freeGroupoidProdEquiv BraidSig BraidSig).inverse >> FreeGroupoid.map braidTensorSig
and freeGroupoidProdEquiv = Localization.uniq is pinned only UP TO NATURAL ISO. So it cannot satisfy an equality-of-functors assoc. This is the exact trap Flow/Flow.lean:387 and FreeGroupoidLift.lean:9 document, and it is why lift2 exists.

WHY THE GERM STACK DOES NOT HIT IT AT ALL:
  Salvetti: BraidCat n is the ACTION CATEGORY of S_n on the Salvetti poset — morphisms are crossings,
            NOT invertible. So you MUST groupoidify (BraidGrpdSig = FreeGroupoid BraidSig), and then
            comp is a functor out of a PRODUCT OF FREE GROUPOIDS -> lift2 dance required.
  Germ:     Braids = Sigma n, SingleObj (Braid n) is ALREADY a groupoid (Braid/Category.lean:41),
            because braids are invertible. So comp = braidsTensor is a PLAIN FUNCTOR
            Braids x Braids => Braids. The enriched assoc is a bare Functor.ext.
            NO free-groupoid machinery at all — no lift2, no lift3_ext.

THE BUILD:
  def BDeloop : Type := PUnit                      -- one 0-cell
  instance : EnrichedCategory Cat BDeloop where
    Hom _ _ := Cat.of Braids                       -- 1-cells = strand counts, 2-cells = braids
    id _    := Cat.Hom.ofFunctor (Cat.fromChosenTerminalEquiv.symm braidsUnit)
    comp    := Cat.Hom.ofFunctor braidsTensor      -- juxtaposition: n (x) m = n + m
  Three laws, each a Functor.ext whose h_obj is congrArg strands (Nat.add_assoc / add_zero / zero_add)
  and whose h_map is the juxHom coherence.

MISSING INPUTS (this is the whole job): Braid/Category.lean has braidsTensor_obj, braidsTensor_map,
braidsUnit — but NO assoc/unit lemmas. Need the braidsTensor_* obj+map pair, same two-column shape as
concConc_obj_* / concConc_map_* in Flow/CFund.lean.

NOT MonoidalSingleObj: it needs MonoidalCategory Braids (associator/unitor isos + pentagon + triangle)
and yields a NON-strict Bicategory, so a 2-functor out of the strict CFund would owe coherence. The
enriched route skips all of it.

THEN Cubical-791 is EnrichedFunctor Cat (CFund K) BDeloop — mathlib's EnrichedFunctor (Enriched/Basic.lean:288),
two laws: map_id and map_comp. map_comp IS the flashy statement: concatenation of executions |-> juxtaposition
of braids, so strand counts ADD.

ONLY THEN does BraidDeloop.lean become retirable (it is already an orphan: nothing imports it; the sole
reference is a comment at Braid/Category.lean:15).

ALGEBRAIC CORE DONE (green, sorry-free, committed):

The three axioms peel (as in Flow/CFund) to Functor.ext over braidsTensor, whose h_obj halves ARE braidsTensor_obj_* and whose h_map halves ARE braidsTensor_map_*. The one obstacle: the eqToHom from Functor.ext's h_obj has implicit object args 'braidsTensor.obj (strands.., strands..)' while the braidHom-slide lemmas expect 'strands (..)' — DEFEQ but not syntactic, so rw won't match and simp-normalizing doesn't fix the proof term inside eqToHom.
