title: BRAID_ENRICHMENT.md: rewrite §1 and §4 — both claims are wrong
description:
Two claims in the doc are false as written.

§1/§4 'CFund K = ->pi_1(K) with every hom-set replaced by a BRAID GROUP' -- FALSE twice over. Hom-objects are GROUPOIDS, not groups; and their vertex groups are PURE and REDUCIBLE: a single n-cube gives P_n (concCubeEquiv + Salvetti), and a wedge gives prod_i P_{d_i} (concWedgeSerialEquiv), i.e. the block-diagonal pure subgroup of B_n. The full braid group is never a vertex group -- non-pure braids arise ONLY from event monodromy, which is global. The sentence only reads as true because 'concurrency braid group' is currently DEFINED to be the vertex group, making it circular.

§4 'you cannot enrich over the braid category' -- true but weak. The real statement is a DEGENERACY THEOREM: a B-enriched category is exactly a SET. Unit forces l(x,x)=0; composition forces l(x,y)+l(y,z)=l(x,z); take z:=x and l >= 0 in N, so l == 0. Nothing to do with K. Worth ~20 lines of Lean.

REPLACEMENT FRAMING: CFund K carries a canonical BRAID GRADING Phi (a lift of the forced event-count grading through B ->> N). Existence of SOME lift is vacuous (the trivial lift Phi_0 sending every 2-cell to the identity braid works), so the theorem is that OUR lift is geometric and non-trivial: writhe = salWind, S_n-shadow = evPerm, loops pure iff HDA, an n-cube contributes P_n, beads in series contribute the tensor.

Also: the braid group is now defined by its GARSIDE GERM (Braid/Germ.lean) -- one generator per permutation, relation [s][t]=[st] when lengths add. The Artin relations are CONSEQUENCES (the braid relation is the 3-cube: two length-additive factorisations of the same A_2 longest element). Salvetti is no longer needed to call the target 'braids'; what is cited instead is Matsumoto/Garside (pure algebra), and only for identifying the germ presentation with the Artin one.
close_reason: BRAID_ENRICHMENT.md §1 and §4 rewritten. Killed both false claims: (a) 'CFund = pi_1(K) with every hom-set replaced by a BRAID GROUP' — hom-objects are GROUPOIDS not groups, and their vertex groups are PURE and REDUCIBLE (P_n for a cube, prod_i P_{d_i} for a wedge); the full braid group is never a cube's vertex group. (b) 'CFund is Grpd-enriched' — it is Cat-enriched (mathlib gives Grpd no monoidal structure). §4 now carries the DEGENERACY THEOREM for B-enrichment (unit forces l(x,x)=0, composition forces additivity, z:=x and l>=0 in N give l==0, so a B-enriched category is just a set) and the correct positive statement: CFund is Cat-enriched (hence Bicategory.Strict via CatEnriched) and carries the braid grading braidGrading : Int(Lines K) => B. Also flagged that BraidDeloop cannot be the tensor target (Localization.uniq), and added the purity result to §1's invariants — plus an explicit warning not to say 'ker Phi is the branching ambiguity' (the proved statement is about ker of the PROJECTION, and Phi does not factor through it).

title: Global grading: ConcCat K => Braids (all strand counts at once)
description:
GAP FOUND: the repo has NEVER had a globally-graded braid functor. Salvetti/BraidDeloop only has braidGrpdIncl (n) : BraidGrpd n => BraidGrpdSig, one stratum at a time. So the doc's 'monoidal 2-functor to the delooped braid category' was never actually assembled -- Phi existed only per-n.

Needed because composition CHANGES the strand count (n (x) m = n+m), so the 2-functor cannot be stated per-stratum.

WHY IT IS WORK, NOT BOOKKEEPING. ConcCat K is not literally a Sigma, so obj x = strands (nEvents x) and obj y = strands (nEvents y) differ syntactically while nEvents x = nEvents y only PROPOSITIONALLY (card_eventObj_eq_of_hom). SigmaHom.mk demands definitional index equality, so map f needs an eqToHom:

  map f := braidHom (ofPerm (evPermAll f)) >> eqToHom (congrArg strands (card_eventObj_eq_of_hom f))

and map_comp then has to push eqToHom past braidHom. Two supporting lemmas:
  (1) eqToHom_braidHom: eqToHom h >> braidHom b = braidHom (cast h b) >> eqToHom h  (by subst)
  (2) evPerm coherence across strata: evPerm computed in stratum nx vs ny is related by finCongr -- evPerm goes through evIdx, which uses finCongr x.property, so this needs proving.

Estimate ~100-200 lines of dependent-type work. Blocks the 2-functor and the enrichment.
notes:
STARTED. Braid/Grading.lean builds (green, axiom-clean) with the transport layer done:

  braidCast h b            -- transport a braid along n = m
  braidCast_ofPerm         -- braidCast h (ofPerm s) = ofPerm (permCongr (finCongr h) s)
  permLen_permCongr        -- length is recast-invariant
  braidHom_eqToHom         -- a recast slides past a braid  (by subst)
  nEvents x                -- Fintype.card (EventObj x.chain)
  concRefine' f            -- f.1.unop, at the ConcCat level (no stratum)
  nEvents_eq f             -- card_eventObj_eq_of_hom: the strand count is well defined
  evIdx' x                 -- keyEquiv (evKey x.line): NO finCongr needed, since
                              nEvents x is DEFINITIONALLY Fintype.card (EventObj x.chain)
  evPerm' f                -- the event permutation, read in the SOURCE's frame

REMAINING (3 lemmas + the functor):
  1. evPerm'_id  : evPerm' (id x) = 1
  2. evPerm'_comp: evPerm' (f >> g)
       = (finCongr (nEvents_eq f).symm).permCongr (evPerm' g) * evPerm' f
     (mirror evPerm_comp; needs eventEquiv_comp)
  3. permLen additivity at ConcCat level. Easiest route: prove
       evPerm' f = evPerm (x := <x, rfl>) (y := <y, (nEvents_eq f).symm>) f
     -- should be near-rfl, because x.property is literally rfl and
     finCongr rfl = refl -- then reuse permLen_evPerm_comp + permLen_permCongr.
     GOTCHA: ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory homs are a STRUCTURE with a .hom field
     (see concRefine in BraidFunctor.lean:354, which writes f.hom.1.unop), so f must
     be wrapped, not passed directly.
  4. braidGrading : ConcCat K => Braids
       obj x := strands (nEvents x)
       map f := braidHom (ofPerm (evPerm' f)) >> eqToHom (congrArg strands (nEvents_eq f))
     map_id  : eqToHom_refl accepts ANY proof of X = X, and proof irrelevance makes
               <x, nEvents_eq (id x)> defeq to <x, rfl>.
     map_comp: push eqToHom past braidHom with braidHom_eqToHom, then it is (2) + (3).
close_reason: braidGrading : ConcCat K ⥤ Braids and braidGrpd : ConcGrpd K ⥤ Braids landed in Braid/Grading.lean, sorry-free. obj x = strands (nEvents x); map f = braidHom (ofPerm (evPerm' f)) ≫ eqToHom recast. Verified by rfl.

title: Phi : ConcGrpd K -> B, the honest braid functor
description:
Psi f := ofPerm (evPerm f); Phi := FreeGroupoid.lift Psi.

title: Braid/Category.lean — the delooped braid category B
description:
B := Sigma n, SingleObj (Braid n): objects are strand counts (NO data on objects, unlike BraidSig), Hom(n,n) = Braid n, tensor n (x) m = n+m by juxtaposition.

Juxtaposition hom Braid n x Braid m ->* Braid (n+m) comes from blockPerm: needs permLen (blockPerm s t) = permLen s + permLen t (cross-block pairs are never inverted -- easy). blockPerm_one/_mul/_assoc are ALREADY PROVED in Salvetti/BraidDeloop.lean:185-200,673 -- extract them to a low-level Braid/BlockPerm.lean so Braid/ does not depend on the Salvetti stack, and have BraidDeloop import it.

Strictness is cheap here precisely BECAUSE objects are naturals: assoc is Nat.add_assoc, not an HEq over Salvetti cells. This is the payoff for dropping BraidSig.

description: Braid n := PresentedGroup over Perm (Fin n), one generator per permutation, relation [sigma][tau] = [sigma tau] when permLen adds. permHom : Braid n ->* Perm (Fin n); PureBraid n := permHom.ker. Mathlib-only, upstreamable.

description:
§3. Assembly — the hard part is already proved.

  CategoryOfElements.pi (Lines K) : ConcCat K => (Ch K)^op
  FreeGroupoid.map (...)          : ConcGrpd K => FreeGroupoid ((Ch K)^op) = Pi_1(P K)   [Gabriel-Zisman]

- Surjective on 1-cells: every chain has at least one line.
- FULL on 2-cells: ALREADY PROVED — linesRestrict_surjective + exists_conc_zigzag (Salvetti/PurityHDA.lean). Every zigzag of chains lifts to a zigzag of executions.
- Kernel = the local pure braid groups.

This is the precise sense in which the result generalizes existing directed-topology work: Fund is the real picture, CFund its complexification, and the braid content is exactly what the projection destroys.

notes:

  CFund : EnrichedCategory Cat (CFund K)   hom u v = ConcGrpd (K.repoint u v)   (Flow/CFund.lean)
  Fund  : EnrichedCategory Cat (Fund K)    hom u v = FreeGroupoid ((Ch (K.repoint u v))ᵒᵖ)  (Flow/Fund.lean)

  obj  := id on vertices
  map u v := Cat.Hom.ofFunctor (concProj (K.repoint u v))
  map_id  : concProj sends the identity execution to the identity chain — should be rfl/lift_ext.
  map_comp: concProj (concGrpdConc a b) = fundConc (concProj a) (concProj b), i.e. FORGETTING THE LINE
            COMMUTES WITH CONCATENATION. On generators this is π (concConc (x,y)) = chConcatOp (π x, π y),
            which is essentially rfl (concConc's chain part IS chConc). Then lift₂_ext carries it.

(Braid/ChGrading, stdSection_comp_π = rfl), so if it is monoidal for concatenation — i.e. the standard
line of a concatenation is the concatenation of the standard lines, which should be immediate since
stdLine reads only dims — then Fund => CFund is an EnrichedFunctor SPLITTING the projection. That would
make CFund ->> Fund a SPLIT epi of 2-categories, upgrading the hom-groupoid splitting already proved in
Braid/Purity (stdSectionGrpdN_comp_concProjN').

title: The generator dictionary at Hbp box^n is bijective
description:
Wanted: obCell and genCell (Concurrency/Presentation/GlueArtin) are bijections, so that glueArtinMap is an isomorphism of the generating data and not only an equivalence of presented categories. Testing/Pi1/GlueCount measures the counts agreeing on the nose (n! 0-cells, n!(n-1) 1-cells at n = 2,3,4).

Missing input: a description of colimit (elementsPoly X P)'s own 0-cells and 1-cells — joint surjectivity of the legs colimit.ι, and the relation two legs' cells are identified by. Machinery/Presentation/Coequalizer has the levelwise construction; nothing assembles it for a general colimit.
notes:
Done (Concurrency/Presentation/GlueArtin), on top of ColimitCells:

  bijective_obCell (n) : Function.Bijective (obCell (n := n))
  bijective_genCell {n} {x y} : Function.Bijective (genCell : (x ⟶ y) → (obCell x ⟶ obCell y))
  bijective_genQuiver (n) : Function.Bijective (genQuiver n).obj ∧ ∀ x y, Function.Bijective ((genQuiver n).map : (x ⟶ y) → _)

0-cells: surjectivity is exists_colimit_ι_obj then exists_glueRunV (every run over d is entered from its own chain, and that leg is an arrow of the elements); injectivity is artinRun_eq_of_iso — an iso of fibre elements is a unit of PosBraid n, hence 1.
1-cells: surjectivity is exists_colimit_ι_map then exists_atomComp_leg (a RunStep is the atom's own cell pushed down: exists_atom_step supplies the leg v, and eq_atomWitness identifies the copy's chart); injectivity is chBraid_genCell — a generator is pinned by the atom posPerm (adjT k) it performs.

Not claimed: an isomorphism of the 2-cells. The two polygraphs relate different things (Artin's commutation/braid versus the slice posets' thinness); Presents.Map only asks that each side's 2-cells hold on the other.

description: Wanted: (presentsChainsRunColimit K).arrow ((colimit.iota (elementsPoly (wedgeHoms K) runPolyFunctor) c).pre.map g) = (locEquivElements K).inverse.map ((glueSliceEval (wedgeHoms K) (W Zbp) (eltBase c) c.unop.2).map ((runSlicePresentation (eltBase c)).arrow g)). With chBraid_glueSliceEval_runStep this gives the braid a glue generator performs directly on the colimit polygraph's generators.

    = eqToHom (at_glueV K c a) ≫ (locEquivElements K).inverse.map ((glueSliceEval (wedgeHoms K) (W Zbp) (eltBase (wedgeHoms K) c) c.unop.2).map ((runSlicePresentation (eltBase (wedgeHoms K) c)).arrow g)) ≫ eqToHom (at_glueV K c b).symm.

title: Colimit legs are jointly surjective on Polygraph cells
description: For a diagram of polygraphs, every 0-cell and every 1-cell of Limits.colimit F is in the image of some colimit.iota. Wanted because a Presents.Map out of a colimit presentation must define ob/gen on every cell and check hgen on every generator; without it the glue -> elements direction of Cubical-kpqb cannot be stated. Route that does not touch the coequalizer-of-coproducts construction: the sub-polygraph cut out by the legs' images, built as Polygraph.comap along the inclusion of the image sub-quiver, receives the legs, so colimit.desc splits comapHom and colimit.hom_ext makes the composite the identity.
notes: 2026-09-05: proved, Machinery/Presentation/ColimitCells.lean. Not by comap: the cells functor is a LEFT ADJOINT (Polygraph.toThin is its transpose — a prefunctor GenObj P.Gen -> GenObj Gen' IS a morphism P -> thin Gen', and thin_hom_ext says a morphism into a thin polygraph IS its prefunctor). So colimitCells descends a compatible family of prefunctors, ι_pre_comp_colimitCells is the fac, colimit_pre_ext the uniqueness. Joint surjectivity is then ONE test of colimit_pre_ext per dimension against a Prop-valued quiver: exists_colimit_ι_obj, exists_colimit_ι_map. colimitCells is the choice-free ob/gen a Presents.Map out of a colimit needs; the leg INDEX is irreducibly existential (there is no canonical leg, which is exactly why the coproduct is not a cocone).

title: A strict retract of Cat-diagrams has equivalent strict colimits, or it does not
description:
For diagrams D, D' : J ⥤ Cat with strict natural transformations E : D' ⟶ D and S : D ⟶ D' satisfying E ≫ S = 𝟙 and a natural isomorphism S ≫ E ≅ 𝟙 whose components are compatible with the transition functors: is colim E : colim D' ⥤ colim D an equivalence?

Wanted: a proof, or a counterexample. The known counterexample to the weaker statement (1 ⇉ SingleObj ℤ against 1 ⇉ 1, levelwise equivalent, non-equivalent coequalizers) is ruled out by the strict retraction — naturality forces both legs to land in the image of E, and the image is then a skeleton, so the two glued objects coincide.

Settling it decides whether Polygraph.SliceSkeleton (Machinery/Presentation/Glue) is needed at all for presentsColimitOfLocalizedSlices, or only for the presentation-level statement. Machinery/Presentation/SliceColimit's module docstring currently declines to assert either way.

description:

title: GlueOn's complete: derive faithfulness from a grading and diamonds, abstractly
description:
STRENGTHENING, not blocking. GlueOn (Machinery/Presentation/GlueOn.lean) has Phi (glueOnDesc) and essential surjectivity unconditionally-plus-covering; Full and Faithful remain. Faithful ('complete') should be DERIVED from geometric conditions rather than assumed, because complete-as-hypothesis is close to assuming the conclusion -- faithfulness is most of what 'presents' means.

THE CONDITIONS TO ASSUME, both now available abstractly:
 - A GRADING. Machinery/Grading.lean now has degFunctor / degLoc / deg_le_of_loc_hom / isEmpty_loc_hom_of_deg_lt: an object degree that arrows lower and W keeps descends to C[W-1], and a hom-set that would raise it is EMPTY. That is CubeCrossing's crossFunctor/crossLoc argument, which was never about the cube; CubeCrossing's versions are now corollaries.
 - DIAMONDS. HasDiamonds (Concurrency/Grading/Degree.lean:602) abstracted: two codimension-one steps out of one object close.
Ch K discharges both (crossLen, hasDiamonds_cube), so nothing is lost at the instance.

WHY IT IS NOT CHEAP, from the survey. The model proof is word_unique (Concurrency/Merge/CubeThin.lean:434) and its supporting cast -- word_of_W, word_of_run_map, wordProp, exists_word_of_hom, descent_of_word_step, word_le, exists_atom_codim, word_diamond, word_of_step -- roughly 200 lines for the CONCRETE cube, where all 0-cells are runs of one polygraph. GlueOn is strictly harder: words CROSS COPIES, since 0-cells are shared between copies, so the induction must move a segment from copy s1 to copy s2. The only tool is GlueOnRel.overlap, which relates the two readings of a generator of P d' along a span s1 <- d' -> s2. The span always exists (a covered 0-cell CARRIES an arrow into its copy's base, by gluePt's definition), but overlap only moves segments IN THE IMAGE of (P.map f).cells, and not every generator of P s1.1 is such an image. So the diamond hypothesis must also say the diamond's legs are SPELLED by generators of the available copies -- i.e. it entangles with Full rather than being independent of it.

CHECK BEFORE STARTING: the GlueRefutation counterexample (Pt = Discrete PUnit, W = bot) is NOT excluded by 'no grading exists' -- it is excluded because W = bot fails ContainsIdentities, so the grading hypothesis needs [W.IsMultiplicative] or the identities explicitly. Do not take the refutation as evidence the route is blocked; it is evidence the hypothesis must be stated carefully.

Done when: complete is a theorem from the grading and diamond conditions, GlueOn's presentation theorem no longer assumes faithfulness, and Ch K discharges the conditions.
notes:
DISCHARGED 2026-09-04, and NOT from the grading + diamonds. `presentsGlueOn`
(Machinery/Presentation/GlueOn.lean) now proves `Φ.Faithful` itself; the `hcomplete`
argument is deleted, and so is its instance at ChainCat.presentsChainsRunGlue, which is
now `(K : BPSet) → Presents (glueOn (wedgeHoms K) runLabels (chGlueV '' MaximalChains K))
((W K).Localization)` with no hypothesis at all.

THE ROUTE THAT WORKED: build the retraction, i.e. Glue.lean's `glueRetractDesc` argument,
for GlueOn. Faithfulness of Φ needs the UNIT (`Φ ⋙ Ψ = 𝟭`), not the counit; `Ψ ⋙ Φ ≅ 𝟭`
plus Full plus EssSurj does NOT give faithfulness (quotient counterexample).

Two obstructions, and what each cost:
(1) An object `c` outside `S` carries no copy, so `Glue`'s `glueRetractPre c` has nothing to
land in. Fix: `spanIncl hs (f : d' ⟶ s.1)` reads `P d'` inside the copy at `s`, and
`spanIncl_eq` — which is `GlueOnRel.overlap` and nothing else — says the reading does not
depend on the leg. So `carriedIncl c` (choose any covering leg) is choice-free as a functor
and strictly natural. That is the whole reason the overlap 2-cells are indexed by spans.
(2) `Glue` needs `(p d).E` bijective on objects (`strictInv`), which a compact presentation
never is. Fix: `SliceRetract L W`, a 6-field GEOMETRIC structure — `ret` (every slice object
is entered from a labelled one), `inj`, `merge` (the entry is a `W`-arrow), `fix` (a label is
entered from itself), `push` (the entry ignores what the base maps into), `top` (the source
of a label carries its own identity as a label) — plus `hthin`, the localized slices being
posets. `ret/merge/fix` + thin give `slInv` with `(p d).E ⋙ slInv = 𝟭` STRICTLY; `push+inj`
give `slInv_square` strictly (no `hP` needed!); and `top` is what makes `Ψ(Φ v) = v` an
EQUALITY rather than an iso — a covered 0-cell's base carries the identity as a label, so
`gluePt_ret` is `Glue`'s `gluePt_base` without surjective labels.

WHY NOT GRADING + DIAMONDS: the target `(∫X)[W⁻¹]` is not thin (it is the braid groupoid at
`Hbp □ⁿ`), so "two parallel words agree" is false and a confluence/normal-form argument would
have to reconstruct the word from its image — i.e. build the retraction anyway. No grading and
no diamond is used anywhere in the proof. `HasDiamonds` and `Machinery/Grading` are untouched.

CLIENT: `runSliceRetract` (Concurrency/Presentation/SliceFunctor.lean) is the entry `runMerge`;
`fix` is `runRet_self` (out of a run the merge is a transport, by `eq_runMerge` + `W_eqToHom`),
`push` is `Category.assoc`, `top` is `⟨Over.mk (𝟙 _), a.2⟩`. `hthin` is `locOver_isThin`, moved
to SlicePresentation.lean beside `locSlice_isThin`.

FLAGGED, not acted on: `Glue.lean`'s `presentsGlue`/`glueRetractDesc`/`Machinery/StrictInverse`
now have no code consumers (only doc references from GlueRefutation). It is the bijective-labels
theorem and its hypotheses are incomparable to GlueOn's (bijective labels do not give thin
slices), so it is not subsumed — but the retraction argument is now written twice. A decision
for the user, not a deletion I should make.

title: Is there a materially faster proof that Ch(cube n)[W-1] is the weak order?
description:
SURVEY ONLY -- nothing rewritten, nothing deleted. Answer: YES, materially, and the model is
ALREADY IN THE TREE AND ALREADY IN SCOPE.

THE BIJECTION HOLDS, and in a better form than the one proposed. The proposed
  Ch (cube n) ~= Sigma sigma : Perm (Fin n), {S // Des sigma subset S}
is a REPARAMETRISATION of chFaceEquiv : Ch (cube n) ~= COM.Face (braidCOM n)
(Concurrency/Salvetti/ChainBraidFace.lean:374) -- a chain IS an ordered set partition, and the
(sigma, S) form is that partition read as (sort order, block boundaries). Also present:
  chFaceCatEquiv : (Ch (cube n))op ~= Face (braidCOM n)      (ChainBraidFace.lean:606)
  blockChain (beta : Fin n -> Fin L) (surjective) : Ch (cube n)   (:415, COMPUTABLE)
  beadOf_blockChain (:418), eq_of_beadOf (:405), blockChain_beadOf (:430)
  reflectHom : chFace b <= chFace a -> (a --> b)             (:569, COMPUTABLE)
so the inverse direction -- construct a chain from a prescribed ordered partition -- is a
standalone computable def with NO hypotheses in its statement.

NO NonSelfLinked / AdmitsAltitude PROBLEM. reflectHom does go through refineToWedge, i.e. the
one-way bridge of beads-to-wedges-is-one-way, but it DISCHARGES both with cube_nonSelfLinked n and
BPSet.cube_admitsAltitude n. The landmine is about general K; the cube satisfies both, so the model
is unconditional here.

AND CubeFaces ALREADY IMPORTS IT. Verified by computing the import closures: ChainBraidFace's cone
contains no Merge/Cube* (so no cycle), and CubeFaces' cone already contains ChainBraidFace. The
990-line file uses beadOf from it and nothing else -- it re-derives the join/meet layer from chart
geometry with the combinatorial model sitting unused in scope.

WHAT WOULD GO. The counting block (CubeFaces:249-470, ~220 lines: beadCard, samePairs,
card_samePairs_le, two_mul_card_lt_pairs, card_samePairs_le_three, beadCard_le_two_of_disjoint)
exists ONLY because the present model cannot COMPUTE cross of a constructed chain -- it can only
BOUND it, so cross_of_meet_far/_braid squeeze permLen between a weak-order lower bound and an
'only so much can be un-crossed' upper bound. In the partition model those are direct computations:
merging two disjoint adjacent singleton blocks of a run sorts two disjoint adjacent transpositions,
giving sigma * adjT i * adjT j on the nose; the adjacent case sorts a 3-window. Likewise
exists_atom_face (~60) and exists_atom_factor (~90) become 'delete cut i'; exists_meet_shape /
exists_meet / exists_meet_W / exists_join (~250) become union and intersection of cut sets. The
tool that makes the sorting computations cheap already exists: flatten_apply (ChartHom.lean, 'a
bijection respecting the (bead, then rank) key IS flatten's inverse').

ESTIMATE, honestly: CubeFaces 990 -> roughly 350-450, so ~550-650 lines saved, plus a smaller
saving in CubeThin (word_diamond's two branches become explicit rather than squeezed). Against
that, ~100-150 lines of new packaging (the (sigma,S) normal form and the cut-set lattice). Net

risk is that the sorting computations are fiddlier in Lean than on paper.

- runAt (CubeWeakOrder.lean:386, NONCOMPUTABLE, via crossRun_bijective.surjective.choose) and

any normal form must be connected to Ch (cube n) exactly once) and the 130 pure-permutation lines
of WeakOrder (mathlib has no right weak order on Perm).
notes:
THE FORK IS SETTLED: the answer is NO. The Artin machinery cannot close word_unique, and the partition-model plan in this bead's description stands as written. Three reasons, independent, in increasing strength.

(1) THE CLOSING MOVE NEEDS A COSPAN APEX IN Ch (cube n), NOT IN THE LOCALIZATION. word_unique's distinct-cut case ends at CubeThin.lean:491 with 'show uc >> v = uc' >> v' from Subsingleton.elim _ _'. Those are two morphisms of Ch (cube n) -- the UNLOCALIZED category -- equal by chCube_isThin, which is free. Everything above it (exists_join, length_of_two_steps, cross_of_meet_*, and the counting block behind them) exists to produce the object e that both land in, and to pin cross e. cubeAtom_comm/cubeAtom_braid are equalities in strictEnd (RunChart (cube n) n), i.e. equalities of PARTIAL FUNCTIONS; no object of Ch (cube n) occurs in them, so they cannot supply the apex.

(3) THE DECISIVE ONE, ALREADY A THEOREM HERE. not_nonempty_equiv_posBraidAction (Concurrency/Merge/CubeCrossing.lean:147) proves Ch(cube 2)[W-1] is NOT equivalent to PosBraidAction 2: the localized cube slice is DISCONNECTED (isEmpty_loc_hom_cubeTop) while the action category is connected. The missing input is geometric, and exists_join is where it enters.

CORRECTION TO MY OWN EARLIER NOTE ON THIS BEAD -- I OVERSTATED IT. atomAct_eq_some_iff does compute cross on the nose, but ONLY ON RUN CHARTS: RunChart (cube n) N is (wedgeHoms (cube n)).obj (op (zObj (1^N))), the all-singleton shape, and atomAct goes run-chart to run-chart. So atomAct_eq_some_iff is the normal form on the BOTTOM STRATUM ONLY, not 'most of the (sigma,S) normal form'. This bead's 100-150 line packaging budget stands.

WHAT (1) DOES GIVE THE REWRITE: it names exactly what the replacement must produce -- an object of Ch (cube n) receiving chain maps from both dc and dc', plus enough to identify its cross. In the partition model that object is literally boundaries dc INTERSECT boundaries dc', which is this bead's 'meets become intersection of cut sets', and the {b // Nonempty (a --> b)} =~ {S // {0,n} subset S subset boundaries a.dims} packaging it flags as 'about five lines, not stated anywhere' is the tool that computes its cross. So (1) confirms the plan and tells you which lemma to write first.

title: Formalize the punctured-cube counterexample to hsound
description:
The refutation of hsound from SeparatesMerges alone (Cubical-vcp) is currently an ARGUMENT, not a theorem. Formalize it: the 2-skeleton of box 3 with one square deleted, as a sub-BPSet of box 3. Separation is inherited by subobjects — maps into a subobject inject into maps into the ambient and restriction commutes, then cancel the mono — so it separates merges by separatesMerges_cube. title: SlicePres C2: the functor P on wedges
description:
Read SlicePresentation.md first. Blocked on C1 and B4.
Wanted: `P (⋁a) := ∏ᵢ P_cube aᵢ`, functorial in `Ch Zbp` via B4, as a functor `Ch Zbp ⥤ Polygraph` (`Polygraph` is already a `Category`; see Machinery/Presentation/Basic.lean).
Done when: sorry-free, `lake build CubeChains` green, debloat pass run.
notes:
UPDATED after B2. Polygraph.prod (Machinery/Presentation/Product.lean:66) is BINARY, and serialWedge is defined by recursion. So the product over a dimension list should be a right fold of binary products, matching serialWedge's own recursion, not a Fin-indexed product. B4 is deciding the same question; follow whatever shape it lands on.
SURVEY DONE 2026-09-04, NOT BUILT. C2 WANTS RESTATING, and the restatement is cheap. Nothing committed; the facts below are machine-checked in scratch, not in the tree.

WHY THE CURRENT SHAPE IS EXPENSIVE. slicePoly is a right fold of Polygraph.prod, so (slicePoly d).V is a nested product indexed by d's beads. A morphism d' --> d regroups d''s beads into consecutive blocks, so P.map has to be defined by a block recursion and map_id / map_comp become equalities of PREFUNCTORS whose object parts are the regrouping -- transport, not rfl. Six things are missing for that route: (1) Hom P (prod P Q) and the symmetric one; (2) prod functoriality Hom P1 Q1 -> Hom P2 Q2 -> Hom (prod P1 P2) (prod Q1 Q2); (3) slicePoly (a ++ b) vs prod (slicePoly a) (slicePoly b), complicated because slicePoly [] = thin (CubeStep 0) is not a unit; (4) a generator map induced by a cube face (C1's unfinished half); (5) an n-ary iterate of splitTarget; (6) an EQUALITY relating overMapLoc (W Zbp) f to the bead splitting -- B4's locChAppend_natural is only an ISO, and hP needs an equality on the nose or GlueRel.overlap does not typecheck. (6) is a hard obstruction, not cosmetic.

THE RESTATEMENT: index the polygraph by the SLICE, not by the product. (P d).V := {u : Over d // IsRun Zbp u.left}; P.map f := Over.map f. Machine-checked in scratch:
• composition in Ch Zbp is strictly associative AND unital -- (f >> g) >> h = f >> (g >> h), f >> 1 = f, 1 >> f = f, all by rfl;
• Over.map is strictly functorial on Ch Zbp, including Over.map f followed by Over.map g = Over.map (f >> g), by rfl;
• the run condition depends only on .left, which Over.map does not touch, so the subtype is preserved definitionally;
• a prototype functor Ch Zbp ⥤ Polygraph with these 0-cells and a position-indexed generator has map_id AND map_comp BOTH Hom.ext' rfl.
Also SliceLabels.ob becomes tautological and map_ob becomes rfl, which is exactly what labelsOf and hP want, so C3 gets easier at the same time.

THE PIVOT, AND IT IS SETTLED. Everything turned on whether overMapLoc f sends ATOMS to ATOMS -- if not, P.map would need the first Polygraph.Hom in this tree that spells a generator as a multi-letter word, and choosing those words by fullness + Classical.choice DOES NOT WORK because Hom.ext' is strict word-level equality, so map_id/map_comp would fail. It does send atoms to atoms. crossPerm_comp gives perm (a >> f) = perm f * perm a, and crossPerm_noDoubleCross (a crossing once made is never undone) gives exactly that a descent of perm a at i is still a descent of perm (a >> f) at i. Machine-checked. So P.map is generator-to-generator, Hom.ofPre suffices, and the index i is unchanged; the only d-dependence in the generator is the side condition 'i is interior to d', which is ANTITONE in f since boundaries d is a subset of boundaries d'.

COST: C1's presentation has to be re-indexed to the new polygraph (cubePresentation is Presents.ofThin via cubeEval, exists_run_of_loc_obj, nonempty_path_of_loc_hom -- all already about run-arrows in spirit, so it should transfer rather than be redone). Note C1 (Cubical-v53) is IN_PROGRESS and its own 'wanted' includes the morphisms induced by [m] --> [n]; that half is not done and it is exactly C2's input, so the two should be restated together.

ALSO WORTH KNOWING: Ch Zbp is NOT thin. Hom-sets are the crossing permutations (hom_ext_of_crossPerm, crossPerm_injective); only W-arrows are unique (eq_of_W). So P.map genuinely depends on f and not merely on d' <= d. Do not assume a poset.
ROUTE B IS WALLED AT TWO LEVELS, NOT ONE -- do not re-open the Polygraph.prod indexing. (a) hP needs an EQUALITY of functors or GlueRel.overlap does not typecheck, and B4's locChAppend_natural is only an iso. (b) Transporting overSlicePresentation into any other indexing needs to know which object of Over (zObj d) each slicePoly 0-cell names, and that runs through locOverEquivWedge, a Localization.uniq flagged opaque on objects at SliceLocalize.lean:82-86.

PARAMETERIZATION, 2026-09-04 -- READ BEFORE BUILDING C2. RunOver is presentation-independent; RunStep is NOT. RunOver.equiv shows the 0-cells are the hom-set out of one fixed run, which names no presentation. But RunStep is 'an interior cut k at which the run-arrow descends', i.e. adjT k -- the ARTIN spelling, baked in. A Garside spelling would name simples, not adjacent transpositions. So C2 as scoped builds ONE CONCRETE FAMILY and the glue route is parametric in nothing.

THE MECHANISM THAT MAKES THE OTHER ROUTE PARAMETRIC is Presents.elements (Machinery/Presentation/Elements.lean:241): a presentation of C induces a presentation of the category of elements of ANY F : C ⥤ Type, with Presents.restrict cutting to the defined part. cubeChartPresentation (CubeChartAction.lean:332) is that at F := cubeFibre n, and it is presentation-independent precisely because cubeFibre was built without a presentation.

SO THE PARAMETRIC ANALOGUE OF C2 IS: is ((W Zbp).over d).Localization the category of elements of a functor on ((W Zbp).op).Localization? I do not believe it is. The natural candidate F c := Hom (c, d) does not obviously descend to the localization: precomposition by a merge is INJECTIVE (crossPerm is injective on hom-sets and a merge has trivial crossing) but surjectivity is a factorisation through the merge, which needs Nonempty (c --> d) and that is not automatic.
DESCENT REFUTED IN LEAN 2026-09-04. The localized slice is NOT the category of elements of a functor on the localized base, so the two-theorem split is STRUCTURAL and C2 stays concrete. Sorry-free, scratch only, nothing committed.

THE CANDIDATE, KILLED. hom_presheaf_not_inverts_merge: at d = zObj (1^2), there are a, b and w : a --> b with W Zbp w such that precomposition (fun y : b --> d => w >> y) is NOT surjective. Concretely w is runMerge (zObj [2]) : zObj (1^2) --> zObj [2], and precomposition maps Hom(zObj [2], zObj (1^2)) -> Hom(zObj (1^2), zObj (1^2)), i.e. EMPTY -> nonempty. So F c := Hom (c, d) does not invert the merges and does not descend.

THE STRUCTURAL REASON, in one line: merge_fibres_clash. The merge is inverted by the localization, yet its two fibres over d are the empty set and {1}. A functor on the LOCALIZED base sends an inverted arrow to a bijection, so no functor on the localized base has these fibres -- i.e. Over.forget d, which IS a discrete fibration before localizing (that is why Over d = the elements of Hom(-,d)), cannot stay one after.
Supporting facts, both proved: isEmpty_hom_two_ones (the square does not refine the run, since arrows only ever add cuts and 1 is a boundary of [1,1] but not of [2]) and one_mem_boundaries_ones / one_not_mem_boundaries_two.

CAVEAT, stated honestly: this refutes descent COMPATIBLY WITH THE PROJECTION to the base. It does not rule out some unrelated functor whose elements category happens to be equivalent to the localized slice -- but such a functor would be useless for the programme, since it is the projection that makes goal (3) a bridge.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE PROGRAMME. Goal (1) unconditional-in-K is the glue route (presentsGlueOn / presentsChainsGlueOn), which consumes slice presentations and is parametric in nothing. Goal (2) parametric-in-a-base-presentation is the elements route (Presents.elements + Presents.restrict, as in cubeChartPresentation), which is conditional: it presents the elements of a functor over the localized base, and that is Ch(K)[W-1] only when the merges act invertibly on wedgeHoms K, i.e. InvertsMerges / IsSegal. Unconditional-and-parametric would need both and the descent is what would have supplied it. Goal (3) is the bridge between the two, and toChZ K is a discrete fibration for every K unconditionally, which is what makes (3) statable.
PARAMETRIC TEST ANSWERED 2026-09-04: THE IDENTIFICATION IS AVAILABLE, IN THE OP ORIENTATION. So the parametric route is LIVE and merge_fibres_clash does not touch it. Do not build C2 concrete on the strength of a two-theorem split; that reading was wrong.

THE STATEMENT IS (defined (cubeFibre n) (cubeBot n)).FullSubcategory =~ ((W (box n)).Localization)^op =~ WeakOrder n, NOT =~ (W (box n)).Localization. Two independent reasons, both forced by the tree: (1) cubeFibre lives on ((W Zbp).op).Localization and Ch K =~ ((wedgeHoms K).Elements)^op (chEquivElements), so the elements category is the OP of the chain category -- the Segal-case template chLocOpEquivElements (HAction.lean:57) has exactly this shape; (2) atomAct goes UP the weak order (atomAct_eq_some_iff, an ascent) while a morphism of (W (box n)).Localization goes DOWN (weakClass_le_of_loc_hom, locCubeWeakOrder : ... =~ (WeakOrder n)^op).

BOTH CONDITIONS ARE SATISFIED. separatesMerges_cube (ElementsFibration.lean:191). And the 3-cell layer NO LONGER EXISTS -- commit 9ba4b14 'Delete the Action-manufacturing layer'; per Cubical-rg5i the braid case uses no 3-cell, and hasDiamonds_cube appears in CubeChartAction.lean only in a comment. So cubeChartPresentation's obligations are structural (cubeBot_absorbing) plus isArtinFamily_cubeAtom, both discharged.

TWO CAVEATS, AND THEY ARE WHAT DECIDES C2.
(a) NOTHING PROVES THE IDENTIFICATION. It is Cubical-mfc, whose own text says the FibrationLocalize conclusion is FALSE as stated in this regime and that a new localization theorem is needed; its parent Cubical-vcp still lists 'Equivalence Ch(K)^op[W^-1] with the defined part; transport' as remaining -- note the ^op, same orientation. A six-step route with every ingredient located is in the survey: crossOnes bijective (crossOnes_injective + crossRun_bijective composed with onesChartEquiv), support at strand count n (isEmpty_runChart), restriction along runBaseAt via CategoryOfElements.isEquivalence_pre as chLocEquivElements does, hom-sets from atomAct_eq_some_iff plus Matsumoto for uniqueness of the reduced positive lift, then locCubeWeakOrder.
(b) THE ORIENTATION MATTERS FOR THE GLUE ROUTE. cubeChartPresentation would present Ch(box n)[W-1]^op, whereas the glue family wants Presents (P d) (((W Zbp).over d).Localization) = Ch(wedge d)[W-1], un-opped. Bridging needs the self-duality of the right weak order (sigma |-> w0 sigma, order-reversing since permLen (w0 sigma) = permLen w0 - permLen sigma), and THE LONGEST ELEMENT IS NOT IN THE REPO -- grep for longest/w0/dual/OrderDual finds nothing relevant. The alternative is to restate the glue machinery on the op, which is a bigger change.

ALSO NOTED: the orient skill's mathlib-reuse table cites Executions/Elements.lean as the Elements-reuse exemplar; that file has only two thinness instances, and the identification Ch K =~ ((wedgeHoms K).Elements)^op lives in ElementsFibration.lean:79. Skill drift, for the user to fix.
BUILT 2026-09-04 — Concurrency/Presentation/SliceFunctor.lean, green, sorry-free, axiom-clean.

  RunOver d := {u : Over d // IsRun Zbp u.left}
  RunOver.push f u := <(Over.map f).obj u.1, u.2>     (the run condition is untouched, so u.2 typechecks as is)
  runPoly d := Polygraph.thin fun a b : RunOver d => PLift (RunStep a b)
  runPolyFunctor : Ch Zbp ⥤ Polygraph      map_id / map_comp = Polygraph.Hom.ext' rfl
  runLabels : SliceLabels runPolyFunctor   ob _ a := a.1, map_ob := rfl

THE SHAPE CAME OUT STRONGER THAN THE SURVEY PREDICTED, and this is the thing to know. The survey said the generator would be 'a position, plus a condition'. It needs NO DATA AT ALL:

  RunStep a b : Prop := exists e (t : a.left --> e) (m : b.left --> e) (z : e --> d),
    permLen (crossPerm rfl t) = 1 AND W Zbp m AND t >> z = a.hom AND m >> z = b.hom

i.e. 'a and b agree after a crosses one pair and b merges' — the atom square, said with arrows. The position is already pinned by the two 0-cells, so carrying it would be exactly what stops the functor laws being rfl.

CONSEQUENCES:
• P.map on 1-cells is RunStep.push, which is the SAME square with z >> f. No permutation is touched.
• So the pivot the bead spent its length on — 'does overMapLoc send atoms to atoms', crossPerm_comp + crossPerm_noDoubleCross, R6.lean — IS NOT NEEDED. It was needed only for a generator indexed by a position in Fin (dimSum d.dims - 1), whose index type varies with d.
• That index type was the real obstacle: dimSum is preserved by arrows of Ch Zbp only PROPOSITIONALLY, so a Fin-indexed generator drags finCongr/Fin.cast through map_id/map_comp. Stating the step by arrows sidesteps it entirely — no transport anywhere in the file.
• crossPerm appears once, as permLen (crossPerm rfl t) = 1, at t's OWN strand count, so no recount either.
• Polygraph.thin is reused rather than a bespoke Polygraph: the localized slice is a poset, so relating every parallel pair is correct and Presents.ofThin will apply downstream.

NAMESPACE TRAP, cost a build: inside namespace ChainCat, 'Hom' resolves to ChainCat.Hom (the Ch K morphisms), not Polygraph.Hom. Spell Polygraph.Hom / Polygraph.Hom.ofPre / Polygraph.Hom.ext' in full.

title: SlicePres A4: Glue, and the theorem that it presents
description:
Read SlicePresentation.md first.  Blocked on A2 and A3.
Wanted: `Glue X P` for `P : D ⥤ Polygraph`, and `Presents (Glue X P) (C[W_C⁻¹])` assuming each `P d` presents `(Over d)[W_D⁻¹]` compatibly.
Shape of `Glue X P`: 0-cells the objects of `∫X`; for each `d`, each `x ∈ X d` and each 1-cell `g : u ⟶ u'` of `P d` (so `u : e ⟶ d`, `u' : e' ⟶ d` in `D`), a 1-cell from `(e, X u x)` to `(e', X u' x)`. 2-cells: those of each copy, plus for each `f : d' ⟶ d`, each `x ∈ X d` and each 1-cell `g` of `P d'`, the relation `(f* x, g) = (x, (P f) g)` — the right-hand side is a word because `Polygraph.Hom` sends a 1-cell to a word.

- `Ψ ⋙ Φ ≅ 𝟭` by `Localization.natTrans_ext` (check after precomposing with `Q`); `Φ ⋙ Ψ ≅ 𝟭` by `Quotient.lift_unique'` (check on generators). Then `Functor.IsEquivalence` from the two isos.

title: SlicePres C3: P presents the localized slices, naturally

So the slice family is the BASE's cells lifted, not a bespoke thin one: a 1-cell is a generator of p acting on a run over d, a 2-cell a relation of p holding there. hP is free for the same reason as before: the 0-cells name their own slice objects (sliceCellOver), and pushing them is Over.map.

The chain that makes it work (all new):
- Machinery/Braid/WeakAction: a DOWNWARD-CLOSED set of permutations carries a partial PosBraid action by length-additive right multiplication. Built with PosBraid.lift, not through Artin.
- Concurrency/Presentation/SliceFibre: the runs over d ARE such a set (exists_runOver_mul_adjT iterated = downward closure), so sliceFibre d is a presheaf on the localized base, and defined(sliceFibre d) is the localized slice REVERSED (a braid raises the weak order; a slice arrow lowers it). Hence the .op in the family.
- Machinery/Presentation/Partial: PartialFam / partialElementsMap — a family of fibre maps that is only LAXLY natural (commutes with the action only where BOTH ends are defined) still gives a morphism of the lifted polygraphs, functorially. Strict naturality is FALSE here: over d=[1,1] the atom is undefined, over d=[2] it is defined.

title: SlicePres A5: GlueOn a generating set
description:
Read SlicePresentation.md first. UNBLOCKED: Cubical-0ws (A4) closed; the 'Blocked on A4' line was stale.

WHY A5 RATHER THAN AN INSTANTIATION OF presentsGlue, settled 2026-09-04. presentsGlue puts a copy of P d at EVERY 0-cell and so needs hb : ∀ d, Bijective (L.ob d), which labelsOf_ob_bijective_iff turns into '(p d).E is bijective on objects'. That FAILS for the slice presentations we have, and not marginally: overSlicePresentation d has 0-cells the runs (a product of Perm (Fin a_i) over the beads) while the objects of ((W Zbp).over (zObj d)).Localization are the objects of Over (zObj d) on the nose (Construction.objEquiv), i.e. ALL refinements of d. At d = [2] that is three objects (the identity of [2], and two arrows [1,1] --> [2] by onesTopEquiv) against two 0-cells. Making the slices bijective instead would mean 0-cells = all refinements, throwing away exactly what Presents.ofThin and Presents.prod bought (one copy of the cube polygraph per bead, with ProdRel.interchange as the 2-cells). Gluing over a generating set keeps the compact presentation; the runs are the generating set.

Wanted: Generating (S : Set C) := ∀ c, ∃ s ∈ S, Nonempty (c ⟶ s); GlueOn S X P with copies of P (F s) only for s in S and overlap relations (s_i, (P a) g) = (s_j, (P b) g) for every span s_i <- e -> s_j in C and every 1-cell g of P (F e), self-spans included; and Generating S -> Presents (GlueOn S X P) (C[W_C^-1]).
Prove it directly with the same universal-property argument as A4, not by comparing with Glue. The content is that an assignment on S extends to a compatible family exactly when the overlap relations hold; spans always exist with apex c itself, which is what makes the extension well defined.
Done when: sorry-free, lake build CubeChains green, debloat pass run.
notes:
FULL, essSurj AND the presentation theorem LANDED. Green 1712 / sweep 1742, sorry-free, GlueOn.lean at 674, Glue.lean +16.

WHAT IS THERE: glueOnDesc_full, glueOnDesc_essSurj (restated), presentsGlueOn. All three take exactly ONE geometric hypothesis, Generating; presentsGlueOn takes in addition the word-problem obligation 'complete' (the Presents.ofDesc shape), which is Cubical-xsm4's target.

CoversUpToW IS GONE, and the reason is the mathematics, not taste. The proof needed a canonical comparison at EVERY object, and CoversUpToW's W-arrow from a covered 0-cell is not canonical -- two objects can be covered from different copies and then nothing compares them. The canonical thing is the BASE 0-CELL: (p d).E is essentially surjective, so choose once, for each d in D, a 0-cell of P d naming the terminal object of Over d (sliceBase / sliceBaseIso), and transport it to c along c's own slice (glueOnBase / glueOnBaseIso). That base 0-cell does NOT depend on which copy you read it in -- gluePt_sliceBase says the reading through any k : c --> elt s is the same -- which is precisely the span-with-apex-c that the overlap 2-cells were built for. Generating then gives Covered (glueOnBase c) for free, and glueOnBaseIso c : Q(elt (glueOnBase c)) =~ Q c gives essential surjectivity. So CoversUpToW was strictly weaker than what was needed AND strictly stronger than what essSurj wanted; it had no remaining role.

THE TRAP THE BEAD WARNED ABOUT was real and this is how it is dodged: 'spelled' conjugates by glueOnBaseIso, which is canonical data fixed before the induction, never a per-case choice, so composition cancels in the middle with no coherence obligation. The Full proof then needs one extra step the plan did not name: a 0-cell v is not its own base, so exists_wordIso_glueOnBase spells the comparison v =~ base(elt v) IN BOTH DIRECTIONS -- possible because (p s.1).E is fully faithful, so Functor.preimageIso turns the slice comparison into an ISO of words.

SHAPE OF THE ARGUMENT (all in one slice, per Generating): sliceBaseOver k is the base cell read under k; glueSliceEval_sliceBaseOver says its image IS glueOnBaseIso, independent of k; exists_word_of_arrow turns any arrow of the slice localization between two such into a word; glueSliceEval_post_map identifies Q.map f with the slice arrow; exists_word_of_Q / exists_word_of_wInv are the two Construction.morphismProperty_eq_top obligations.

title: SlicePres C1: presentations of the localized cube slices
description:
Read SlicePresentation.md first. Blocked on B3 only.

Wanted: `P_cube n` presenting `(Over [n])[W_Z⁻¹]`, and the morphisms induced by maps `[m] ⟶ [n]`, as ONE construction parametrized by the input presentation of the base — not written twice for Garside and Artin, and not waiting on any concrete presentation.

This bead is parametric and must not depend on Phase Z. Take the base presentation as a hypothesis. Phase Z supplies the Garside and Artin instances, and they are consumed at D2, not here. If you find yourself needing a specific presentation to state C1, the parametrization is wrong.

Why this is tractable, and the thing to build on: the slice collapses. `exists_W_from_ones` (Concurrency/Grading/TopBead.lean:76) gives a W-arrow `1ⁿ ⟶ c` for every shape `c` with `dimSum c = n`, and that arrow is automatically a triangle over any `u : c ⟶ [n]`. So every object of `Ch(Z)/[n]` is W-isomorphic to one of the form `(1ⁿ, σ)`, and `onesTopEquiv n` (TopBead.lean:98) says those `σ` are exactly `Perm (Fin n)` — i.e. the generators are the maps `1ⁿ ⟶ [n]`, one per permutation.

Do NOT route this through `IsSegal` or `Hbp`. `Ch(Z)/[n] ≅ Ch(□n)` and `□n` is not Segal, so the descent machinery does not apply and does not need to.

Expect the answer to have the shape of `hLocActionPresentation n : Presents (hLocPoly n) ((PosBraidAction n)ᵒᵖ)` (Concurrency/Presentation/HAction.lean:298) — the Garside simples acting on `Sₙ`. Compare against it as a check; do not derive from it, since that one is produced by the Segal route at `Hbp □n`.

Done when: sorry-free, `lake build CubeChains` green, debloat pass run.
notes:
UPDATED after B3. The concrete input now exists: overEquivWedgeChains : Over (zObj d) ≌ Ch (⋁d) (Concurrency/Merge/WedgeSlice.lean:53) identifies the slice with the chains of the wedge on the nose, and over_W_eq_inverseImage (:58) matches the W classes. So (Over [n])[W⁻¹] is Ch(□n)[W⁻¹]. Expected answer, computed by hand at n=2 and unproved: PosBraidAction n, objects the n! runs, End at a run PosPureBraid n. Consequence to check against hLocActionPresentation: Ch(□n)[W⁻¹] ≌ Ch(Hbp □n)[W⁻¹], i.e. inverting the merges forgets the decoration.
CORRECTION 2026-09-03: my earlier steer was WRONG and is refuted. Ch(box n)[W-inv] is NOT PosBraidAction n. At n=2 both have two objects, but End in PosBraidAction 2 is PosPureBraid 2 (endEquivPosPure, Machinery/Braid/PosAction.lean:43) which contains sigma-1 squared, non-trivial (machine-checked); whereas Ch(box 2)[W-inv] has trivial End by enumeration - objects t=([2],id), r1=([1,1],cubeMerge), r2=([1,1],cubeReorder), arrows r1->t and r2->t only, nothing maps INTO r1 or r2, so inverting the single merge creates no loop. The descent shape is also unavailable: it needs wedgeHoms (box n) to invert merges, and at n=2 that map is one element to two. not_isSegal_cube_two (SegalCondition.lean:422) proves box 2 is not Segal. Expected correct answer: Ch(box n)[W-inv] is the weak order on Perm (Fin n), opposite - a POSET, since Ch(box n) is thin and localizing adds no loops. Braiding comes from gluing slices (A4/A5 overlap relations), not from inside a slice.
C2's SURVEY BEARS ON THIS BEAD, 2026-09-04. Read Cubical-06w's latest note before continuing C1.

Two things. First, C1's 'wanted' has two halves and only the first is done: cubePresentation n exists (CubePresentation.lean:66, Presents.ofThin) but 'the morphisms induced by maps [m] --> [n]' does not, and that half IS C2's input. There is no map CubeStep m -> CubeStep n anywhere in the tree.

Second, C2's survey found that the polygraph's INDEXING is the thing that decides how expensive both beads are, and the current one (slicePoly as a right fold of Polygraph.prod, 0-cells a nested product) is the expensive choice: a morphism d' --> d regroups beads into blocks, so P.map needs a block recursion and the functor coherences become transport rather than rfl. Indexing the 0-cells by the SLICE instead -- {u : Over d // IsRun Zbp u.left}, with P.map := Over.map -- makes both coherences Hom.ext' rfl, because composition in Ch Zbp and Over.map are strictly associative and unital by rfl (machine-checked). It also makes SliceLabels.ob tautological and map_ob rfl, which is what C3 needs.

If that restatement is taken, C1's presentation should be stated at the re-indexed polygraph. cubePresentation's inputs -- cubeEval, exists_run_of_loc_obj, nonempty_path_of_loc_hom -- are already about run-arrows in spirit, so this should be a re-indexing rather than a second proof. Decide the indexing here, before writing more of C1.
RE-INDEXING ATTEMPTED 2026-09-04. ANSWER: THE THREE CUBE INGREDIENTS DO NOT RE-INDEX -- AND SHOULD NOT. Nothing committed; ~99 lines of Lean verified in scratch.

WHAT DOES RE-INDEX, verified and cheap (~35 lines):
• RunOver d := {u : Over d // IsRun Zbp u.left} -- the 0-cells.
• RunOver.equiv (h : dimSum d.dims = N) : RunOver d =~ (zObj (1^N) --> d). The source of a run-arrow is forced to be the run on d's events, so the subtype IS the hom-set out of one fixed run, for every d.
• RunOver.perm h u := crossPerm _ u.1.hom : Perm (Fin N) -- uniform in u because N comes from d, not from u -- and RunOver.perm_injective. A run-arrow is pinned by its crossing permutation.
• locOver_isThin d : Quiver.IsThin (((W Zbp).over d).Localization), general d. Only the wedge version (locSlice_isThin) existed.
Plus, from the C2 survey: Over.map is strictly functorial on Ch Zbp and the prototype functor has map_id and map_comp both Hom.ext' rfl.

WHY THE THREE DO NOT RE-INDEX. cubeEval, nonempty_path_of_loc_hom and exists_run_of_loc_obj are CUBE-level, and the re-indexed C1 is a general-d statement, so there is nothing to re-index them to. And transporting the existing general-d presentation (overSlicePresentation, the Presents.prod induction) into the new indexing is BLOCKED: it needs to know which object of Over (zObj d) each slicePoly 0-cell names, and that runs through locOverEquivWedge, a Localization.uniq flagged opaque on objects at SliceLocalize.lean:82-86. That is the SAME WALL as hP's iso-vs-equality, one level down. Route B is walled at two levels, not one.

BUT THE ROUTE IS BETTER THAN THAT SOUNDS, and this is the finding: Concurrency/Presentation/LocPresentation.lean ALREADY HAS THE GENERAL-d GEOMETRY that the cube ingredients are the special case of. I missed this file in the first survey.
• exists_atom_step (:253) -- the atom step at GENERAL d, with 'cut k is interior to d' spelled arrow-theoretically as Nonempty (zObj (atomComp N k) --> d). No boundaries bookkeeping. This is the hard geometric input and it is done.
• exists_leg (:236), exists_merge_leg (:366), atomLoop_comm (:374), atomLoop_braid (:396), artin_of_codim_two (:437).
• exists_W_ones (:41) -- essential surjectivity, general d.
• exists_atomWord (:505) -- the permLen induction, at the top; the model for the slice version.
So the re-indexed C1 SUPERSEDES cubePresentation and overSlicePresentation rather than re-indexing them, and it does so with geometry that already exists.

THE ONE REMAINING UNKNOWN, and it is the size-determining one. Fullness needs the permLen induction on exists_atom_step. The cube's version (nonempty_path_of_loc_hom) feeds exists_word a WEAK ORDER comparison from weakClass_le_of_loc_hom (CubeWeakOrder.lean:299), which has NO general-d analogue. The LENGTH half is available generally -- Machinery/Grading.lean's deg_le_of_loc_hom applied to a general-d crossOver/degOver, the analogue of CubeCrossing's cross/crossLen. Whether the induction needs the weak order or only the length is what I cannot settle without doing it, and it is the difference between a bounded job and a second CubeWeakOrder.
PROBE RESULT 2026-09-04: LENGTH ALONE IS NOT ENOUGH, AND THE GAP IS EXACTLY ONE STATEMENT. Sorry-free, verified in scratch, nothing committed.

WHAT THE LENGTH GRADING DOES GIVE, general d, no hypothesis (~40 lines, first try):
• crossOver h y := crossPerm _ y.hom -- how much an object of the slice has braided, its own arrow to the top of the slice. CubeCrossing.cross at an arbitrary base.
• degOver, degOver_eq_add (permLen_crossPerm_comp at the top), degOver_le, degOver_eq_of_W, and degOver_loc : an arrow of the localized slice never raises the crossing count. That is Machinery/Grading's deg_le_of_loc_hom; nothing in it is about the cube.

AND THE INDUCTION GOES THROUGH ON THAT ALONE, GIVEN ONE HYPOTHESIS. nonempty_path_of_over_hom compiles: 0-cells RunOver d, 1-cells RunStep (an INTERIOR cut at which the run-arrow descends, interiority spelled arrow-theoretically as Nonempty (zObj (atomComp N k) --> d), exactly exists_atom_step's own hypothesis), and the recursion terminates because a descent drops permLen by one (permLen_mul_adjT_of_descent). The base case is RunOver.perm_injective.

THE ONE MISSING INPUT, named: ExchangeStep. Given an arrow Q a --> Q b of the localized slice with perm a != perm b, SOME INTERIOR DESCENT of a leads to an a' still lying over b. degOver_loc bounds lengths and says nothing about WHICH descent keeps b below; that is the weak order.

REVISED ESTIMATE, and it is better than 'a second CubeWeakOrder': the gap is ONE exchange lemma, not an order theory. Everything else in fullness is discharged. Whether that lemma is cheap is a further question, but the scope is pinned to a single statement.
EXCHANGESTEP DECOMPOSED, 2026-09-04; two of four pieces in hand.

CORRECTION TO MY OWN STATEMENT. ExchangeStep as I wrote it last round is CIRCULAR: it demands an ARROW Q a' --> Q b, and getting one from the order needs the converse 'order implies hom', which is fullness again (at the cube that is nonempty_loc_hom, CubeWeakEquiv.lean:52). The induction must carry the WEAK ORDER RELATION, not the arrow: prove nonempty_path_of_le (hle : weakOver b <= weakOver a), then fullness follows by (A) below.

(A) DONE AND VERIFIED (scratch): weakOver_le_of_loc_hom at general d -- an arrow of the localized slice descends the weak order. crossOver_eq_mul, weakOver, weakOver_le, weakOver_eq_of_W, weakFunctorOver, weakFunctorOver_inverts. This is CubeWeakOrder's weakClass/weakFunctor/weakLoc/weakClass_le_of_loc_hom transferred VERBATIM with crossOver for cross; nothing in it was about the cube. Fifth time this session a cube proof turned out general.

(B) DONE, ALREADY IN THE TREE: WeakOrder.exists_cover_of_lt (CubeWeakOrder.lean:216) -- below and not equal means below a lower cover, giving the descent k with of tau <= of (sigma * adjT k). The whole WeakOrder namespace is pure permutation combinatorics despite living in a cube-named file.

(D) REDUCES TO (C). Given (C), exists_factor (Coarser.lean:388) splits a.hom through zObj (atomComp N k), and eq_mergeOnes_or_atomOnes (LocPresentation.lean:102) says the run-arrow leg is the merge or the atom; a descent at k forces the atom, so a.hom = atomOnes N k >> e and a' := mergeOnes N k >> e has crossPerm e = sigma * adjT k. All ingredients exist.

(C) IS THE ONE REMAINING UNKNOWN: a crossing of perm a at k forces k to be INTERIOR to d, i.e. Nonempty (zObj (atomComp N k) --> d). Geometrically 'two events in different beads of d never cross'. Via nonempty_hom_iff this is boundaries d.dims subset boundaries (atomComp N k), i.e. k+1 not in boundaries d.dims. Candidate inputs: crossPerm_chConcat (the crossing over a wedge concat is the block sum permSum), index_lt_of_index_lt and nonempty_hom_of_index (ChartHom.lean:512, :521). Not yet located as a lemma.
EXCHANGESTEP DONE 2026-09-04 — the family p exists, unconditionally, and the glue route's only remaining hypothesis is the word problem. New module Concurrency/Presentation/SliceExchange.lean (379 lines), green, sorry-free, axiom-clean.

(A) LANDED VERBATIM from the scratch prototype, no changes needed: over_left_dimSum, crossOver, degOver, degOver_eq_add/le/eq_of_W/loc, crossOver_eq_mul, weakOver, weakOver_le, weakOver_eq_of_W, weakFunctorOver, weakFunctorOver_inverts, weakOver_le_of_loc_hom. CubeWeakOrder at an arbitrary base; sixth time a cube proof turned out general.

(C) IS PROVED, AND IT IS ONE LEMMA, NOT A SEARCH:
  index_crossPerm (hd : dimSum d.dims = N) (hc : dimSum c.dims = N) (a : c --> d) (r) :
    index_{d.dims} (crossPerm hc a r) = index_{d.dims} r
'an arrow permutes each block of its target and no more'. Proof: read the target in its OWN standard chart. Then crossPerm_flatten says the source's firing order inverts crossPerm (flatten_stdChart = 1), and beadOf_of_hom (CubeFaces.lean:86) says a coarsening's beads are the target's blocks read in that order; beadOf_stdChart closes it. Six lines.
NOTE THE HYPOTHESIS I DID NOT NEED: the source need not be a run. The proof never uses the source's shape, so it is stated for any c --> d.
Then index_adj_eq_of_descent (descent at k puts k and k+1 in one block, by index_monotone both ways) and nonempty_atomComp_of_descent (that IS the arrow, via nonempty_hom_of_index + eq_adj_of_index_eq). The candidate crossPerm_chConcat was NOT needed.

(D) IS ALSO ONE LEMMA, and it did not go through exists_factor / eq_mergeOnes_or_atomOnes as the plan expected:
  exists_run_mul_adjT : at a descent, exists a' with crossPerm a' = crossPerm a * adjT k
by exists_crossPerm_of_blocks (ChartHom.lean:379) — REALISE the shortened permutation directly. Its hrise is vacuous at the run (index_ones is injective) and its hface follows from index_crossPerm plus 'distinct blocks are ordered by their members' (index_lt_iff_lt, new, two lines from index_monotone). The only pair adjT k reorders is {k,k+1}, which (C) puts in one block, so the block condition survives. Shorter and more direct than the factor-then-classify route.

THE REST: runStep_of_descent bridges to SliceFunctor's arrow-theoretic RunStep via exists_atom_step at the ASCENT (perm a' ascends at k exactly when perm a descends), nonempty_path_of_le is the permLen induction carrying the WEAK ORDER (not an arrow — the circularity the earlier note flagged), exists_runOver_iso is runMerge inverted, and runPresentation assembles them with Presents.ofThin since locOver_isThin makes the slice a poset.

ALSO NEW, both general: eq_adjT_of_permLen_eq_one (Machinery/Braid/Generated.lean — NOT Artin.lean beside permLen_adjT as suggested: Artin cannot reach exists_adjacent_descent, which lives in Generated and imports it) and permLen_crossPerm_recount.

title: mathlib names this repo keeps re-proving (Fin/Composition)
description: PLACEHOLDER

comments.author: zstone
comments.text: RECURRING BLOCKER (has now defeated three attempted reuses): mathlib packages these facts inside an OrderEmbedding and never exposes the underlying value. Composition.boundary is built by OrderEmbedding.ofStrictMono with only boundary_zero and boundary_last stated -- there is no (c.boundary i : N) = c.sizeUpTo i to rewrite with, so Composition.boundaries = univ.map boundary cannot be evaluated without unfolding ofStrictMono by hand. Same shape blocked beadStart_lt_beadStart (the strict monotonicity is sealed inside Composition.boundary) and boundaries_ones. Ingredients that DO exist and still do not help: Composition.ones, ones_blocks, ones_sizeUpTo, ones_length, Fin.map_valEmbedding_univ. Conclusion: for anything about boundary VALUES, write it locally against sizeUpTo; do not re-attempt the transport.

comments.author: zstone
comments.text: FORMAL-INVERSE QUIVERS (checked against mathlib, answer is: write it locally, but know these). Mathlib HAS: Localization.Construction.LocQuiver W -- structure wrapping the objects, Hom A B := (A.obj -> B.obj) + {f : B.obj -> A.obj // W f} -- and Localization.Construction.relations with constructors id/comp/Winv1/Winv2, and Quiver.Symmetrify (the same shape at S = top, as a type synonym) with of/lift/lift_spec/lift_unique and the HasReverse / HasInvolutiveReverse classes. NEITHER can be reused for a formal-inverse quiver on a bare Quiver V with a predicate on EDGES. Two independent obstructions. (1) LocQuiver needs [Category C] and a MorphismProperty; the only category around a quiver is Paths V, and LocQuiver on Paths V takes ALL PATHS as forward edges and adjoins inverses to paths -- that is precisely the coarse presentation (all arrows of C, modulo functoriality) that a generating-quiver presentation exists to refine. (2) Symmetrify.lift requires [HasReverse V'] on the TARGET, i.e. every arrow of the target must have a designated reverse; targets here are arbitrary categories in which only the images of S-edges are invertible. InvQuiver S is a proper subquiver of Symmetrify V and mathlib has no subquiver former. ALSO NOT IN MATHLIB: any Tietze reduction of a localization presentation to a generating quiver. Note Functor.IsLocalization L W is BY DEFINITION 'L inverts W and Construction.lift L is an equivalence', so proving IsLocalization IS the comparison with mathlib's presentation; IsLocalization.mk' + Localization.StrictUniversalPropertyFixedTarget is the intended route and there is no lighter one (Quotient.isLocalization_functor in Localization/OfQuotient needs model-category cylinder objects). See Machinery/Localization/PresentedLocalization.lean.

comments.author: zstone
comments.text: CALCULUS OF FRACTIONS / ZIGZAGS -- mathlib HAS this, do not hand-roll a fraction type. CategoryTheory/Localization/CalculusOfFractions.lean plus the CalculusOfFractions/ subdirectory (Fractions, ComposableArrows, OfAdjunction, Preadditive). Available: MorphismProperty.LeftFraction W X Y (a structure: an object Y', f : X -> Y', s : Y -> Y', hs : W s -- i.e. f followed by s-inverse, ONE ZAG), RightFraction (the mirror), LeftFraction.ofHom / ofInv / map / map_comp_map_s / cases, LeftFractionRel with refl/symm/trans and equivalenceLeftFractionRel, Localization.Hom W X Y := Quot LeftFractionRel with Hom.mk / mk_surjective / homMk_eq_iff_leftFractionRel, comp/comp_eq, the model category Localization W with its Q and Qinv, and the classes HasLeftCalculusOfFractions / HasRightCalculusOfFractions (each extends IsMultiplicative; the first has exists_leftFraction, the Ore condition, plus an ext/cancellation axiom). HANDEDNESS FOR Ch Zbp: arrows run fine -> coarse and the merges W run the same way, so a LeftFraction from 1^n to 1^n is exactly 'two maps out of the run into a common shape, the second a merge' = a one-zag element of End 1^n. LEFT is the correct handedness; RightFraction would want a merge INTO the source. CAUTION: HasLeftCalculusOfFractions must FAIL for W Zbp -- under it Localization.Hom.mk_surjective makes every morphism a single fraction and the Garside canonical length collapses to 1. Do not try to instantiate it.

comments.author: zstone
comments.text: GARSIDE HEIGHT: after the monoid-route deletion the tree has the VOCABULARY and none of the CONTENT. On the record so it is not rediscovered. The only three witnesses that height > 1 is attained were locOf_ne_atomLoc_sq (sigma_i squared lies in the localized monoid but is the class of no arrow), length_eq_permLen_crossPermN (every atom-word for locOf f has exactly permLen (crossPermN f) letters) and wStrands_iff_permLen (a refinement is a merge exactly when permLen = 0). All three lived in ArtinRelations/GarsideChains via LocMonoid (WStrands Zbp n), all three die with LocalizationMonoid.lean, and none was ever phrased as a LeftFraction statement. Note also they were phrased at the TOP object [n], not at the base point 1^n that goals 1-2 are based at, so they would have needed rebasing anyway. The Ore condition is ruled to fail (user: 'obviously there is no calculus of fractions') -- if it held, Localization.Hom.mk_surjective would make every morphism one fraction and the height would be identically <= 1. Restate height against mathlib's LeftFraction at 1^n; do not hand-roll a fraction type.

title: IsLocal and IsSegal restated on mathlib's ObjectProperty.isLocal
description:
`CubeChains/Chains/SegalCondition.lean` defines `IsLocal K w := Function.Bijective (fun f : B.toPsh ⟶ K => w.hom ≫ f)` and hand-proves its closure lemmas. Mathlib v4.30.0 already has this notion, as a Galois-connected pair:

- `CategoryTheory.MorphismProperty.isLocal (W) : ObjectProperty C` — `Mathlib/CategoryTheory/ObjectProperty/Local.lean`; `isLocal_single_iff_bijective` is literally the project definition at `MorphismProperty.single w.hom`.
- `CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.isLocal (P) : MorphismProperty C` — `Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Localization/Bousfield.lean`; at `ObjectProperty.singleton K` it is the same predicate read in `w`.

Wanted: the project notions stated on those, so that the following stop being hand-proved —
`IsLocal.of_isIso` (= `ObjectProperty.isLocal_of_isIso`), `isLocal_congr`/`IsLocal.congr` and `IsLocal.of_unit_tensor`/`of_tensor_unit` (= the `RespectsIso` instance + `MorphismProperty.arrow_mk_iso_iff`), `IsLocal.of_iso` (= the `IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms` instance), `precompIso`/`postcompIso` (= `ObjectProperty.isLocal.homEquiv`), and `isSegal_iff_isLocal_cubeMerge` (= `MorphismProperty.isLocal_iSup`). `IsMultiplicative` and `HasTwoOutOfThreeProperty` in `w` come free.

Blocker to weigh: neither mathlib form is defeq to the bare `Function.Bijective`, so a bridge lemma is needed and every `h.1`/`h.2` call site goes through it. `IsLocal.tensor_id`/`IsLocal.id_tensor` have no mathlib counterpart either way (they need the wedge pushout).

Not covered by mathlib and noted separately: `tensor_id`/`id_tensor` are two 26-line mirrored proofs with no symmetry to exploit (`(BPSet, ∨)` has no braiding); both are instances of "locality is stable under cobase change", which `Glue.isPushout` + `IsPushout.of_top` would supply.
close_reason: Done: IsLocal is now ObjectProperty.isLocal (singleton K); IsSegal is locality at wedgeToTensor. The tensor_id/id_tensor pushout idea remains open — refiled.

title: No star for the merges on Ch (Hbp Zbp) in degree n >= 2
description:
Wanted: IsEmpty (Star (WinfHn n) x) for every x, when n >= 2 — the mirror of CubeChains.isEmpty_costar_cube (Salvetti/RunClassifier.lean), on the OTHER side of the interval and for the point rather than the cube.

Reason to expect it: a Winf arrow out of the one-bead chain forces the target to be the one-bead chain with the identity wedge map (blockIdx is surjective, so the target has at most one bead, and Ch is rigid there), hence x.map is pinned to the source's own decoration. The one-bead chains of Hbp Zbp carry n! decorations, so no single x serves them all.

Consequence: Ch (Hbp Zbp) degree n has a Costar (costarOnesH) but no Star, so GarsidePresentation.locEquivGarside — which needs both ends of the interval — does not apply to it. NOT VERIFIED; the argument above is a sketch.

title: No product splitting of wedgeHoms (Hbp box n) for every n
description:
Wanted: for every n >= 2, IsEmpty (ProductSplitting (box n)) given InvertsMerges (Hbp.obj (box n)) — i.e. the statement of CubeChains.isEmpty_splitting_of_invertsMerges_cube_two (Salvetti/RunClassifier.lean) at every n, not only n = 2.

not_invertsMerges_of_splitting currently needs a point of Hom(wedge[1+1], K), which for K = box n exists only at n = 2 (a chain of box n has dimSum = n). The general case needs the merge mergeHom l r 1 1 spliced inside a longer all-edges word, so that the source shape is 1^n and the target has one square.

title: Sn acts on H(cube n) but not on cube n x runPresheaf — the discriminator
description: salCompare does NOT distinguish the two candidate models for complexification: its hypotheses mention only Ch K and Lines K, and both H(K) and K x runPresheaf have the same Ch*, so nothing at the level of Ch, Ch* or the Salvetti poset can tell them apart. The discriminator is the arrangement's symmetry group. Wanted, and being built: (a) symFree of a cube is representable, symFree (cube n) iso yoneda (sbox n); (b) hence Perm (Fin n) = Aut (sbox n) acts on H(cube n) by PRECUBICAL AUTOMORPHISMS, via Yoneda upstairs restricted along J — an action that moves faces, witnessed by the two 2-cells of H(cube 2) having different (eps,i)-faces; (c) the product model cannot carry it: prodFst to cube n is a BPSet map, Box is rigid so Aut (cube n) is trivial (Box.endo_eq_id), hence any automorphism of the product over prodFst induces the identity on Ch (cube n) and can only permute chambers — whereas salReorient acts non-trivially on Face (braidCOM n). Deferred: full equivariance of Ch (Hbp cube n) with (Sal (braidCOM n))op against salReorient, which needs linesTopeIso. The moral: the symmetries Box refuses to have are exactly what H supplies. Box is rigid by design (that is why the braiding must be created by passing to executions); H(cube n) is rigid no longer because sBox put the symmetries back, and the resulting action is the arrangement's. The product keeps cube n as a factor and inherits its rigidity — it can decorate cells with chambers but can never move a cell.

title: When K has a COM L, is H(K) its complexification? (the runs-are-topes hypothesis)
description: Not every precubical set has a COM; the question is conditional. Wanted: whenever K carries a COM L, Ch (Hbp K) ≌ (Sal L)op. This is provable in general from existing machinery, because BOTH sides are categories of elements: Ch* K = (Lines K).Elements with Lines K a the runs refining the chain a, and salElementsEquiv gives Sal L ≌ (salFunctor L).Elements with salFunctor L X the topes above the face X. So given (1) an equivalence e : (Ch K)op ≌ Face L and (2) a natural iso Lines K ≅ e.functor followed-by salFunctor L, the conclusion follows by mapEquivalence, then preEquivalenceComp, then salElementsEquiv — three steps, all in Salvetti/Elements.lean. Hence the ENTIRE content of the complexification claim is hypothesis (2): the runs refining a chain are exactly the topes above its face. The Salvetti pairing X ⊑ T and the wall-crossing rule T' = X' o T are then automatic. Corollary worth taking on elegance grounds: braidSalEquiv (currently a bespoke ~100 line construction in SalExec with salExecData/execSal round trips) becomes the instance at K = cube n, L = braidCOM n, with (1) from chFaceCatEquiv and (2) from wordTopeEquiv plus isRun_of_isTope.
notes: CORRECTION: salCompare (landed in Salvetti/SalCompare.lean) does not answer this bead's question. Its hypotheses mention only Ch K and Lines K, so it applies verbatim to BOTH H(K) and K x runPresheaf — it is a theorem about executions, not about complexification. It earns its keep by making braidSalEquiv a corollary. The model-distinguishing statement is the Sn-equivariance one.

title: Ch X is a full subcategory of the slice BPSet/X
description: An object of Ch X is a serial wedge together with a map to X, and a morphism is a wedge map commuting over X — i.e. Ch X is the full subcategory of the slice BPSet/X cut out by the serial-wedge domains. Consequence worth exploiting: a functor Ch X to Ch Y does NOT need a presheaf map X to Y, only a natural iso between the hom-functors restricted to serial wedges. That is strictly weaker, and it is why Ch (H K) can be equivalent to Ch (K.prod runBp) even though there is no presheaf map H K to K at all (the projection forgetting the permutation is not natural, because H restricts the K-component along the twisted face). Wanted: the slice description recorded, and an assessment of whether stating Ch this way shortens the refinement machinery in Chains/Correspondence.

title: The eqToHom load comes from indexing chains by a computed dims list
description: 164 eqToHom in the tree, 41 in Chains/Correspondence alone, plus the permCast family in Salvetti. One root cause: dependent types indexed by COMPUTED data. Ch K stores (dims : List PNat, map : wedge dims --> K), so two chains with propositionally equal dims have different wedge types and every construction that computes a dims list needs eqToHom (congrArg serialWedge h); Correspondence carries bpset_eqToHom_hom, eqToHom_type_apply and map_eqToHom_op_cell purely as transport plumbing. The same cause gives permCast: permOf flattens events to Fin (dimSum dims) so that comparing two orderings lands in a GROUP, and at the unflattened beadEvent level there is no transport at all (eventEquiv is an honest equivalence). CubeChain (a cube list) is transport-free and chCubes proves it equivalent to Ch. Wanted: an assessment of whether making the cube list the primary definition removes the plumbing, or merely moves it.

title: H is complexification: an H-cell is a cell plus a chamber of its local braid arrangement
description: H(K)(box n) = Perm (Fin n) × K(box n), and wordTopeEquiv : Perm (Fin n) ≃ Tope n says a permutation IS a tope of braidCOM n. So an H-cell is an n-cell of K decorated with a chamber of its own local braid arrangement, which is the cellwise Salvetti decoration; Ch assembles the local chambers into global Salvetti cells. The evidence that this is not a coincidence: H's restriction sends the pair (sigma, y) along a face delta to (tau, K psi y) where J delta followed by symHom sigma equals symHom tau followed by J psi, so tau is sigma restricted to the face — and SalExec already proves wordTope (runWord y) = (chFace y.chain).1 composed-with wordTope (runWord x), i.e. Salvetti's second clause T' = X' o T. The sBox unique factorization IS the tope composition, read through wordTopeEquiv. This also explains why H K is a TWISTED product and not K x H Z: a trivial bundle would mean the chamber restricts independently of the cell. Note the dimension shift: it is Ch(H K), not H K, that is the Salvetti complex. For the cube this follows from conjecture 2 composed with braidSalEquiv. For general K there is no COM at all, which suggests H is the right general definition of complexification for precubical sets.

title: Ch (H K) ≌ (Ch⋆ K)ᵒᵖ, via the twist (H K is NOT a product)
description: The title premise is FALSE: H K is not the product K ⨯ H Z. H's restriction along a face sends (σ, y) to (τ, K ψ y) where J δ ≫ symHom σ = symHom τ ≫ J ψ — the K component is restricted along the σ-twisted face ψ, not along δ. Counterexample: in H(□²) the two 2-cells id and swap have different faces (δ at (ε,i) versus δ at (ε, swap i)), while the two 2-cells of □² ⨯ H(Z) have identical faces; an iso would force δ_{ε,0} = δ_{ε,1}. What remains wanted: Ch (H K) ≌ (Ch⋆ K)ᵒᵖ, via the twist. Objects match because extremal vertices are symmetry-invariant (J v ≫ symHom σ = J v). Morphisms correspond by φ ↦ boxPart (J φ ≫ β) with β the target's run, a bijection because t_β is invertible; functoriality is J (φ ≫ φ') ≫ γ = α ≫ J (ψ ≫ ψ'), i.e. associativity in sBox. Ch⋆ K ≅ (Ch (K.prod runBp))ᵒᵖ is already proved (chStarProdIso).
close_reason: chSymChStarEquiv (K : BPSet) : Ch (Hbp.obj K) ≌ (Ch⋆ K)ᵒᵖ in Salvetti/ChStarSym.lean — unconditional, no NonSelfLinked, no AdmitsAltitude. Via chSymEquiv : Ch (Hbp.obj K) ≌ Ch (K.prod runBp) composed with chStarProdEquiv. The object correspondence INVERTS the bead permutation (matching (sigma,y) with run sigma is not an equivalence; witness in the file's docs), justified by the new SHom.sortPerm_sortFace_inv. The twist is und (phi followed by symOf rho) and its functoriality is associativity plus uniqueness of the factorization.
