title: C creates the braiding: monoidality over the geometric tensor
description: ARCHITECTURE records that (GeoBP, geo-tensor) is monoidal with NO swap -- Box is rigid, so no block transposition exists -- and that the braiding is created by the passage to executions. The crisp form of that: C is a BRAIDED monoidal functor out of a merely monoidal source, i.e. C(X tensor Y) carries a braiding that X tensor Y does not. The shuffle statement (Ch of a geometric tensor decomposes as pairs of chains plus their interleavings) is then exactly the monoidality of C, and 'maximally braided' is the claim that the braiding on C(X tensor Y) is FREE -- generated by the interleavings, with no relations beyond those each factor already has. Checkable at the bottom: square = interval tensor interval, and End(run) = N is free on one generator, already verified in Testing/CubeC3 and by hand for the square. Distinguish this from subdivision: subdivision substitutes into ORDERED slots, so everything in one bead precedes everything in the next, and the only mixing across cables is what the outer braid does. Subdivision is operadic composition; the geometric tensor is the tensor. cubeTensorIso (Foundations/GeoTensor/Cube.lean:105) already gives that the tensor of cubes is a cube, and is currently unused.
notes:
REFUTED for the strong version, using only facts already verified. C (cube 1) is the terminal category: Ch (cube 1) has exactly one object, since dims are positive so there are no vertex-only chains, hence one object in ECh*, no codimension-one morphisms, no moves. Same for C (cube 0), which is the tensor unit. So C (cube 1) is isomorphic to the unit. cubeTensorIso gives cube 1 tensor cube n = cube (n+1), so strong monoidality would give C (cube (n+1)) = C(cube 1) tensor C(cube n) = C (cube n) for every n -- but C (cube 2) has 3 objects and C (cube 3) has 13, the latter machine-checked in Testing/CubeC3. So C is NOT a strong monoidal functor from the geometric tensor to any monoidal structure on Cat. Lax monoidality is not refuted by this, since the comparison map need not be invertible, but it is much weaker than 'the braiding is created' and no canonical comparison is evident (given a chain of X and one of Y, which interleaving?). The formulation that matches the phenomenon is GENERATION, not equivalence: C(X tensor Y) is generated by the images of C(X) and C(Y) together with the interleaving braidings. Equivalence would say there is no excess; the excess is exactly the braiding. Any future formulation must account for C (cube n) growing with n rather than quotient it away.
CORRECTION to the framing. 'Braided monoidal functor' is the wrong shape: the source has no braiding at all -- Box is rigid, the geometric tensor has no swap -- so there is no braiding for a functor to respect, and the phrase is vacuous or ill-typed. The refutation above is unaffected and applies to STRONG monoidality alone, for any target whose unit is terminal. LAX monoidality is untouched and remains open; the honest gap is that no canonical comparison map is evident (given a chain of X and one of Y, which interleaving?). REFORMULATION that makes this the same statement as Cubical-zmi.13: iterating cubeTensorIso gives cube n = (cube 1) tensored n times, and C (cube 1) is terminal, so everything in C (cube n) is created by the tensor. The claim is then that C (cube n) is the FREE braided structure on n trivial objects, which is the braid operad's arity-n piece reached from the tensor side rather than the cabling side. 'Maximally braided' is freeness, and it is falsifiable: at n = 2 it says End(run) = N free on one generator, verified; at n = 3 it says the relations are exactly the braid relations, machine-checked in Testing/CubeC3. Note this does NOT depend on lax monoidality -- the operad statement stands alone, so the geometric tensor is an alternative description rather than a prerequisite.
DOWNGRADED to P2 and off the critical path. A clean presentation of Ch(X geo-tensor Y) for general X, Y is not expected: the wedge is clean because its two halves do not interact, giving a product, whereas the tensor is shuffles, whose interleavings grow combinatorially with no evident canonical generating set. Nothing on the path needs it. The operad's cabling only ever tensors CUBES, and cubeTensorIso (cube m tensor cube n = cube (m+n)) is already proved and clean. So keep the cube-level tensor, and treat the general presentation as an open curiosity rather than a prerequisite. What freeness actually needs is the presentation, not the tensor: 'C (cube n) is free braided on n generators' has no referent until the generators are named, and that is Cubical-zmi.30 section 3 -- the atoms out of a run should be the n-1 adjacent transpositions, with braid and commutation the only surviving relations. In cube 3 that is visible: 4 length-one moves per run collapse to 2 under the parallel-pair relations, and the length-two moves factor into them.

title: Mazurkiewicz traces: runs are linearizations, arrows are path names
description:
Results wanted:
* Runs of K are exactly the linearizations of the Mazurkiewicz trace of K, made precise for precubical K.
* Two runs are connected in B(K) iff they linearize the same trace, so pi_0 of B(K) is the set of traces -- trace theory recovered as the pi_0 shadow.
* An arrow of B(K) is a NAME for a path between two linearizations, and the braid is that name. Distinct arrows between the same pair of runs are distinct names, which is exactly what trace theory discards.
* A statement of the form: trace equivalence is pi_0, and the braid group is pi_1.

title: n |-> B(cube n) is an operad, and it is braid cabling
description:
Results wanted:
* An operad structure on n |-> B(cube n): substitution B(cube k) x prod_i B(cube n_i) --> B(cube (sum n_i)).
* Substitution is built from the geometric tensor, together with the block permutations that reindex the events.
* The operad agrees with the classical cabling operad on braids, under the equivalence B(cube n) = positive braids.
* Unit, associativity and equivariance laws.

Braid/Sum.lean already has the block-diagonal permSum and braidSum, and the fact that crossing counts add over disjoint blocks; that is the arity-2 shadow of this.
notes:
The localization is the bridge. C(K) = ECh*(K)[W^-1] has cabling patterns (chains) as objects and braidings plus cablings as morphisms, so it is the natural home of the braid operad. W is 'same attached data, different base', so inverting it makes a braiding independent of the subdivision that witnessed it -- which is exactly what permOf_noDoubleCross says at degree 0, where the well-definedness of Conc IS this statement one degree down. Consequence worth stating: loc_isLocalization implies the labelling functor of Cubical-zmi.35 is well defined, so the operad structure is a corollary of the localization rather than a separate construction.
Evidence from Testing/CubeC3.lean: in C(cube 3) the generators split 42 degree-preserving (cable swaps) and 42 degree-dropping (cablings), and of the 78 relations 30 are entirely among the first kind, 18 entirely among the second, 6 vacuous, and 24 mixed. The mixed family is the equivariance between the two operations and is where the braided-operad structure lives; a product of a braid structure and an operad structure would have none.
TARGET STATEMENT, sharpened. Cubes give PURE braids: End of C-zero (cube n) at a run is the positive pure braid monoid, verified as N = P2+ for the square and as P3+ for the 3-cube (Testing/CubeC3). The FULL braid group lives at Zbp, where events carry no axis names (runWedgeEquivChStarZbp). So the cube-indexed family is the positive braid CATEGORY -- objects the permutations, homs positive braids, machine-checked at n = 3 as the Artin/Deligne category of B3 with the Cayley graph of S3 as generators -- and the comparison should be stated against that, not against n |-> B n as a family of groups.
CABLING HALF DONE (Operad/CubeCable.lean): cableCh w hw : Ch (cube k) => Ch (cube N) and its strict descent ECh.cable w hw : C (cube k) => C (cube N), unconditional, with cableCh_of_one and cableCh_cableCh (the operad unit and associativity laws for the cabling half). Zero widths included.

BLOCKED, and the blocker is mathematical, not engineering: the two-variable comp (P k x prod_i P (w i) => P N) has no known object formula satisfying all three axioms.
  * comp_unit_right forces comp(x; pt,...,pt) = x, so the slots may not be laid out sequentially inside a bead of x: the formula 'concatenate the slots (cSubstList), then cable x' returns the sequential chain of cube k when every slot is a point, not x. cSubst appends dims, so its bead count is additive, while cabling must keep the bead count of x.
  * The only formula compatible with both unit laws is lock-step (levelwise) merging: rank(p) = (rank_x (block p), rank_{y_i} (offset p)) read lexicographically. It fails comp_assoc. Witness, N = 4, x = the one-bead chain of cube 2, y0 = (a0 < a1), y1 = pt, then z = (b0 < b1) into the third slot:
      gamma(gamma(x; y0, pt); pt, pt, z) = {a0,b0} < {b1} < {a1}
      gamma(x; gamma(y0; pt,pt), gamma(pt; z)) = gamma(x; y0, z) = {a0,b0} < {a1,b1}
    and the axiom demands these agree. The cause is structural: after the first substitution the sub-levels of y0 have become levels of the intermediate chain, so the second substitution refines below them instead of aligning with them; any lexicographic-type rule fails the same way.
  Not settled: whether some other object formula works, i.e. whether a set-operad structure exists on ordered set partitions with these units. Both unit laws hold for the cabling alone, so the obstruction is entirely in how two concurrent slots interleave -- which is exactly where the braiding lives.

comments.author: zstone
comments.text:
The substitution maps exist AT THE Ch LEVEL at 99ac0b5: chSubst m n : Ch (cube m) x Ch (cube n) => Ch (cube (m+n)) and chSubstList, from lax monoidality read through cubeTensorIsoBP (previously unused). Machine-checked at the bottom: the two beads of chSubst 1 1 have sign vectors *0 and 1*, the sequential run of the square.

THE OUTER FACTOR IS A STRUCTURAL OBSTRUCTION, not a gap in effort. Lax monoidality supplies exactly the product of the inner factors, prod_i C(cube n_i) --> C(cube N). It cannot supply the C(cube k) factor, and neither can functoriality of C, because THERE IS NO MAP OF PRECUBICAL SETS BETWEEN cube k AND cube N IN EITHER DIRECTION when k < N:
- cube k --> cube N in BPSet is a sign vector in {*,0,1}^N with k stars; app_init forces every non-star entry to 0 and app_final forces every non-star entry to 1, so the vector is all stars and k = N.
- cube N --> cube k in PrecubicalSet is an N-cell of cube k, i.e. Hom_Box of the two, empty for N > k since Box has no degeneracies.
CAVEAT: these are Box.sign computations done on paper, NOT machine-checked.

So cabling C(cube k) --> C(cube N) is genuinely EXTRA STRUCTURE. Its natural home is the sign-vector level: Box is the free strict monoidal category on an interval, a morphism being a word in {*,0,1}^k, and cabling repeats letter i exactly n_i times. UNIFORM width is a strict monoidal endofunctor of Box and would give cabling for free; variable widths need the coloured version, a different category.

FURTHER CAVEAT, a hypothesis rather than a result: even granting cabling, there may be no canonical object-level substitution when an outer bead has more than one element -- inside a concurrent outer bead the inner subdivisions must be shuffled, and the geo tensor has no swap to choose the shuffle. The one unital and associative choice found is 'lockstep', which is pure index arithmetic. The alternative that IS canonical is to restrict the arities to RUNS, where substitution is the block permutation sigma[tau_1..tau_k] -- already permSum/braidSum in Braid/Sum.lean.

comments.author: zstone
comments.text:
CORRECTION and machine-check, at 1dc0922. Both claims are TRUE and now proved in Foundations/CubeRigid.lean, but the SUMMARY SENTENCE I recorded above is FALSE.

'There is no map of precubical sets between cube k and cube N in either direction' is wrong: at the PRESHEAF level every face inclusion is such a map. nonempty_cubePsh_hom_iff : Nonempty ((cube k).toPsh --> (cube N).toPsh) iff k <= N.

The obstruction is ASYMMETRIC:
- BPSet.cubePsh_dim_le (N <= k for a presheaf map cube N --> cube k) is a crude dimension count needing no base points -- and it was already in the repo one spelling away, as boxHom_dim_le.
- BPSet.cube_dim_eq (k = N for a BPSet map cube k --> cube N) is carried ENTIRELY BY THE BI-POINTING. Box.eq_id_of_endpoints: a Box morphism keeping both extremal vertices is free everywhere, since a fixed coordinate would have to read 0 at the initial vertex and 1 at the final one. Both endpoint conditions are needed: initVertexMap satisfies app_init alone and finalVertexMap satisfies app_final alone, each with 0 != N.

STRENGTHENING, free: even at k = N the hom-set is {identity} -- cube_hom_eq_id and instance cube_hom_subsingleton. The cubes are a DISCRETE full subcategory of BPSet, so cabling is extra structure not merely because dimensions differ but because BPSet sees nothing at all between cubes. This is the machine-checked form of the Aut(cube n) = {id} slogan, which previously had no proof in the tree.

The corollary is stated for an arbitrary functor so it applies to chFunctor and cFunctor without Foundations depending on Chains: not_functorial_cube_map (F : BPSet => D) (h : k != N) (Phi : F.obj (cube k) --> F.obj (cube N)) : no f with F.map f = Phi.

title: ConcPos out-labels are the parabolic of the bead dimensions
description:
STATEMENT. For X : FExec n with beads (d1,...,dk),
  { fperm X Y | Refines X Y }  =  S_{d1} x ... x S_{dk}   (as a subgroup of S_n)
an interval [1, Delta_{d1} ... Delta_{dk}] in the Garside order on simple braids.

Should be close to immediate in the fast model: Refines is defined blockwise, so both sides are literally 'independent shuffles within each bead'. Containment is by construction; equality then follows from the cardinality count.

VERIFIED at every object of □3, □4, ∂□4 and the 2-skeleton of □4: #distinct out-labels = prod di!.
Profiles: □3 gives [1,1,1]->1 [1,2]->2 [2,1]->2 [3]->6 (all 4 compositions);
          ∂□4 gives all 7 compositions of 4 with parts <= 3, topping out at 6 rather than 24.

WHY IT MATTERS. The parabolic determines the composition uniquely ([1,2] and [2,1] both have 2
labels but different subgroups), so ConcPos recovers the bead composition of every execution, hence
which faces of □n are present. Corollary: labels = [1,Delta] iff w0 is a label iff the top cell is
present — ConcPos detects the top cell via the Garside element. This is the sharp contrast with
Conc, whose IMAGE is P3 for □3, ∂□3 and ∂□3-minus-a-face alike.

Proved in Testing/Parabolic.lean, sorry-free, axioms [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]:

  FExec.outLabels_eq_parabolic (X : FExec n) :
    {σ | ∃ Y, X.Refines Y ∧ fperm X Y = σ} = (parabolic n X.dims : Set (Equiv.Perm (Fin n)))
  FExec.dims_eq_of_outLabels_eq — same out-labels ⟹ same bead dimensions
  FExec.outLabels_eq_top_iff (hn : 0 < n) — the full symmetric group is available iff X has one bead

parabolic is a genuine Subgroup, carrier {σ | ∀ i, blockIdx ds (σ i) = blockIdx ds i}. Set equality
proved; the cardinality fallback was not needed.

Two structural lemmas carry both inclusions: RefinesRel.getElem_flatten_mem_beadAt (a refinement
keeps every letter in the bead its position belongs to — induction on RefinesRel, no nodup) and
refinesRel_map_singleton (the converse). ⊆ is then Y.word[fperm X Y i] = X.letter i by defeq;
⊇ builds X.shuffled σ with fperm X (X.shuffled σ) = σ by group algebra alone.

CAVEAT: outLabels_eq_top_iff needs 0 < n. It is FALSE at n = 0 — the unique execution has no beads,
Perm (Fin 0) is trivial so the LHS holds but length = 0. All n ≥ 1 covered.

title: runProj has no computational characterization

title: Extracting implementations
description:
We cannot test our code on small examples very easily because native_decide is willing to tolerate all the `Set` and noncomputables we have. On the other hand, all the noncomputables are spurious, arising from various generalized constructions (like pushouts) that are actually quite computable in our setting. The goals of this epic are to 
1. Testing hypothesis against real examples
2. Extract implementations for integrating it into, say, a haskell library

Failure modes are 
1. duplicating implementations
2. losing generality of the theorems

I don't care about performance. If the extracted thing is slow that's fine. I also do not care about legibility. As long as we are extracting "exactly" what we are proving stuff about, it does not need to be nice.

title: xhj.6 general-n: forced axiom decision (Pₙ has no presentation; abstract Salvetti iso insufficient)
description:
Deciding how to close features 2+3 (injectivity + surjectivity) of xhj.6 for general n. Feature 1 (purity) is DONE on the real functor (cube_braidGrpd_pure, CubeChains/Braid/CubeIso.lean). The remaining iso ConcBraid(□n) x ≅ Pₙ = ker(permHom n) forces a decision, per subagent findings:

1. Pₙ HAS NO PRESENTATION anywhere (mathlib or repo) — it is only defined as ker(permHom n). Constructing the inverse map Pₙ → ConcBraid is BLOCKED without first formalizing the Artin pure-braid presentation (generators A_ij) AND proving it equals the kernel — a Reidemeister–Schreier theorem, a major undertaking.

2. AN ABSTRACT SALVETTI ISO AXIOM IS PROVABLY INSUFFICIENT. Assuming only 'ConcBraid(□n) x ≃* Pₙ' abstractly does NOT make the SPECIFIC map Φ = mapVertexGroup(braidGrpd) bijective (an abstract iso between two groups says nothing about a given homomorphism between them). Therefore any general-n axiom MUST NAME braidGrpd — e.g. 'Function.Bijective Φ', or a section s : Pₙ → ConcBraid with Φ∘s = id plus surjectivity on a generating family. This mirrors the Matsumoto-naming pattern already used in Braid/Artin.lean. THIS IS THE FORCED DECISION the parent bead anticipated.

3. SURJECTIVITY IS THE LINCHPIN. Given surjectivity of Φ onto Pₙ plus Pₙ Hopfian (finitely generated + residually finite ⟹ Hopfian; true, but not in mathlib), a surjective endomorphism of Pₙ is injective, so INJECTIVITY FOLLOWS. The converse (inj ⟹ surj) does NOT hold. Prioritize surjectivity.

4. MISSING PREREQUISITE: IsConnected(ConcGrpd(□n)) is needed and absent (Testing/ConcSpace has only native_decide b0=1 evidence). Sal(braidCOM n) has no initial/terminal/weakly-terminal object, so the xhj.11 μ-generator trick does not transfer — needs a general spanning tree + IsConnected.

RECOMMENDATION: (a) land n=2 unconditionally first (P₂=ℤ, ConcCat(□²)=K22 4-cycle, Φ via winding/writhe abelianization — no axiom needed); (b) for general n, prove surjectivity as far as possible, build IsConnected(ConcGrpd(□n)); (c) then adopt an axiom that NAMES braidGrpd (bijectivity or a named section), not an abstract Salvetti iso. DECIDE which of these before writing more general-n code.
notes: RESOLVED (2026-07-16). Axiom decided: salvettiConstruction_faithful (Braid/SalvettiConstruction.lean). It NAMES the actual map (the computable Salvetti braid grading salvettiGrading: Sal(braidCOM n) => SingleObj(Braid n), map = ofPerm(crossPerm), crossPerm read directly off sign-vector topes), satisfying the xhj.6.1 requirement (no abstract iso). It states FAITHFULNESS = injectivity DIRECTLY, so combined with green surjectivity gives bijectivity with NO Hopfian and NO Pn presentation needed (avoids the two blockers in this bead). Connection to braidGrpd/concBraidHom is the AGREEMENT lemma (crossPerm = evPerm' o braidSalEquiv), tracked in xhj.6.
close_reason: Forced axiom decision made: salvettiConstruction_faithful names the actual computable Salvetti map and gives injectivity directly (no Hopfian, no Pn presentation).

title: ZP: pi_1(N(Ch Z)) = B_n for Z terminal — SKELETON + why it is NOT easy
description:
*** READ THIS BEFORE ATTEMPTING. THIS WAS TRIED AND ABANDONED. ***

CubeChains/FinalPrecubical/ was EXACTLY this theorem. Quarantined (ARCHITECTURE.md:36) and then deleted
('salvage old code', 24b76fc). Its STATUS.md (git show 88f2ce0) records what HAD landed green:
  * Ch(box^m) equiv OSPcat m           (ordered-partition poset)
  * Sal0Br n equiv Composition n x Perm (CompositionSalvetti, 672e4d3)
  * HomAnalysis (PARTIAL): blockMap(+monotone), blockMap_spec, fibreShape  (d8cba4e)
and it STALLED on the 'R2 crux' = the object-level Segal decomposition of a wedge map, with an explicit
note that the net size win was 'modest, not dramatic'. Salvage from git before rebuilding.

MY SKELETON (derived independently this session; DIFFERENT attack, and better-positioned now):
Let Z = terminal BPSet. r = [1,1,...,1], c = [n].
 1. Ch(Z) = THE WEDGE CATEGORY. Z terminal => the classifying map is unique and the triangle
    (phi >> b.map = a.map) is AUTOMATIC. So Hom_Ch(Z)(A,B) = ALL bipointed wedge maps <A -> <B.
    (Contrast box^n, where b.map is an iso so phi is FORCED — that is why Ch(box^n) has a terminal
    object and Ch(Z) does not.)
 2. Hom(r,c) = S_n; r weakly initial, c weakly terminal.
 3. Aut(mk r) = < mu_pi : pi in S_n >, mu_pi := g_pi g_1^-1.  EASY: for any e : A -> B pick f : B -> c
    and insert f f^-1, giving gamma_e = mu_pi mu_rho^-1. No topology, no nerve.
 4. chBraid(mu_pi) = ofPerm(pi^{+-1})  =>  chBraid : Aut(mk r) ->> B_n is SURJECTIVE. EASY.
 5. INJECTIVITY = THE THEOREM. Need Psi : B_n -> Aut(mk r), [pi] |-> mu_pi, well-defined, i.e. the germ
    relation mu_sigma mu_tau = mu_{tau sigma} for LENGTH-ADDITIVE pairs. Hand-verified at n=3: these DO
    fall out of the factorization relations g_{h>>f} = h^ >> f^, and they are exactly the PARABOLIC
    decompositions sigma = w.u (w a minimal coset rep, u in the Young subgroup S_X) — which are
    length-additive. Needs: (a) the parabolic relations GENERATE the germ presentation; (b) upstream,
    the WEDGE-MAP CLASSIFICATION (Hom(<A,<B) determined by blockIdx + blockFace, every compatible pair
    realized) — which IS HomAnalysis, i.e. exactly where the old effort stalled.

WHY BETTER-POSITIONED NOW: Braid/Germ.lean presents B_n BY THE GARSIDE GERM, so step 5's target is
literally 'check the germ relations in Aut(mk r)' — a PresentedGroup.toGroup — not a Salvetti/Segal
argument. And chBraid (Braid/ChGrading.lean) already exists.

TRACTABLE HALF (do this first if resumed): steps 1-4 => 'B_n is a quotient of pi_1 N(Ch Z)'. Bounded.

WHY IT MATTERS (the conceptual payoff, already established this session):
  box^n : H = pi_1 N(Ch) = 1 (terminal chain => codiscrete);  G = pi_1 ConcGrpd = P_n
  Z     : H = B_n (!);                                        G strictly BIGGER (F_2 at n=2)
So the two extremes are OPPOSITE. For box^n the chain category sees NOTHING and the lines carry
everything. For Z the chain category already sees the FULL braid group and adding lines OVERSHOOTS.
Reason: Z's events are UNLABELED (one cell per dimension), so refining a square has TWO parallel arrows
— and that IS the braid generator. box^n's cubes are rigid/labelled, so those parallel arrows split into
distinct objects and the category collapses. Matches 1 -> P_n -> B_n -> S_n -> 1: box^n has global event
naming (monodromy trivial, get P_n); Z has none (monodromy all of S_n, get B_n).

n=2 CHECK (hand-done): Ch(Z)_2 = 2 objects, 2 PARALLEL arrows => circle => pi_1 = Z = B_2. And
ConcCat(Z)_2 = 3 objects, 4 morphisms => b1 = 2 => G = F_2. So q : G -> H is a SPLIT SURJECTION but NOT
an iso, and Phi : F_2 ->> Z is not either. The generator of ker q maps to sigma_1^2, the full twist —
exactly as Cubical-xhj.10 predicts.
close_reason: Closed

title: Linking-number characters ℓ_ij — the pure-braid invariant writhe throws away
description:
writhe is the abelianization of B_n: ONE integer. P_n abelianizes to Z^(n(n-1)/2), the pairwise LINKING NUMBERS l_ij = how many times event i winds around event j along a loop of executions. writhe = sum of l_ij, so it sums away exactly the structure we want. This is the hole in BraidCharacters, and likely why salWind has no bead-size formula (Cubical-l3v): it is a projection of a richer object.

STRUCTURE (the thing to get right): l is NOT a homomorphism on B_n -- the crossing pairs get relabelled by the permutation. It is a 1-COCYCLE
    l : B_n -> Z^Pairs(n),   l(gh) = l(g) + perm(g) . l(h)
for the S_n action permuting the pairs. Restricted to P_n (action trivial) a crossed hom IS a hom -- and that hom is the abelianization of P_n. So l_ij is exactly the braid content invisible to permutations.

The germ presentation makes this cheap: one generator [sigma] per permutation, l([sigma]) := inversions(sigma) as an element of Z^Pairs (the repo already has 'inversions' in Braid/Germ.lean). The cocycle law on a length-additive product is Inv(st) = Inv(s) union s.Inv(t) -- which is exactly salCross_add, already the composition law of refinements.

DONE WHEN: l_ij defined, cocycle law proved, restriction to pure loops is a homomorphism, and writhe = sum l_ij.
notes:
LANDED (Salvetti/Braiding.lean, green, sorry-free):
  salCrossVec a b : E -> Z          -- WHICH walls separate a from b, not how many
  salCrossVec_add                    -- additive WALL BY WALL along a <= b <= c
  salWindVec : Sal L => SingleObj (Multiplicative (E -> Z))   -- the vector winding functor
  sumWalls, sumWalls_salWindVec_map  -- salWind IS its sum
The pointwise additivity was already hiding inside salCross_add's proof: 'tope_eq_of_cross' says a wall
crossed by a<=b is not crossed again by b<=c. So the linking numbers were one un-summing away. For the
braid arrangement a WALL IS A PAIR OF EVENTS, so salWindVec is literally l_ij, and writhe = sum l_ij.

*** THE EXPERIMENT CANNOT RUN ON THE TRINITY, FOR A STRUCTURAL REASON. ***

BraidGround n = {(i,j) : i<j}, card = n(n-1)/2. MACHINE-CHECKED: card (BraidGround 2) = 1.

Every chain of the trinity runs a->d in exactly TWO events (three length-2 lines; three single 2-beads).
So n=2. At n=2 there is EXACTLY ONE WALL: the linking vector has one component and l == writhe,
identically. The refinement is VACUOUS there.

The trinity was never the right shape anyway: it IS the event-naming counterexample, so its permutation
monodromy is nontrivial BY CONSTRUCTION. It is the case where permutations already see everything.

TwoSquares has the right SHAPE (S_no_fold => global event naming => BraidPure => permutation trivial;
N(Ch S) ~= S^1 => pi_1(Fund S) = Z, a genuine global loop) but its chains are ALSO 2 events. And there is
a decisive argument it can never work: at n=2, P_2 = Z, and the single square's full twist (writhe +-2)
GENERATES ALL OF IT. So a global loop's pure braid is necessarily a multiple of the local twist.
Nothing beyond local, provably.

=> EVERY EXISTING WITNESS IN THE REPO IS BLIND TO THIS QUESTION BY CONSTRUCTION. All are built from
length-2 chains. The complexification CANNOT show content at n=2 -- not 'hasn't been shown', cannot.

SPEC FOR A WITNESS THAT COULD (now precise):
  (i)   chains with >= 3 events (>= 3 walls, so l is strictly finer than writhe);
  (ii)  global event naming / BraidPure (permutation identically trivial, braid pure) -- else
        permutations already win;
  (iii) a nontrivial loop in Fund: N(Ch K) not simply connected;
  (iv)  PAYOFF: the pure braid of that global loop is NOT in the subgroup generated by the local cubes'
        pure braids.
threeSquare / fourSquare have 4-event chains (two 2-beads in series -> 4 events -> 6 walls), so they clear
(i). (ii) and (iii) are UNCHECKED for them.

BLOCKER for any computation: Testing/Model.lean is DECOUPLED from the main library -- it models Ch K
combinatorially and knows nothing about Lines, chambers or braids. Computing l on a witness means building
the execution/chamber layer in the surrogate (chains -> chamber per bead -> refinement block data ->
crossing vectors -> cycle in the graph). Real work; worth doing ONCE, against a witness that can show
something.

title: beadCard's two sums are degree_add_length, once a List.sum/Fin-sum bridge exists
description:

What blocks the last step: dimSum and degree are List.sum of a map, while sum_beadCard is a Finset.sum over Fin c.dims.length. The bridge

  (l.map f).sum = sum over k : Fin l.length of f (l.get k)

does NOT exist in mathlib (grepped Algebra/BigOperators/Group/List/ and Algebra/BigOperators/Fin.lean) and does not exist in this repo. title: SlicePres A2b: coherence for sliceLocEquivNatIso
description:
Missing from A2 (Cubical-78j), which I closed prematurely. A2's bead asked for the localized slice comparison to be 'natural in c', and the agent delivered a natural isomorphism for each u : c' to c — sliceLocEquivNatIso, a bare Localization.liftNatIso. That is naturality in the per-arrow sense, but NOT the pseudo-functorial coherence: nothing says the family is the identity at id, or compatible with composition of u. A4's OverPseudoCoconeLoc needs exactly those, because a composite of three natural isos satisfies the pseudo-cocone coherences only if each factor does. Factors 2 and 3 of A4's comparison are fine — factor 3 is a strict equality so its coherence is functoriality of P, and factor 2 follows from hP being a functor equality plus overMapLoc_comp. Factor 1 has no coherence at all.

Wanted, in Machinery/Localization/SliceLocalize.lean beside sliceLocEquivNatIso: that it is the identity at 𝟙 (up to the canonical eqToIso of overMapLoc_id) and compatible with composition (up to the canonical eqToIso of overMapLoc_comp) — the same two shapes as OverPseudoCoconeLoc's iso_id and iso_comp, which is what will consume them.

Route: Localization.natTrans_ext reduces each to components after Q, where compUniqFunctor and overMapLocFac make everything computable. Judged provable but a fresh chunk of work rather than a corollary.

Note this is a gap in the statement, not in the proof: nothing already proved is wrong, and nothing about GlueRel is implicated. The overlap relations are sound (glue_sound_overlap) and sufficient (glueIncl_naturality), both proved.

Done when: sorry-free, lake build CubeChains green, debloat pass run.

title: IsLocal.tensor_id and id_tensor are one cobase-change statement
description:
`CubeChains/Chains/SegalCondition.lean` proves `IsLocal.tensor_id : IsLocal K w → IsLocal K (w ⊗ₘ 𝟙 Y)` and `IsLocal.id_tensor : IsLocal K w → IsLocal K (𝟙 X ⊗ₘ w)` as two 26-line mirror images. There is no symmetry to exploit — `(BPSet, ∨)` has no braiding, by design — and mathlib's Bousfield `isLocal` API has no counterpart.

Wanted: both as instances of one statement, that locality is stable under cobase change:

    IsLocal.of_isPushout {K} {A B P Q : BPSet} {w : A ⟶ B} {i : A ⟶ P} {j : B ⟶ Q} {w' : P ⟶ Q}
      (sq : IsPushout w.hom i.hom j.hom w'.hom) (h : IsLocal K w) : IsLocal K w'

(injectivity from `sq.hom_ext`, surjectivity from `sq.desc`/`sq.inr_desc` — about 12 lines, no
limit-preservation API needed), together with the two squares saying a whiskering is a cobase
change: `IsPushout w.hom (wedgeInl A Y) (wedgeInl B Y) (w ⊗ₘ 𝟙 Y).hom` and its mirror on
`wedgeInr`. Those follow from `Glue.isPushout` and `IsPushout.of_top`/`of_left` by pasting, using
`finalVertex_comp`/`initVertex_comp` and `tensorHom_inl`/`tensorHom_inr` to recognise the outer
rectangle.

Weighed and deferred once: the pushout route is roughly line-neutral (about 65 lines against 52).
It is wanted for the reason, not the line count — "locality is stable under cobase change" is the
textbook fact, and the square lemmas are reusable.
